en.name: Flag of a workers’ league bearing the sign
short_description:
This flag presumably belonged to a league of navvies, or labourers. It shows the tools used by workers employed in road construction, i.e. pickaxe and shovel.  
Starting from the last decades of the XIX century, trade unionism flourished in Italy. In the 1890s, in many towns different unions started to reunite in general unions at a town level, known as Camere del Lavoro (labour unions, modelled on the French Bourse du Travail). In 1906 the Confederazione Generale del Lavoro (CGdL), a national confederation of trade unions, was founded.
dates: Unknown (probably immediately after World War I)
partner: MIBACT | Central State Archives of Italy

en.name: Qasr al-Hallabat
description:
The site of Qasr al-Hallabat comprises a conglomerate of separate and widely spaced units. These include: a *qasr* (castle), a mosque, a huge reservoir and eight cisterns dug into the western slope. In the plain next to the reservoir is an irregularly shaped agricultural enclosure with an elaborate system of sluices and a cluster of poorly built houses, which extends to the northwest of the reservoir. To these units should be added the baths complex of Hammam al-Sarah (see Hammam al-Sarah) situated 2 km. to the east of the castle.  
The plan of the castle measures 44 m. in length with square corner towers, which project from the face of the enclosure wall. The entrance to the building is through a single doorway in the middle of the east wall. It opens into a passageway, leading to an open courtyard paved with flagstones. Originally a portico surrounded the courtyard because the walls facing this courtyard were plastered, which in some places preserved faint traces of paintings in dark brown. A series of oblong and nearly square rooms surrounds three sides of the central courtyard. The northwestern quadrant is occupied by an inner structure, which also consists of a central courtyard surrounded on all sides, except the south, by a number of rooms. This quadrant, is set apart from the rest of the building. It contained a small winepress and may have served as servants’ quarters. In each of the two courtyards there is a cistern.  
There were two inscriptions thought to be related to the architectural phases of the castle: one is in Latin, dated 212, and refers to the construction of a *Novum Castellum*; the other is in Greek and dated 529. Excavations and clearance work within the castle uncovered a total of another 142 Greek inscriptions, in addition to two Nabataean, one Safaitic and one modern Armenian inscription. The vast majority of the Greek inscriptions, engraved on regularly dressed basaltic stone, belong to an edict issued by the Byzantine emperor Anastasius (491-518) for the administrative and economic reorganisation of Provincia Arabia. It is likely that all the inscribed stones were brought from a nearby settlement, possibly Umm al-Jimal, and reused as building material during the Umayyad reconstruction of the castle. In the course of this reconstruction, the castle was provided with elaborate decorations in carved stucco, frescoes and coloured mosaics, and thus transformed from a fortified building into a palatial residence. This change was accompanied by a remarkable development of the site, which can be seen in the appearance of new monuments such as the extra-mural mosque, the agricultural enclosure with an elaborate irrigation system, and the bath complex of Hammam al-Sarah.

es.name: Qasr al-Hallabat
description:
El emplazamiento de Qasr al-Hallabat está formado por un conjunto de unidades independientes y ampliamente espaciadas, entre las que se cuentan: un *qasr* (castillo o alcázar), una mezquita, un depósito enorme y ocho cisternas excavadas en la ladera occidental. Sobre la llanura contigua al depósito se extendían hacia el noroeste un recinto agrícola de planta irregular equipado con un elaborado sistema de esclusas y un aglomerado de casas pobremente construidas. A esta serie variopinta de elementos habría que sumar las termas del Hammam al-Sarah, situado 2 km al este del castillo.  
La planta del castillo tiene 44 m de lado, con torres cuadradas de esquina que sobresalen por la cara exterior del muro de cerramiento. La **entrada** al edificio se efectúa a través de un único umbral situado en medio del muro oriental. Esta puerta da a un pasadizo que conduce hasta un patio abierto, pavimentado con losas. Originariamente, este patio estaba flanqueado por una galería porticada, como lo indican los leves restos de pintura que se vislumbran en algunas zonas donde se ha conservado el enlucido que recubría las paredes interiores. Una serie de estancias alargadas y casi cuadradas rodea tres lados de este patio central. El cuadrante noroeste está ocupado por una edificación interior que consiste, a su vez, en otro patio central rodeado por todos los lados, excepto por el sur, por una serie de habitaciones. Este cuadrante, separado del resto del edificio, albergaba una pequeña prensa de vino y pudo haber servido como residencia del servicio. En cada uno de los patios hay una cisterna.  
En este lugar se descubrieron dos inscripciones que se han querido relacionar con las fases arquitectónicas del castillo: una de ellas, con fecha del 212, está en latín y hace referencia a la construcción de un *Novum Castellum*; la otra está en griego y fechada en el año 529. Las excavaciones y las obras de desescombro llevadas a cabo en el castillo permitieron sacar a la luz un total de 142 inscripciones en griego, además de dos nabateas, una safaítica y una moderna inscripción en armenio. La mayoría de las inscripciones griegas, grabadas en sillares de basalto, hace referencia a un edicto emitido por el emperador bizantino Anastasio (491-518) con motivo de la reorganización administrativa y económica de la *Provincia Arabia*. Es muy probable que todos los sillares con inscripciones proviniesen de un asentamiento cercano, posiblemente Umm al-Yimal, y fueran reutilizados por los omeyas como material para la reconstrucción del castillo. En el transcurso de esta reconstrucción, se dotó al castillo de elaboradas decoraciones de estuco tallado, frescos y mosaicos de colores, transformándolo así de un recinto fortificado en una residencia palaciega. Junto con esta transformación, se produjo un notable crecimiento del conjunto, que se vio enriquecido con una nueva mezquita extramuros, el recinto agrícola con su sofisticado sistema de riego y las termas de Hammam al-Sarah.

fr.name: Qasr Al-Hallabat
description:
Le site de Qasr al-Hallabat rassemble des vestiges dispersés sur une très grande superficie, dont un *qasr*, une mosquée, un immense réservoir et huit citernes creusées dans la pente occidentale. Dans la plaine, près du réservoir, on a retrouvé un enclos agricole de forme irrégulière, avec un réseau d’irrigation et de vannes, et des vestiges de maisons très modestes groupées au nord-ouest du réservoir. À cet ensemble, il faut rattacher Hammam al-Sarah qui se trouve à 2 km à l’est du château.  
Le plan du château dessine un quadrilatère de 44 m de côté, flanqué de quatre tours d’angle carrées en saillie des murs d’enceinte. L’unique entrée, au milieu du mur est, donnait sur un passage couvert conduisant à une cour ouverte à dalles de pierre. D’après les traces ténues de peinture brun foncé retrouvées sur des fragments d’enduit, il semble qu’à l’origine les murs de la cour intérieure étaient plâtrés et peints, et certainement protégés par un portique. Sur trois côtés, la cour centrale ouvrait sur un alignement de pièces, rectangulaires ou presque carrées, sauf pour l’angle nord-ouest occupé par un bâtiment. Ce dernier comprenait une cour centrale entourée, sauf au sud, par des petites pièces. Cet espace ainsi séparé du reste pourrait avoir délimité le quartier réservé aux serviteurs. On y a trouvé un petit pressoir à vin. Les deux cours étaient dotées d’une citerne.  
On a retrouvé deux inscriptions qui semblent faire référence aux phases de construction du château: l’une, portant la date de 212, est en latin, et évoque la construction d’un *novum castellum*; l’autre, en grec, est datée de 529. Au cours des fouilles menées à l’intérieur du château, on a encore dégagé cent quarante-deux inscriptions grecques, deux nabatéennes, une safaïtique et une inscription en arménien moderne. La majorité des inscriptions grecques, gravées sur des pierres de taille de basalte, concernent un édit promulgué par l’empereur byzantin Anastase (491-518) sur la réorganisation administrative et économique de la *Provincia Arabia*. Il est probable que toutes ces pierres proviennent du site voisin d’Oum al-Jimal, et qu’elles ont été réemployées par les Omeyyades lorsqu’ils ont reconstruit le château. C’est au cours de cette reconstruction que le château recevra sa décoration raffinée de stucs, ses fresques et ses mosaïques multicolores qui transformeront la forteresse en un palais d’agrément. Cette transformation s’est accompagnée d’un développement remarquable du site: de nouveaux monuments sont créés, comme la mosquée extra-muros, l’enclos agricole avec son réseau d’irrigation élaboré et les bains de Hammam al-Sarah.

en.name: Mardhouf al-Qawasim
names: Coin used by the Qawasim rulers of the lower Gulf region in the AH 13th century / AD 19th century
short_description: This rare copper alloy coin, known as 'Madhrouf Al Qawasim and weighing around 6.5 grams in weight, was minted in the trading port of Lanja (Linga) on the Persian coast of the Gulf in 1247 H/ 1831 CE.  In the 12th/18th and early 13th/ early 19th century, Lanja belonged to the extensive territories on both sides of the Gulf held by the Al Qawasim, and coins like this were used throughout the regions ruled by the Qawasim family at the time, including their main centres in Sharjah, Ras al Khaimah, Kalba, Khor Fakkan and Diba.
holder: Sharjah Heritage Museum / Sharjah Museums Department

en.name: Esterházy Palace
description:
The main building of the palace complex is a complicated one, redesigned and modified in several periods. The middle part and the connecting sections of the side wings are three-storeys high; the horseshoe-shaped wings are one-storey high and, directed towards the main gate, rectangular side wings are connected to them. There is a belvedere over the middle bay. The main façade is decorated with pilasters, tympanum motifs, military trophies and a shield within which is the Esterházy coat of arms. There is a clock in the middle of the tympanum on the garden facade decorated with vases and *putti* and oval windows in the middle of the tympanums of the arched connecting wings. Balconies with wrought-iron balustrades on the second-floor level of the side wings, and a two-armed stairway with wrought-iron railings decorated with *putti* holding wrought-iron lamps, leads to a balcony from which the banqueting hall on the first floor is accessible. There are fountains in the courtyard and at the sides of the building.  
Among the most outstanding spaces are the *sala terrena* (with coloured stuccoes and wall paintings; the reconstruction of its 18th-century grotto with fountains whose porcelain animals spit water, began more recently); the summer dining area (with stuccoes); the ceremonial banqueting hall on the first floor of the middle bay with a ceiling painting, *Apollo's Triumph*, and allegorical statues of the Four Seasons in four corners of the hall.  
In the 18th century, the palace was famous for its exquisite furnishings and valuable artefacts, for example the *panneaux*, silk tapestries (e.g. those with the Esterházy design), *boiserie* with *panneaux* and wall-paintings in some rooms; chandeliers, clocks, ceramics, books, carpets, furniture and paintings; *chinoiserie* (furniture, ceramics \[also Japanese\], blue-and-white wall paintings, wallpapers and Chinese-lacquer panels in three rooms).  
In the garden (the first design by Anton Zinner) orange trees from the princely orangerie were planted in large buckets to furnish the *parterre* and chamber-gardens on both sides of the palace. The garden and park complex were organised around three main avenues, a *broiderie parterre* (large *parterre*) decorated with fountains and sculptures, *boskes,* and a garden for wild animals (*Lustgarden*). But the most valuable artefact of all was Franz Joseph Haydn, who lived in Eszterháza for 30 years and composed music to entertain Prince Nikolaus, his patron, and presented his operas in the then famous “great theatre” on the palace's west side (no longer extant).

The Esterházy Palace complex in Fertőd-Eszterháza is an outstanding creation of 18th-century European and Hungarian palace architecture; a *maison de' plaisance* – “merry residence”, or *Lustschloss* in German – that was constantly reshaped, along with its garden, by its *Maecenas,* Nikolaus Esterházy, from the 1750s to the 1780s. In the period, it was the centre for Hungarian *chinoiserie*. The *opera* (great theatre) and the marionette theatre (small theatre) were exquisite parts of the complex. Franz Joseph Haydn was head of Prince Nikolaus's orchestra for 30 years and lived in the *Muzsikaház* (Music House) in the palace grounds.
artist: Architect: Anton Erhard Martinelli; roof design: Simon Mödlhammer; design for the 18th-century reconstruction attributed to: Nicolaus Jacoby; various stages of reconstruction: Girolamo le Bon, Melchior Hefele, Nicolaus Jacoby, Ferdinand Mödlhammer; initial garden design: Anton Zinner, (fountain): Franz Gruss; *opera* design (after fire): Michael Stöger painter/sculptor: Johann Friedrich Schrott; sculptor: Josef Ressler/Rössler; ironwork: Carl Franke; painters: Johann Ignatz Mildorfer, Wolfgang Köpp; textile designer: Philipp de Lasalle
history:
The settlement in Eszterháza, now part of Fertőd, was connected to Süttör in the 18th century, along with the building complex and the estate. At the time Süttör was a Nádasdy estate, which was confiscated from the family as a result of the Wesselényi Conspiracy, and given to Palatine Pál I Esterházy. After the death of Prince Pál his youngest son, József I, inherited the estate. In 1720, József commissioned Anton Erhard Martinelli to design a hunting lodge, which according to some scholars made use of an old Renaissance hunting lodge built on the Süttör part of the estate, and for which Simon Mödlhammer created the palace roof.  
This building was inherited by József I's youngest son, Miklós II (Prince Nikolaus II Esterházy) in 1721, and in the early 1750s, Nikolaus moved there with his wife. The design of the building complex, the garden and the forest around it, were documented in a contemporary oil painting that went missing during the Second World War, but a photographic reproduction of the painting is extant.  
Nikolaus probably began reconstruction of the palace complex and enlargement of the main building in 1762, maybe to the designs of Nicolaus Jacoby an Alsatian *ingenieur*. According to recent research, the first phase of reconstruction took place between 1762 and 1764, and the second phase between 1765 and 1768. The expansion plan of Eszterháza – known as a “directive” – can probably be dated to 1762, and recent research connects it to Girolamo le Bon or Melchior Hefele.  
An important milestone in the reconstruction of the palace was Queen Maria Theresia's visit in 1773:  for the occasion, the marionette theatre was completed, and the marionette opera, *Philemon and Baucis* by Joseph Haydn, was presented as a tribute to her. Two guard's buildings were built at this time and were complete by 1776. In the garden boskets, the temples to Diana, Venus, the Sun and Fortuna were built, and the inner ”large *parterre*” was redesigned, or rather reformed, in the garden. A third, greater period of construction took place between 1775 and 1778: the building of the Belvedere as it is seen today. The *Ermitage* (hermitage) was complete by 1775, when Archduke Ferdinand Habsburg and Maria Beatrice d'Este visited Eszterháza. The so-called Bagatelle, a Chinese pavilion, was finished by 1783. Reconstruction of the garden was almost continuous until the 1780s. The fountain, with an artificial waterfall on the east side of the large *parterre*, was built between 1783 and 1784, based on designs by Franz Gruss.  
To the east of the palace, the prince built a separate row of houses for the masters and other personnel. On this side, near to the marionette theatre, were the administrative buildings (“small palace”) and the orangerie. Actors, musicians and the pharmacist lived in the *Muzsikaház* (Music House), built to the west of the palace, where the three-roomed apartment of Joseph Haydn was. The stables and the inn for travellers who were not accommodated in the palace were also located on the west side.  
The first *opera* burnt down in 1779, but the prince erected an even more exquisite building within two years of its demise, designed by Michael Stöger.  
As to the identity of the architect responsible for reconstruction of the palace, a scholarly debate rages even today as to whether it was Melchior Hefele, Nicolaus Jacoby or Ferdinand Mödlhammer.  
The blue-and-white wall paintings in some of the rooms relate to the early period of construction (1750s and 60s). The ceiling paintings in the banqueting hall, chapel and the *sala terrena* were painted by Josef Ignatz Mildorfer; the sculptures made by, among others, Josef Ressler/Rössler and Johann Friedrich Schrott; the wrought-iron work by, among others, Carl Franke.  
The Golden Age of the palace ended in 1790 with the death of Prince Nikolaus II Esterházy. The family left Eszterháza to live in their residences in Kismarton (Eisenstadt) and Vienna.  
Then, at the end of the 19th century, Prince Nikolaus IV and his wife Countess Margit Cziráky, moved in. They renovated, modernised and decorated the palace with Rococo, Neo-Rococo and other period furniture, and extensively redesigned the garden.  The interior decoration was accomplished by Miksa (Maximilian) Schmidt and the F. O. Schmidt company.  
After the death of Prince Nikolaus V his eldest son, Pál V Esterházy, became the next and last master of the property. After the Second World War the Soviet army established a military hospital there and some of the furnishing was destroyed, the rest salvaged by soldiers and locals. Later the palace was nationalised.  
Reconstruction of the main building began under Jenő Rados in 1957, and was completed by 1959 for the anniversary of Haydn's death when a palace museum was opened with a Haydn Memorial Exhibition. The University of Sopron was the guardian of the palace until 1996. Currently it is managed by the National Trust of Monuments for Hungary. The Trust is repurchasing artefacts from the palace that have been dispersed, and renovating the complex in the framework of an EU-funded project.
keywords: Palace, *Opera*, *chinoiserie*, Nikolaus Esterházy, Franz Joseph Haydn, Anton Erhard Martinelli, Simon Mödlhammer, Melchior Hefele, Johann Friedrich Schrott, Johann Ferdinand Mödlhammer, Franz Gruss, Wolfgang Köpp, Johann Ignatz Mildorfer, Johann Josef Ressler (Rössler), Philipp de Lasalle, Paul Ungleich, Carl Franke, Anton Zinner, Eszterháza, Fertőd
partner: Eszterháza Centre for Culture, Research and Festivals

en.name: Hearth of Ateşbaz-ı Veli (*Makam-ı Ateşbaz-ı Veli*)
description:
Ateşbaz was a Mevlevi *dede* (elder) who lived during the lifetime of Mevlana. It is said that one day an elder was preparing a meal in the kitchen when he discovered that he had exhausted his supply of fuel. He informed Kazancı Dede of the situation. Upon receiving the reply, "If there is no wood, you should have put your foot," he did not hesitate, and placed his foot into the fire, cooking the food in its flame. This earned him the name Ateşbaz, or "playing with fire”. A sign reading *Ya Hazret-i Ateşbaz-ı Veli* (O His Holiness Ateşbaz-ı Veli) used to be hung over the hearth in Mevlevi kitchens.  
According to sources associated with the Mevlevi Order, Sultan Veled, the son of Mevlana, engaged in a period of asceticism lasting forty days. This involved seclusion and reduced food, sleep and speech. Once the forty days of asceticism had been completed, Ateşbaz would prepare a meal. The first mausoleum for a cook was constructed for Ateşbaz in Meram, Konya.

en.name: Three
short_description: These water pipes, or *araghil* (sing. *arghile*), is made of translucent glass painted with floral patterns in pale colours. The *araghil* have three main parts: first, you have a bowl for the coals sitting on top of a metal plate. Under this is the body of the *arghile*, which can come in a variety of shapes and sizes, and consists of a gasket and water jar. Connected to the main body is a pipe for smoking. The *arghile* originated in Persia and later became popular in 17th century Turkey, used by the Ottoman elite as a status symbol. The water pipe became hugely popular, and in 1841 even sparked a diplomatic crisis between France and the Ottoman Empire. However, although it remains popular in the modern Middle East, it was largely replaced by cigarettes in the 20th century. The *arghile* woks by vaporizing a flavoured tobacco called *shisha*, which is passed through water and then inhaled. Depending on their placement, the coals can either be used to boil the water and thus create water vapour, or to produce smoke by burning the tobacco. These *araghil* were used by Ottoman officials in 19th century Lebanon.
keywords: Glass; Water pipe; Smoking

en.name: Views with ruins
description:
These pictures decorated one of the halls in Palazzo Aldrovandi, later called the Palazzo Montanari. They were moved to the Collezioni Comunali d'Arte in 2001 after they were purchased by the Municipality of Bologna.  
The series was painted between 1724 and 1733 by Pietro Paltronieri called Mirandolese (architectures) and Vittorio Maria Bigari (figures). Both artists worked for Pompeo Aldrovandi (1668-1752), a famous Bolognese prelate who was ordained cardinal in 1734. He transformed the family house in Via Galliera into a sumptuous residence, inspired to the most famous French models.  
Il Mirandolese was a very celebrated landscape and ruins painter. He was so celebrated that he participated in a series of the *Allegorical Tombs*, commissioned by Ms. Mac Swiny and dedicated to the Duke of Richmond. This patronage involved other painters, both Bolognese and Venetians including Pittoni, Cimaroli, Canaletto, and the Riccis.  
In this painting he freely combines ruins of imposing classic architecture, fragments of gothic churches, allegorical tombs, and simple wooden houses whilst using complex scenic perspectives.  
In this pre-romantic atmosphere Vittorio Maria Bigari places his slender and elegant figures. They are painted with a swift brushwork, which allows them to appear to move gracefully and indifferently, as they are walking, talking, and sitting on the ruins.  
The collaboration between the two artists is exceptionally good, as the high quality of Bigari's work emphasises the elegant scene created by Mirandolese.  
This cycle of paintings is part of a movement in archaeology, perspective and landscape which was starting to develop. The trend continued in France and England and can be seen in the paintings of Hubert Robert and Jean Honorè Fragonard. In Italy, the etchings by Giovanni Battista Piranesi were also a continuation of this movement.

This series was painted between 1724 and 1733 by Pietro Paltronieri called Mirandolese (architecture) and Vittorio Maria Bigari (figures). It was originally hanging in Palazzo Aldrovandi Montanari.  
This cycle of paintings reflects the taste for archaeology, perspective and landscapes made popular in England and France by the paintings of Hubert Robert and Jean Honorè Fragonard and in Italy by the etchings of Giovanni Battista Piranesi.

it.name: Vedute con rovine
description:
Questi dipinti decoravano una delle sale di  Palazzo Aldrovandi, poi  Montanari (mon 29); furono trasferite alle  Collezioni Comunali d'Arte nel 2001, dopo l'acquisto da parte del Comune di Bologna.  
La serie fu dipinta tra il  1724  e il  1733 da Pietro Paltronieri detto il  Mirandolese (architetture) e Vittorio Maria Bigari (figure). Entrambi gli artisti lavorarono per Pompeo Aldrovandi (1668-1752), un celebre prelato bolognese che dal 1734, quando venne nominato cardinale, iniziò a trasformare la dimora della sua famiglia in via Galliera in una sontuosa residenza, ispirata ai più celebri modelli francesi.  
Il Mirandolese fu un famoso pittore di paesaggie rovine. La sua fama giunse così in alto che prese parte alla serie delle Tombe Allegoriche, commissionate da Owen Mac Swiny e dedicate al duca di Richmond. Questa commissione coinvolse altri pittori, sia bolognesi che veneziani come  Pittoni, Cimaroli, Canaletto e i Ricci.  
In questi dipinti egli combina liberamente rovine di imponenti architetture classiche, frammenti di chiese gotiche, tombe allegoriche, semplici casette di legno, utilizzando prospettive altamente scenografiche.  
In questa atmosfera quasi preromantica Vittorio Maria Bigari colloca le sue figure snelle ed eleganti. Dipinte con una pennellata rapida esse si muovono con grazia e indifferenza, camminano, parlano e siedono tra le rovine.  
La collaborazione tra I due artisti è eccezionalmente buona, al punto che l'alta qualità del lavoro di Bigari enfatizza le scene eleganti create dal Mirandolese.  
Questo ciclo di dipinti è parte di quel gusto oscillante tra archeologia, prospettiva e paesaggio che si stava sviluppando in questi anni e che avrebbe prodotto in Francia e Inghilterra la pittura di Hubert Robert e Jean Honorè Fragonard e in Italia le incisioni di Giovanni Battista Piranesi.

en.name: Base of globular waterpipe (hookah)
description: This globular hookah base has a short cylindrical neck that flares at the top.  Plant and floral decorations are distributed on the body and separated vertically by cords in relief. At its base, the neck is marke by two rings: the first has a triangular section and the latter - decorated with a chevron pattern - has a cylindrical section. The upper part of the neck is decorated by arches filled with ornamental plant motifs.
dates: Hegira 12th century / AD 18th century, first half

en.name: Kula Rug
description: Kula, Manisa Province was an important rug producing centre. During the 18th and 19th centuries they supplied the demand of international rug companies. Most Kula rugs, including this example are prayer rugs. The main component of prayer rug decoration is the *mihrab* and can be described as a stylized arch surrounding the prayer area. This is a double *mihrab* Kula rug with band stairs on both sides. In double *mihrab* rugs there are two *mihrab*s, one at the bottom of the image and the other at the top. This Kula rug with a double *mihrab* has eight borders, four wide bands and four narrow bands. It is decorated with an image of flowers in a vase.
keywords: West Anatolia; Manisa; kula Rug

ar.name: سجادة
description:
سجادة من الصوف الكاشان الفارسي تعرض صورة لملك أو نبيل جالس على كرسي مزين بالتيجان. هذا الشخص يشرب بيده الأخرى إبريقًا من النحاس.  
  
من شأن السجاد المصور في قاجار إيران أن يصور أفراد العائلة المالكة والمشاهير في سيناريوهات مختلفة.  
  
مشهد صيد يميز سجادة قاجاري ، مع مجموعة متنوعة من الحيوانات والنباتات. يمثل طائر الفينيق فوق الرجل النبيل الخلود ، كمخلوق شائع في الأساطير بيريسان. كلاب الصيد ترمز إلى الشرف والمجد ، والغزال يرمز إلى البراءة.  
  
تشير الصور المهمة للمياه إلى النقاء ومصدر الحياة ، حيث تجسد السمكة حبًا لا يموت. خلال هذه الفترة ، تدل شجرة القرداء على الفخر والفخر الفارسيين.

en.name: Qajar Carpet -Hunting Scene
description: The pictorial carpets of Qajar Iran illustrate royals and famous people in various scenarios. This Persian Kashan wool rug displays a hunting scene with a portrait of a king or a nobleman sitting on a chair embellished with crowns, drinking and holding a copper ewer in his other hand, and a wide variety of animals and plants. The phoenix above the nobleman, a popular creature in Persian mythology, represents immortality. Hunting dogs symbolize honour and glory, while the gazelle symbolizes innocence. The imagery of water is significant, denoting purity and the source of life, and in which the fish embody undying love. The cypress tree signifies Persian perseverance and pride.
holder: Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani

en.name: Single-volume Qur’an
description: The text is written in a fine *andalusi* hand with 25 lines to the page. *Sura* headings are in single-line gold *kufic*, except for the headings to *sura*s I and II, which are written in a different *kufic* in white in illuminated panels. The two-page colophon (folios 121b–122a), which is written in gold *naskhi*, states that the manuscript is the work of a hitherto unknown scribe, Yusuf ibn ‘Abdallah ibn ‘Abd al-Wahid ibn Yusuf ibn Khaldun, and that it was copied for Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Biyatush al-Makhzumi. To judge from his great grandfather’s Christian name Beatus, the patron was of Spanish stock.

en.name: Parish Church of Sümeg
names: Church of the Ascension of Christ
description: The church is a prototype of a simple, rural, Baroque single-tower church. On entering the church are the organ-loft and the entrance hall; the building then continues in three sections topped by a sail vault and ends with the sanctuary. The façade is furnished with statues of the Virgin Mary, and two Hungarian Holy kings, St. Stephen and St. Ladislaus. In the entrance hall are statues of the precursors of Christ, the prophets and sibyls. On the pillars are representations of David as an ancestor of the Family of Christ in front of King Saul and, later, as King David. In the Chapel of the Holy Sepulchre, accessible from the entrance hall, are frescoes depicting the *Limbo of the Fathers* (the *Bosom of Abraham*) and *Sacrifice of Abraham*. In the first section of the nave the ceiling frescoes depict *God Dispatches the Archangel Gabriel* and *Moses Receives the Tablets of the Law*. Underneath these scenes are the *Birth of Christ* and the *Annunciation* on the right, and the *Naming of Jesus* on the left. On the ceiling of the second section are the *Star of Bethlehem* and the *Road to Calvary*. To the right of this is the *Adoration of the Magi* and, to the left, the *Hill of Calvary*. The decoration on the ceiling of the third section portrays *Angels*, *Christ with the Apostles*, and the *Arrival of the Holy Spirit*. Underneath the image of *Christ* a depiction of the *Resurrection* can be seen; and beneath the *Arrival of the Holy Spirit* are the *Pentecost* and *St. Peter*. The main wall of the sanctuary is decorated with the *Transfiguration*, where the damned are seen on the right and the saved on the left. The ceiling frescoes portray the *Holy Trinity*, *St. Martin*, *St. Francis de Sales*, and the *Four Church Fathers* (St. George, St. Jerome, St. Ambrose and St. Augustine). *St. Michael* and the *Twenty-Four Elders of the Apocalypse* are pictured weighing souls in the fresco in the organ-loft, where there is also a portrait of Bishop Márton Padányi Bíró. There are two self-portraits of Maulbertsch in the church: one in the organ-loft among a crowd of nobles and another in the *Birth of Christ* where he is seen among the shepherds.

The significance of the Church of the Ascension of Christ in Sümeg lies in its magnificent fresco cycle, painted by Franz Anton Maulbertsch in 1757. Born in Langenargen, Maulbertsch was a disciple of Peter van Roy and Paul Troger in Vienna. Following the Baroque tradition, the fresco cycle carries a complex theological message probably composed by the learned and rigid Márton Padányi Bíró Bishop of Veszprém, who also built for himself a mansion in the town.
artist: Project coordinator and Master mason: Joseph Tiethart; painter: Franz Anton Maulbertsch (1724–1796)
history: Bishop Márton Padányi Bíró inherited a diocese that was in financial ruin. A talented administrator, he managed to restore the economy of the Veszprém diocese and ordered the construction of several parish churches. The church in Sümeg was of course one of these, and its special significance was probably due to the fact that the bishop also built a mansion for himself in the town, which became his favourite residence. The church was built between 1756 and 1757 presumably under the auspices of Joseph Tiethart a master mason from Veszprém, who conducted the construction of the mansion as well. The bishop entrusted Franz Anton Maulbertsch with painting the fresco cycle that delivered a complex theological message. This proved to be Maultbertsch's most outstanding work in Hungary.

ar.name: مخطوطة لفيفة
description:
تضمّ هذه المخطوطة القرآن بأكمله، مأطر بزخارف أوراق الشجر على شكل دمعة، تحتوي هذه المخطوطه الطويلة والمُمتده بطول خمس واجهات للعرض سور القرآن كاملاً وعددها 114 سورة كتبت بشعر حصان بخط يصعب قراءته بالعين المجردة.  
نظرا لحجمه ووزنه، يفضل المسافرون المسلمون والحُجّاج على وجه الخصوص هذا النوع من المخطوطات القرآنية لسهولة حمله. مع ذلك يُعتقد أن هذا النوع من المخطوطات كالمعروضه هنا إنها كانت تُستخدم كتميمة للحماية خلال الرحلات الطويلة أكثر منه للقراءة .  
  
أما اليوم، فتتيح التطبيقات على الهواتف الذكية إمكانية الوصول للقرآن الكريم بنقرة واحدة، فيما تُوفّر العديد من الفنادق حول العالم كتبا مُقدسة لنزلائها.

en.name: Traveller's Qur’an Scroll
description:
This parchment encapsulates the entire Qur’an. Tear-shaped leaf-patterns frame the holy book, which stretches across five showcases. The 114 chapters are written with horsehair with scripts illegible to the naked eye.  
  
Due to its shape and weight, Muslim travellers, in particular pilgrims, would carry this type of Qur’an, ensuring lighter luggage than traditional books. However, it is believed that Qur’an scrolls like this sample would function as a talisman or good-luck charm on long journeys rather than a book for reading.  
  
Today, smartphone applications make holy books accessible at your fingertips, while many global hotels provide religious texts for their guests.
holder: Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani
keywords: Quran; Manuscripts; Kashmir
partner: Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani Museum (FBQ Museums)

en.name: Parts of the St. Mary and St. Ladislaus altarpieces from Zagreb Cathedral
names: St. Mary and St. Ladislaus altarpieces
description:
The museum's altarpiece composition comprises parts of two altarpieces, that of St. Mary and St. Ladislaus. It has a central niche from the altarpiece of St. Mary – decorated with acanthus leaves, putti and bunches of fruit – within which the statue of Mary with the Child Jesus in her arms is standing on a half-moon entwined by a serpent. In front of the niche stand the statues of St. Ladislaus, the King, and St. Emeric, the Duke, which belonged to the altarpiece of Ladislaus.      
The composition, flanked by carved consoles attached to the wall, has the same ornamental decoration as seen in the central niche of the altarpiece of St. Mary; the consoles used to support painted altarpiece wings. Above them are the statues of the four evangelists, which were originally in the niches of the predella panel of the altarpiece of St. Ladislaus.  
In a contract of 1686, the sculptor from Ljubljana, Ivan Komersteiner, agreed to make the altarpiece of St. Mary for the apse of the north aisle of Zagreb Cathedral. In another contract of 1688, he agreed to make its pair, the altarpiece of St. Ladislaus, for the apse on the south aisle. Komersteiner was already a citizen of Zagreb with a workshop in Zagreb's Kaptol.    
The two altarpieces were identical in design: winged altarpieces with painted panels showing scenes from the Life of Mary on the altarpiece dedicated to her, with statues distributed on two levels and in the attic. Painted panels depicting scenes from the Life of St. Ladislaus decorated the altarpiece dedicated to him, with appropriate statues. While the wings from the altarpiece of St. Mary were destroyed those from the altarpiece of St. Ladislaus are kept in Zagreb City Museum.     
St. Ladislaus, the King of Hungary, was responsible for the foundation of the Zagreb Diocese.  
Komersteiner was responsible for the statues and woodcarving. Ivan Eisenhort and Bernardo Bobić collaborated on the painting and gilding of the altarpieces, while Matijaž Erlman began the work on the architecture for the altarpiece of St. Mary.  
The arrival of the sculptor, Komersteiner, to Zagreb marked the final entrance of the Baroque in the sculpture of continental Croatia. He brought with him as a novelty the ornamental decorative motif of Baroque acanthus, so-called Italian leaves, and his statues anticipate a new style expressed in the mobility of the slender figures of saints in characteristic counterpoise, freeing them from dependence on altarpiece niches.      
Komersteine's expression in his work has no direct analogies either in Croatia or in neighbouring territories, but the indirect influence of Italian art in his work is undeniable.  
During renovations in 1882, both altarpieces were removed from Zagreb Cathedral.

A “composite” altarpiece composition comprising parts from the Altarpieces of St. Mary and St. Ladislaus originally designed for the apses of the north and south aisles of Zagreb Cathedral.  
During renovation of the cathedral in 1882, both altarpieces were removed and partially destroyed in the process. They were made by Ivan Komersteiner, a sculptor who worked first in Ljubljana and then in Zagreb. His arrival in Zagreb marked the final entrance of the Baroque to continental Croatia.

en.name: Castle
description:
The stronghold of Aci, of Byzantine origin, was built at the beginning of the 9th century as a fortified outpost for control of the coastline. The first certain date referring to it is that of 902, the year in which Aci is recorded by the Arab chronicler Ibn al-‘Atir, but the original Byzantine site is not identifiable with any certainty, and could, therefore, not coincide with the stronghold of the castle. Shortly afterwards it was conquered by the Muslims, who flattened the fortifications, throwing the stones of the walls into the sea.  
They ruled for about two centuries, until the stronghold was conquered by the troops of the Great Count Ruggero d’Altavilla, who handed the castle and its appurtenances to Angerio, the Bishop of Catania.  
Subject to numerous assaults in the course of the centuries and today used for museum activities, there still remain parts of the original structure of the castle. The best preserved is the principal tower, a rectangular structure, built of lava stone.

es.name: Castillo sobre el peñón
description:
La fortificación de Aci, de origen bizantino, fue edificada a principios del siglo IX como puesto avanzado para el control de la costa. La primera fecha segura relacionada con ella es la de 902, año en que el cronista árabe Ibn al-‘Atir la cita, pero no es segura su identificación con el sitio bizantino, que podría, pues, no coincidir con la peña del Castillo. Poco después sería conquistada por los musulmanes, que demolieron las fortificaciones y arrojaron al mar las piedras de las murallas. Fueron sus dueños durante cerca de dos siglos, hasta que la plaza fuerte fue expugnada en 1092 por las tropas del gran conde Ruggero de Altavilla, que concedió el castillo y sus pertenencias a Angerio, obispo de Catania.  
Del Castillo, sometido a numerosos asedios en el curso de los siglos y hoy destinado a actividades museísticas, quedan algunos cuerpos de fábrica del conjunto original. El mejor conservado es la torre principal, de planta rectangular, construida en piedra de lava.

ar.name: طبق
description: طبق ذو شكل دائري"كوينكو"، أبعاده متوسطة وخط السطح متصدع قليلاً، مدهون باللون الكستنائي على خلفية بيضاء وبريق معدني (انعكاسات معدنية). ينتمي هذا الطبق إلى سلسلة "الباردالو" ذات الأسلوب الفارسي؛ ويتكون الموضوع المركزي لزخرفته من طائر مجرد محاط بزخارف نباتية. ينحشر الطائر في مكان تحدده خطوط ثلاثية متساوية الأبعاد عن المركز، تتناوب مع شرائط من التشبيكات. أما حافة الصحن فمستديرة ويبرزها شريط عريض مستمر يحيط بها ويستطيل نحو الخلف. الوجه الخلفي من الطبق خالي من الزخرفة، لكنه يقدم عليه تدفقات متأتية من تطاير الأكاسيد المعدنية خلال عملية الشيّ في الفرن. ويمكن أن نميز فيه ثلاث"ثآليل" تبتعد عن بعضها البعض بشكل متساوٍ، وهي آثار حامل قديم ثلاثي الأرجل. تشكل أواني المائدة من هذا الصنف تقليداً لقطع من المعدن، لكن يمكن اعتبارها تحفا فاخرة.

ينتمي "كوينكو" مانيسيس هذا المدهون باللون الكستنائي فوق خلفية بيضاء ذات بريق معدني إلى سلسلة "الباردالو" ذات الأسلوب الفارسي. يتكون الموضوع المركزي من عصفور مبسط محاط بزخرفة نباتية؛ وقد كان هذا الطبق يقلد الأواني المنزلية المصنوعة من المعدن ويستعمل مكانها.

en.name: Earthenware dish.
description: Medium-sized circular earthenware dish, with the surface line slightly broken. It is decorated in chestnut colour on a white background with metallic lustre. It is one of the Persian-style *pardalot* series, whose central theme is a stylised bird surrounded by plant decoration. The bird is contained within a central area bounded by triple concentric lines, alternating with a band of interlacing. Its rim is rounded, accentuated by a wide continuous band, crossing over to the back of the dish. This is not decorated, but has drips resulting from the volatilisation of metal oxides during firing. Three equidistant spurs are still visible resulting from the mark left by the trivets. This dish is designed to resemble and substitute for tableware which was previously made of metal; it is nevertheless also considered a luxury object.

This ‘cuenco’ dish from Manises, decorated in brown on a white lustre background, is part of the Persian-style *pardalot* series. The central motif is a stylised bird surrounded by plant decoration. This plate imitates, and was used instead of, metal tableware.

es.name: Plato.
description: Plato circular de dimensiones medias, con superficie de línea ligeramente quebrada. Está decorado en castaño sobre fondo blanco, en reflejo metálico. Se encuadra en la serie *pardalots*, de estilo persa, cuyo tema central es un pájaro estilizado y rodeado de decoración vegetal. El ave se inserta en reserva limitada por líneas concéntricas triples, alternadas con una franja de entrelazo. Tiene el borde redondeado, acentuado por una larga franja continua que llega hasta la parte posterior del plato, que por lo demás no está decorada, aunque se observan escurrimientos provenientes de la volatilización de los óxidos metálicos durante la cocción. Aún son visibles tres verrugas equidistantes resultantes de la marca de las trébedes. Este plato imita y sustituye, como loza de mesa, a las piezas de metal, aunque también se consideraba un objeto de lujo.

Plato procedente de Manises (Valencia) con decoración en castaño sobre fondo blanco, reflejo metálico. Se encuadra en la serie *pardalots*, de estilo persa. El tema central es un pájaro estilizado y rodeado de motivos vegetales. Este plato imita y sustituye, como loza de mesa, a las piezas de metal.
keywords: Reflejo metálico; pardalot; estilo persa.
materials: Barro torneado y vidriado (mayólica con reflejo metálico).
tags: Barro torneado y vidriado (mayólica con reflejo metálico).

fr.name: Plat “cuenco”.
description: Plat de forme circulaire, “cuenco”, de dimensions moyennes, la ligne de surface étant légèrement brisée. Peint en châtain sur fond blanc à reflets métalliques. Appartient à la série *pardalot,* de style persan, dont le thème central est composé d'un oiseau stylisé, entouré d'un décor végétaliste. L'oiseau s'insère dans une réserve limitée par des lignes concentriques triples, alternant avec une bande d'entrelacs. Son bord est arrondi, accentué par une large bande continue, se prolongeant vers l'arrière. Celui-ci n'est pas décoré mais présente des coulées provenant de la volatilisation des oxydes métalliques lors de la cuisson. On peut y distinguer trois “verrues” équidistantes, la marque d'un ancien trépied. Les vaisselles de table de ce genre sont des imitations de pièces de métal, mais peuvent être considérées comme des objets de luxe.

Ce “cuenco” de Manisès, peint en châtain sur fond blanc à reflets métalliques, appartient à la série des *pardalot*, de style persan. Le thème central est composé d'un oiseau stylisé, entouré d'un décor végétal. Ce plat était utilisé à la place de vaisselle en métal, qu'il imitait.
holder: Musée national de Machado de Castro.
keywords: plat “cuenco” ; mudéjar ; Manisès ; argile; modelée ; vernissé ; reflets métalliques ; pardalot ; style persan
materials: Argile modelée au tour et vernissée (faïence à reflets métalliques).
tags: Argile modelée au tour et vernissée (faïence à reflets métalliques).

pt.name: Prato “cuenco”
description: Prato de formato circular, *cuenco*, de médias dimensões, com a superfície de linha ligeiramente quebrada. É decorado a castanho sobre fundo branco e reflexo metálico. Enquadra-se na série *pardalot*, de estilo persa, cujo tema central é um pássaro, estilizado e rodeado por decoração vegetalista. A ave insere-se em reserva limitada por linhas concêntricas triplas, alternadas por faixa de entrelaçados. Tem o bordo arredondado, acentuado por larga faixa contínua, trespassando para o tardoz. Este não é decorado, mas possui escorrimentos provenientes da volatização dos óxidos metálicos durante a cozedura. São ainda visíveis três verrugas equidistantes resultantes da marca das trempes. Este prato imita e substitui, como louça de mesa, as peças de metal, sendo no entanto igualmente considerado um objecto de luxo.

Prato “cuenco” oriundo de Manises. Tem decoração a castanho sobre fundo branco e reflexo metálico e enquadra-se na série *pardalot*, de estilo persa. O tema central é um pássaro, estilizado e rodeado por decoração vegetalista. Este prato imita e substitui, como louça de mesa, as peças de metal.

ar.name: مخمل مقصب
description: ازدهرت التصاميم التصويرية في المنسوجات الصفوية في القرن العاشر الهجري/منتصف القرن السادس عشر الميلادي. وغالباً ما تشابهت هذه الأشكال مع رسوم الكتب من تلك الفترة. يتميز هذا المخمل بكبر حجم أشكاله، وهو أمر غير مألوف في مخمليات أخرى من القرن العاشر الهجري/السادس عشر الميلادي، وثراء ملمس سطحه. وقد أُضيفت في بعض المناطق حلقات غير مقطوعة من خيوط الحرير الملفوفة بالمعدن إلى كومة الحرير التقليدية، متباينةً مع خلفية الخيوط المعدنية البراقة.
keywords: مقصب؛ مخمل؛ صفوي؛ نسيج؛ إيران

en.name: Brocaded velvet
description: Figurative design flowered in Safavid textiles in the AH 10th century / AD mid-16th century. These figures often share the same features as book paintings from the period. This velvet is unique due to the large size of its figures, unknown on other velvets of the AH 10th century / AD 16th century, and the richness of surface textures. Uncut loops of metal-wrapped silk thread have been added in some areas to the traditional silk pile, contrasting with the glittering metal thread background.
keywords: Brocaded; Velvet; Safawid; Textile; Iran

en.name: Pendant
short_description: A thin silver triangular pendant and welded decoration with blue glass beads. Five chains dangle with Ottoman coins at the end. This kind of jewellery was part of the dowry the groom gave to the bride. Dowries consisted mostly of silver jewellery because only the rich could afford gold jewellery. The use of coins as pieces of jewellery, worn by brides in front of their relatives and friends, was an indirect statement of the financial status of the groom.
holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
keywords: triangle; silver; blue beads; Ottoman coins
partner: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery

en.name: *Madame X*
short_description: The basis of Turkish painting drawing influence from western tradition was laid when *Mühendishane-i Berr-i Hümayun* (the Naval Academy) opened in 1795. Halil Pasha was foremost among the painters with a military background who founded a western-style art tradition in Turkey. He worked with Jean Leon Gerome in his atelier in Paris. He provided a unique distinction to the analysis of impressionist light and colour, and was an example of artists dealing with impressionist technique. Because of his qualified knowledge about anatomy and his interest in depicting the human figure, Halil Pasha had a unique place in Turkish Art History.
keywords: Painting; Halil Pasha; orientalist Turkish painters

de.name: Kath. Pfarr- und Wallfahrtskirche „Mariä Schmerzen und St. Ulrich“
description:
Umgürtet von Gesimsen und umgeben von einer Doppelreihe großer Rundbogenfenster und vier Giebelrisaliten besitzt die Kirche im Westen ihre Hauptansichtsseite. In barocker Manier wölbt sich diese konkav von außen zur konvexen Mitte vor und wächst dabei über ein mittig aufgebogenes Kranzgesims und einen mehrfach geschweiften Ziergiebel in die Höhe, um in einem gedrungen wirkenden Zwiebelturm auszuklingen.  
Im lichtdurchfluteten vierjochigen Schiff der Wandpfeilerkirche mit Emporen bewirken schräg gespannte Gewölbefelder einen zentrierenden Effekt, so dass es mit dem von einer Flachkuppel überspannten, reich ausgestatteten Chorraum zu verschmelzen scheint. Ergänzend leiten die beiden Seitenaltäre den Blick auf den Hochaltar. Den farbenfroh-heiteren Raumeindruck erzeugen die virtuosen Stuckdekorationen im Rokoko-Stil zusammen mit den großflächigen Deckenfresken, die dem Doppelpatrozinium gemäß Kreuzverehrung und Marienkult im göttlichen Heilsplan verorten. Zunächst sind an den Emporenunterseiten an die Pilger gerichtete Szenen aus der Wallfahrtsgeschichte dargestellt, sodann an den Quertonnen die Passion Jesu und die Leiden Mariens ineinandergeschoben. Darüber schließt sich der Raum durch das ovale Deckenfresko, das sein Echo in den Gewölbemalereien des Chores findet.

Die großräumige Wallfahrtskirche des Prämonstratenserklosters Rot an der Rot in Maria Steinbach, erbaut ab 1749, um dem enormen Zustrom an Pilgern gerecht zu werden, gilt als ein Juwel des bayerischen Rokoko. Ihr kunstgeschichtlicher Ruhm begründet sich auf der überwältigend prachtvollen Innenausstattung, bestehend bildreich-beredten Fresken, virtuosen Stukkaturen sowie kapriziösen Altären.
artist: Ignatius Vetter (reg. 1739-1755), Benedikt Stadelhofer (reg. 1755-1760), Mauritius Moritz (reg. 1760-82), jeweils Äbte der Prämonstratenserabtei Rot an der Rot
history: Die Wallfahrt in Maria Steinbach ist der 1126 gegründeten Prämonstratenserabtei Rot an der Rot inkorporiert. Ab 1723 gilt die einstige Pfarrkirche infolge der Stiftung eines Kreuzpartikels durch Abt Hermann Vogler als Wallfahrtsheiligtum. Zu dessen Verehrung ließ man ein 100 Jahre älteres Kruzifix mitsamt den beiden Assistenzfiguren, einer Schmerzhaften Muttergottes und des Apostels Johannes, restaurieren und im Hochaltar aufrichten. Ein daraufhin anwachsender Zustrom an Pilgern, wohl aufgrund von Wunderheilungen durch die Marienskulptur, war Anlass, Steinbach 1734 zusätzlich zum Marienwallfahrtsort zu erheben. Um den vielen Pilgern gerecht zu werden, entschied man sich 1746 für einen Neubau der Kirche nach dem so genannten Vorarlberger Münster-Schema und erwählte den baukundigen hauseigenen Pater Benedikt Stadelhofer zum Architekten. Nach der Übertragung des marianischen Gnadenbildes 1754 wurde die Kirche 1755 konsekriert, jedoch vollendet erst 1770 mit der Weihe des Hochaltars.
keywords: Wallfahrtskirche; Deckenfresko; Stuck; Marienwallfahrt

en.name: Catholic Parish and Pilgrimage Church of the Exaltation of the Cross and Our Lady of Sorrows
description:
The church is not only girded by cornices but also surrounded by a double series of large round-arched windows and four projections, each of them crowned by a tympanum. In the west – and very typically in the Baroque style – the main facade balloons out in a dish-shape manner from the exterior to the pulvinate middle part. Here it then rises, over a diadem-like curved cornice and a multi-scrolled ornamental gable, up into a squat looking turret with an onion-shaped roof.  
A centralised effect within the light-flooded galleries and four-bay aisle of the wall-pillar church is created through diagonally bent vaults, which allow the whole aisle to blend seamlessly with the richly decorated choir and its flat cupola vault. In addition to this effect, the two side altars also lead the viewer’s eye towards the high altar. The colorful and bright spatial impression is created through virtuoso stucco decoration in the Rococo style. This, together with the large ceiling frescos place the adoration of both the Cross and the Virgin Mary within the heavenly plan for salvation in accordance with the double patronage of the church. But, at first, the undersides of the galleries depict scenes from pilgrimage history directed towards pilgrims; the upper lateral barrel-vaults then show the suffering of the Virgin Mary. Finally, above these, one can find the oval ceiling fresco which echoes the paintings in the vault of the choir.

From 1749, under the auspices of the Premonstratensian monastery Rot an der Rot, the spacious pilgrimage church in Maria Steinbach was rebuilt and enlarged in order to do justice to the enormous inflow of pilgrims. The church is deemed to be one of the jewels of Bavarian Rococo. Its art historical fame originates from its overwhelmingly rich interior with its eloquent frescos rich in images, virtuosic use of stucco and whimsically designed altars.
artist: Abbots of the Premonstratensian Abbey Rot an der Rot, Ignatius Vetter (gov. 1739–1755), Benedict Stadelhofer (gov. 1755–1760), Mauritius Moritz (gov. 1760–1782)

Design of architecture: Pater Benedikt Stadelhofer (1694–1760); master builder: Anton Lacher (1705–1777); stucco: Johann Georg Üblher (1703–1763), of the altar and ornamental niche: Franz Xaver Feichtmayr the Younger (1735–1803), Franz Xaver Schmuzer (1713–1775); frescos: Franz Georg Hermann the Younger (1692–1768)
history: The pilgrimage to Maria Steinbach is incorporated in the Premonstratensian abbey Rot an der Rot which was founded in 1126. From 1723 onwards the former parish church was considered a pilgrimage centre due to Abbot Hermann Vogler's donation of a particle of the cross. For the purposes of adoration, a 100-year-old crucifix was restored and erected upon the high altar along with two assistant sculptural figures, a *Mater Dolorosa* and the *Apostle St John*. The steadily growing flow of pilgrims, supposedly due to the miraculous healing powers attributed to the sculpture of the Virgin Mary, was the reason that, in 1734, Maria Steinbach was elevated to a special place of pilgrimage dedicated to the Virgin Mary. To meet the demands of such a steadily growing number of pilgrims it was decided to rebuild the church according to the so-called “Vorarlberger Münster” scheme (named after the regional school of Austrian master builders). The architecturally trained local Premonstratensian monk, Father Benedict Stadelhofer was chosen as architect in 1746. After the transferral of the miraculous image of the Virgin in 1754, the church was then consecrated in 1755 although consecration of the high altar and thus the ultimate finish of the building process took place later, in 1770.
keywords: Pilgrimage church; ceiling fresco; stucco
partner: University of Munich, Institute of Art History

cs.name: *Valtice, Lichtenštejnský zámek, průčelí*
description:
Návrh na fasádu představuje vedle sebe původní stav fasády (vpravo) a novou dekoraci podle návrhu císařského divadelního inženýra a dekoratéra Antonia Beduzziho. Pro Beduzziho dekoratérské myšlení je charakteristické, že vyšel ze stávajícího stavu a fasádu doplnil o planimetrické ozdoby na plochu fasády kladené postupně ve vrstvách na sebe. Důležitou roli pro něj přitom hrála především sochařská výzdoba a vojenská emblematika spojená s důstojnickou kariérou vládnoucího knížete.  
Kresba souvisí s důležitou etapou ve stavebních dějinách lichtenštejnského zámku Valtice. Rezidenční sídlo jednoho z nejvýznamnějších knížecích rodů  
v Habsburské podunajské monarchii bylo stavěno na hranicích Dolních Rakous a Moravy po celou první polovinu 17. století a ještě na jeho sklonku bylo znovu upravováno. Na jeho vzniku se podílela postupně řada významných stavitelů, pracujících ve Vídni (Giovanni Battista Carlone, Giovanni Giacomo Tencalla, Giovanni Tencalla, Giovanni Pietro Tencalla, Domenico Martinelli, Pietro Giulietti ad.). Teprve však s nástupem knížat Antona Floriána a Josefa Jana došlo k jeho závěrečné přestavbě, jejímž výsledkem se stala dnešní podoba zámku.  
Architektem první etapy byl v letech 1713–1722 Anton Josef Ospel. Vytvořil rozsáhlý urbanistický projekt rezidence spojující nově upravené starší části  
s novými hospodářskými a správními trakty. Ve druhé etapě nový kníže zastavil další budování prostorově rozlehlého sídla a soustředil se především na dekorativní výzdobu interiérů a fasád ústředního panského corps de logis. Nový architekt Beduzzi vytvořil pro knížete sérii vysoce kvalitních kreseb, které sloužily jako ukázkové modello pro závěrečné úpravy.

Rezidenční sídlo jednoho z nejvýznamnějších knížecích rodů v Habsburské monarchii bylo výrazně upravováno v 1. polovině 18. století. Jeho novým architektem se stal císařský divadelní inženýr a dekoratér Antonio Beduzzi. Ten vytvořil sérii kreseb, které sloužily jako ukázkové modello pro závěrečné úpravy. Návrh na fasádu představuje vedle sebe původní stav fasády a návrh nové dekorace.
keywords: Emblematika; dekorace; modello
materials: Kresba perem a tuší, lavírováno modře, papír adjustovaný na plátně
tags: Kresba perem a tuší, lavírováno modře, papír adjustovaný na plátně

en.name: *Valtice/Feldsberg, Liechtenstein Chateau, Frontage*
description:
The design presents the original state of the frontage (right) and its redecoration by Antonio Beduzzi, an imperial theatre engineer and designer. Beduzzi based his design on the existing state, supplementing the frontage area with layered planimetric ornamentation. A pivotal role was played by sculpted decoration and military emblems associated with the military career of the count.  
Detailed decorative drawings are part of an important phase in the history of the Valtice/Feldsberg, Liechtenstein Chateau. The chateau, residence of one of the most prominent court families in the Habsburg monarchy, Valtice, was constructed on the border of Lower Austria and Moravia in the first half of the 17th century, with finishing touches added towards the end of the century. Its construction was associated with a number of leading architects active in Vienna (Giovanni Battista Carlone, Giovanni Giacomo Tencalla, Giovanni Tencalla, Giovanni Pietro Tencalla, Domenico Martinelli, Pietro Giulietti and others). Yet the final phase of the construction, during which the building acquired its present appearance, only came about during the period of the counts Anton Florián and Josef Jan.  
Anton Josef Ospel, the architect of the first part of the final phase between 1713 and1722, produced a bold design merging the newly modified older sections with new outbuildings and administration tracts. In the following building phase, a new count put a halt to the further spread of the construction and concentrated on decoration of the interior and frontages of the main *corps de logis*, for which he hired Antonio Beduzzi. Beduzzi created a series of high quality drawings for the count that served as template *modellos* for the final building modifications.

The residence of a prominent Habsburg court family saw a major reconstruction in the 18th century under a new architect, the imperial theatre engineer and designer Antonio Beduzzi. He created a series of drawings that served as templates for the final building modifications.
keywords: Emblems; *modello*; engraving; palatial architecture; design; coat of arms
materials: Pen and Indian ink drawing with blue wash; paper adjusted on canvas
tags: Pen and Indian ink drawing with blue wash

ar.name: جامي، مولانا نور الدين عبدالرحمن، يوسف وزليخا (يوسف وزليخا)
description: أشهر صيغة ملحمية رومانسية لقصة يوسف وزليخا كتبها مولانا نور الدين عبد الرحمن المعروف بـجامي (توفي 898هـ / 1492م) ضمن عمله هفت أورنگ. ووفقًا للخاتمة (الكولوفون)، كُتبت هذه النسخة يخط النستعليق على يد الناسخ شرف الدين الشريف الخوارزمي سنة 982هـ / 1574م في يزد، إيران. ويرجَّح أن المخطوطة اقتُنِيت مع مجموعة أخرى من المخطوطات مقابل 20 دوقية ذهبية على يد بيتر لامبك في القسطنطينية عام 1677، ثم نُقلت إلى المكتبة الوطنية النمساوية. وتضم المخطوطة سبع لوحات تصويرية كاملة الصفحة، مستوحاة من أسلوبي مدرستي شيراز وقزوين في التصوير. غير أن مُذهِّبًا عثمانيًا أضاف زخارف هامشية فخمة في أواخر القرن السادس عشر أو أوائل القرن السابع عشر.
keywords: لوحة؛ صفوي؛ يوسف؛ زليخا
materials: حبر وألوان مائية معتمة وذهب على ورق. خط نستعليق خطّي يتألف من 15 سطرًا في الصفحة.
tags: حبر وألوان مائية معتمة وذهب على ورق. خط نستعليق خطّي يتألف من 15 سطرًا في الصفحة.

en.name: Jami, Maulana Nur ad-Din 'Abd ar-Rahman, *Yusuf u Zulaikha* (Yusuf und Zuleikha)
description: The most famous romantic epic version of the story *Yusuf u Zulaikha* was written by Maulana Nur ad-Din 'Abd ar-Rahman called Jami (died 898 AH /1492 AD) in his *Haft Awrang*. According to the colophon, this copy was penned in calligraphic *nasta’liq* by the scribe Sharaf ad-Din ash-Sharif al-Khwarazmi in 982 AH/1574 AD in Yazd, Iran. It was likely purchased with a group of other manuscripts for 20 gold ducats by Peter Lambeck in 1677 in Constantinople and then transferred to the Austrian National Library. It includes seven full-page paintings that are modelled on the *Shirazi* and *Qazwini* schools of painting. However, an Ottoman illuminator added elaborate marginal decoration at the end of the 16th or the early 17th century.
keywords: Painting; Safavid; Yusuf; Zulaikha
materials: Ink, opaque watercolour and gold on paper. Calligraphic *nasta'liq* script of 15 lines per page.
tags: Ink, opaque watercolour and gold on paper. Calligraphic nasta'liq script of 15 lines per page.

en.name: Qusayr Amra
short_description: Qusayr Amra is one of few Jordanian sites that have been listed as a World Heritage site. It represents the formative stage of Islamic art and architecture. It consists of vaulted reception hall and a bath house the walls of which were richly decorated. Its famous figurative wall paintings are proof that figurative art was not prohibited outside religious contexts at least during the first two centuries of Islam.
dates: AD 8th century; visited by Alois Musil in 1896
history: The best-known of the desert castles and a World Heritage Site. This monument was most probably built sometime between 723 and 743, by al-Walid Ibn Yazid, the future Umayyad caliph Walid II. The abandoned structure was re-discovered by Alois Musil in 1898, with the frescoes made famous in drawings by an Austrian artist named Mielich for Musil's book.
keywords: World Heritage Site; Alois Musil; rediscovery; archaeological investigation

en.name: Stuccowork
description: Stucco floral ornamentation and figurative scenes depict the life of the patron saint and saints to which the side chapels were dedicated between 1713 and 1726. The stuccowork, by the Italian master Anton Joseph Quadrio, was constructed between 1713 and 1721, and an anonymous Italian master between 1724 and 1726. With this exquisite work, St. Catherine's reached the ideal of *bel composto*, the characteristic Baroque unity of architecture, sculpture and painting.

ar.name: إبريق.
description: للإبريق جسم كروي منخفض وعنق عالٍ مقعر وحافة متجهة نحو الخارج وقاعدة منخفضة، وقد تم تلوين الآنية تحت التزجيج بالأزرق البراق والأحمر الكتيم والفيروزي المخضر المخفف على أرضية بيضاء وتحديد الزخارف باللون الأزرق الغامق. التصميم مؤلف من تركيب أفقي من زهرة خزامى متناوبة مع قرنفلة مما يذكر بالأسلوب الزهري المستخدم على الخزف الإزنيقي خلال القرنين العاشر- الحادي عشر/ السادس عشر-السابع عشر، ولكن الاختلاف واضح في نوعية الأرضية والتزجيج كما هو واضح في النماذج المبسطة والمجردة التي تم تنفيذها. تم تزيين الحواف الضيقة والزخارف الزهرية بنماذج هندسية. ويظهر في أسفل الإبريق علامة الهلال والنجمة.
إبريق من الخزف المطلي بألوان متعددة. رسوم الزخرفة ــ الزنابق والقرنفلات ــ تشير إلى الأسلوب النباتي للخزفيات الإزنيقية. يشي المقبض بشكل هندسي. ثمة هلال ونجمة تحت قاعدة الإبريق.
holder: المتحف الوطني للفنون الجميلة، استوكهولم الذي أعار القسم الرئيس من المجموعة الإسلامية إلى متحف آثار المتوسط والشرق الأدنى بشكل دائم منذ عام 1982 بهدف إعادة تنظيم مجموعاته المتزايدة.
keywords: خزف؛ زخرفة زهرية؛ فخار.
partner: متحف آثار البحر الأبيض المتوسط والشرق الأدنى

en.name: Jug.
description: The jug has a squat globular body, a high concave neck with a flared rim and a low foot. It has underglaze painted in a bright blue, a thick opaque red and a diluted turquoise-green on a white slip. The design outlined in dark blue appears in two horizontal registers alternating tulips and carnations, referring to the floral style of the Iznik ceramics of the AH 10th–11th / AD 16th–17th centuries. However, as well as an obviously different kind of slip and glaze, the motifs are simplified and schematically executed. The handle and the narrow bands edging the floral depictions are ornamented with geometrical patterns. The jug is marked under the foot with a crescent and an asterisk.

Jug of polychrome painted pottery. The motifs of the decoration – tulips and carnations – refer to the floral style of Iznik ceramics. The handle shows a geometrical pattern. The jug is marked under the foot with a crescent and an asterisk.
holder: Museum of Mediterranean and Near Eastern Antiquities (Medelhavsmuseet).

National Museum of Fine Arts, Stockholm. In order to reorganise the expanding collections, the main part of the Islamic collection has been on permanent loan to the Museum of Mediterranean and Near Eastern Antiquities since 1982.
keywords: Ceramic; pottery; floral decoration

es.name: Jarro.
description: Jarro de pie bajo, cuyo cuerpo globular de poca altura, contrasta con la forma cóncava del elevado cuello de marcada convexidad. Pintado bajo vidriado en azul brillante; rojo opaco espeso y un diluido verde turquesa, sobre engobe blanco. La decoración, trazada en negro, remite al estilo floral de Iznik del X-XI/ XVI-XVII, con dos registros horizontales que alternan tulipanes y claveles. La diferencia, a parte del engobe y el vidriado, radica en la simplificación y ejecución esquemática de los motivos decorativos. El asa y las estrechas cenefas que enmarcan las representaciones florales, están decoradas con diseños geométricos. La base presenta una marca en forma de media luna y otra de un asterisco.

Jarro de loza pintada en varios colores, decorada con tulipanes y claveles, dos motives que remiten al estilo floral de Iznik. El asa está decorada con un diseño geométrico. Presenta una marca de una media luna y un asterisco en la base.
holder: Museo de Antigüedades del Mediterráneo y Próximo Oriente (Medelhavsmuseet).

Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes, Estocolmo. En 1982, el grueso de la colección islámica se prestó de forma permanente al Museo de Antigüedades del Mediterráneo y Próximo Oriente (Medelhavsmuseet) en un intento de reorganizar una colección en constante crecimiento.
dates: Siglo XIII de la Hégira/ XIX d.C.
keywords: cerámica; alfarería; decoración floral
partner: Museo de Antigüedades del Mediterráneo y Oriente Próximo

fr.name: Pichet.
description: Pichet à panse bulbeuse de forme ramassée à important col concave, ouverture évasée et court pied annulaire. Il est peint sous glaçure en bleu vif, rouge opaque épais et vert turquoise dilué sur fond de couverte blanche. La composition à contours bleu foncé présente deux registres horizontaux alternés de tulipes et d'œillets, rappelant le style floral des céramiques d'Iznik des Xe-XIe siècles H (XVIe-XVIIe siècles J.-C.). Cependant, le type de couverte et de glaçure est différent et les motifs simplifiés sont exécutés de façon schématique. La poignée et les étroits bandeaux séparant les représentations florales sont ornés de motifs géométriques. Ce pichet est marqué sous le fond d'un croissant et d'un astérisque.

Jarre en céramique peinte polychrome. Les motifs décoratifs – tulipes et œillets – rappellent le style floral d'Iznik. La poignée est ornée d'un motif géométrique. La jarre est marquée sous le fond d'un croissant et d'un astérisque.
holder: Musée des antiquités méditerranéennes et proche-orientales (Medelhavsmuseet)

Musée national des Beaux-Arts, Stockholm. Dans le cadre de la réorganisation de ses collections en expansion, la plus grande partie des pièces d’art islamique ont fait l’objet d’un prêt permanent au Musée des antiquités méditerranéennes et proche-orientales en 1982.
dates: XIIIe siècle de l'Hégire (XIXe siècle J.-C.)
keywords: Céramique; poterie; décoration florale
