en.name: Mekleb bridal ornament
description: Dating to approximately 1900, this exquisite Mekleb ornament worn on the back of the bride serves as both a significant ceremonial adornment and a powerful protective token. The piece is richly embellished with an array of historical coins, traditional amulets, and vibrant glass beads. Notably, the prominent blue-colored elements integrated into the ornament function as protective amulets, culturally intended to shield the bride from the evil eye and envy.
holder: Tiraz: Widad Kawar Home for Arab Dress
keywords: Bridal; Wedding; Ornament; Ceremony; Protection
partner: Tiraz: Widad Kawar Home for Arab Dress

en.name: Toujane
description:
Toujane’s name is today a generic term used to describe three urban communities that represent the historical stages of the occupation of the area in this mountain range composed of the south-eastern edge of the Matmata massif, facing the Djeffara plain and the coast. At first the ancient village, which is still spoken of as if it were a distant memory, perched on a mountain peak of the Jabal Toujane not far from the Jabal Zembayet, was known for the crucial source of water that flows down its slopes. Only a few indefinable wall remains are left to be seen on this impregnable site, but we know that a citadel was once perched on this ridge; the locals call this installation “*mrah al-qsar*”, the forecourt of the *qsar*. Toujane as it is today, a more recent village, starts further down but without breaking away, and backs onto the mountain sides which, at this level, form a sort of creek pierced by the river; from there, the valley widens out, and one already gets a glimpse of the Djeffara. A new hamlet appeared right on the plain just over 20 years ago, in the Oued Troumane Valley: Dkhilet Toujane. As we cannot date the displacement of Matmata from its perch earlier than two centuries ago, thus similarly, the desertion of the perched site of Toujane must have occurred around the same time. Even taking into account an inscription that appears to date the foundation of its mosque, we are led to assume that present-day Toujane’s existence dates back to about four centuries ago.  
The 1,100 or so inhabitants of this village, which today is half deserted, continue to live a traditional way of life that is based economically on mountain arboriculture, in particular on olive groves, on some ploughed land in the shallower regions, and on some amount of breeding; they also exploit fields of esparto-grass which is used for weaving, most notably for the creation of large grain-containers known as *kambut* or *runiya*.  
Housing in Toujane is organised in levels on the slopes of the creek. A road traverses the agglomeration, linking it to Banu Zelten and to Mareth. The houses are built of bare stone which is bonded with plaster mortar. Each one is covered by a terrace, and their roofs are made of olive-tree or thuja-tree wood which has the advantage of not being susceptible to rot, except for the sheds whose vaulted roofs have openings through which grain can be poured in. Experience showed that this type of roofing prevented the proliferation of insects that threatened the conservation of cereals. Some houses have one or two rooms that have been created by excavating the mountainside, but every room is laid out on one or two levels around a modest courtyard, given the limited cramped space available. It can also be the case, due to the process of inheritance, that a house is divided into two or three more or less independent houses, whilst still sharing a single principal entrance.  
The mosque, gleaming with immaculate whiteness, highlights its contours against the fawn background of the mountain. This oratory is without doubt one of the oldest built in the Jabal: the relief inscription, on the wall that faces the entrance, features a date, probably the date of foundation, the year 1004/1596. It features three narrow bays parallel to the *qibla* wall, designed to follow the direction of prayer, and three further perpendicular bays, covered in vaults supported by masonry pillars and semi-circular arches. Enhanced by two small columns and framed with sculpted stone defined by serrated outlines, the *mihrab* is distinct for its accentuated bulge. The *minbar* is reached via two steps which stand against the base of a large window.  
Toujane represents a particular type of mountain habitat. It is a village, no longer on its perch, which occupies the two slopes of a creek that is pierced on both sides by the foreshore of the *wadi*. Its houses are built according to an original formula, following a plan consisting of a central courtyard with rooms excavated around it. It is also the prime example of a habitat that exploits the possibilities offered by nature, a habitat which responds adequately to the needs of this way of life.

es.name: Tuyan
description:
El nombre de Tuyan se ha convertido hoy día en un término genérico que designa tres unidades urbanas, representativas de otras tantas etapas en la historia de la ocupación del espacio en esta zona de montaña, delimitada por el lado sudeste del macizo de Matmata frente a la llanura de la Yeffara y la costa. En primer lugar, el antiguo pueblo del que aún se habla como un lejano recuerdo, colgado sobre un risco del Yebel Tuyan, no muy lejos del Yebel Zembayet, conocido por su importante fuente de agua, que surca las vertientes. Sobre este enclave inexpugnable, en el que aparecen únicamente algunos vestigios de muros difícilmente definibles aunque visibles, se sabe que había una ciudadela, los habitantes llaman a este promontorio Mrah el-Ksar, es decir, “el paso del *ksar*”. Más abajo, sin que llegue a haber una verdadera ruptura, comienza el Tuyan actual, constituido por una aldea más reciente, adosada a los flancos de la montaña que en este nivel forma una especie de grieta colgada sobre el *wad*; a partir de allí, el valle se alarga y se empieza a distinguir la Yeffara. Con un trazado cuadrado, apareció, hace más de 20 años, una nueva aldea en el valle del *wad* Truman: Djilet Tuyan. Si bien en el caso de Matmata no se ha podido demostrar su fundación hasta hace más de dos siglos, aquí, siempre que creamos la datación de una inscripción, que parece dar la fecha de la fundación de la mezquita del pueblo, se podría avanzar que la aparición del Tuyan actual se remonta a unos cuatro siglos, pero que el abandono total del enclave se debe situar bastante más tarde.  
Los 1.100 habitantes de este pueblo, hoy en día medio desierto, continúan viviendo según el modo de vida tradicional, fundamentado económicamente en la arboricultura de montaña, sobre todo olivares, algunos cultivos en las depresiones y una ganadería escasa. Explotan también los campos con esparto, que sirve para la fabricación de cesterías, sobre todo esos grandes contenedores de grano llamados *kambut* o *runiya*.  
El hábitat en Tuyan está organizado en gradas sobre las vertientes de las grietas. Una carretera atraviesa la población y la une con Banu Sultan y Mareth. Las viviendas están construidas con piedras desnudas unidas con yeso. Están cubiertas con terrazo, con techos de madera de olivo o de tuya, que tiene la ventaja de no pudrirse. En los graneros, los techos son reemplazados por bóvedas provistas de orificios destinados a verter el grano que hay que ensilar. La experiencia ha demostrado que este tipo de cubierta impide la proliferación de insectos dañinos para la conservación de los cereales. Algunas casas poseen uno o dos niveles alrededor de un modesto patio, dada la exigüidad del espacio disponible. Puede también ocurrir que, a causa de las herencias, la vivienda sea dividida en dos o tres viviendas más o menos independientes, siempre con una entrada principal única.  
La mezquita es de una blancura inmaculada, lo que hace que su contorno pueda divisarse desde lejos, sobre el fondo ocre de la montaña. Este oratorio es, sin duda, uno de los más antiguos del Yebel. La inscripción en relieve sobre el muro que queda frente a la puerta de entrada indica una fecha probable de fundación en 1004/1596. Se compone de tres estrechos tramos paralelos al muro de la *qibla*, en la dirección de la oración, y otros tres tramos perpendiculares cubiertos por bóvedas portadas por unos pilares de albañilería y arcos de medio punto. Realzado por dos columnitas, enmarcado en piedra tallada y terminado en dientes, el *mihrab* se distingue porque está muy abombado. Dos marcas adosadas al basamento de una ventana de amplia factura sirven como *minbar*.  
Tuyan representa un tipo particular de hábitat de montaña. El pueblo ocupa dos laderas de una grieta, de una parte a la otra de un valle formado por el lecho del río. Sus viviendas están construidas según una fórmula original, siguiendo un plano de patio central con habitaciones excavadas. Es así el ejemplo de un hábitat que explota las posibilidades ofrecidas por la naturaleza, con respuestas adecuadas a las exigencias del modo de vida.

fr.name: TOUJANE
description:
Le nom de Toujane est devenu aujourd’hui un terme générique qui évoque trois unités urbaines, représentant autant d’étapes dans l’histoire de l’occupation de l’espace dans cette zone de montagne formée par les rebords sud-est du massif de Matmata, en face de la plaine de la Djeffara et de la côte. D’abord l’ancien village dont on parle encore comme d’un souvenir lointain, perché sur un piton du Djebel Toujane non loin du Djebel Zembayet, connu pour son importante source d’eau qui déferle de ses versants. Sur ce site inexpugnable, seuls quelques vestiges de murs indéfinissables sont encore visibles, mais l’on sait qu’une citadelle se juchait sur cette crête; les habitants appellent cette installation “*mrah elqasr*”, c’est-à-dire le parcours du ksar. Plus bas, mais sans véritable rupture, commence le Toujane actuel, un village plus récent, adossé aux flancs de la montagne qui forme à ce niveau une sorte de crique, percée par l’oued; à partir de là, la vallée s’élargit, et l’on entrevoit déjà la Djeffara. Carrément en plaine, un nouveau hameau est apparu, voilà plus de vingt ans, dans la vallée de l’Oued Troumane: Dkhilet Toujane. Si l’on n’a pas pu remonter au-delà de deux siècles pour situer le déperchement de Matmata, ici, à en croire une inscription qui semble dater la fondation de la mosquée du village, on peut avancer que l’apparition du Toujane actuel remonterait à environ quatre siècles, mais que l’abandon total du site perché se situerait bien plus tard.  
Les quelque 1 100 habitants de ce village, aujourd’hui à moitié déserté, continuent à vivre selon un mode de vie traditionnel fondé économiquement sur une arboriculture de montagne, surtout d’oliviers, quelques labours dans les dépressions, et un élevage d’appoint; ils exploitent aussi des champs d’alfa qui sert à la fabrication de la sparterie, notamment ces grands contenants à grains appelés *kambout* ou *rouniya*.  
L’habitat à Toujane est organisé en gradins sur les versants de la crique. Une route traverse l’agglomération et la relie à Banu Zelten et à Mareth. Les habitations sont construites en pierre nue liée par un mortier de plâtre. Elles sont couvertes en terrasse par des toits en bois d’olivier ou de thuya qui a l’avantage d’être imputrescible, sauf les greniers où les plafonds sont remplacés par des voûtes munies d’orifices destinés à verser le grain à ensiler. L’expérience a montré que ce type de couverture empêchait la prolifération d’insectes nuisibles à la conservation des céréales. Quelques maisons possèdent une ou deux pièces excavées dans le flanc de la montagne, mais toutes sont organisées sur un ou deux niveaux autour d’une modeste cour, étant donné l’exiguïté de l’espace disponible. Il peut aussi arriver que, par le jeu des héritages, la maison soit divisée en deux voire en trois demeures plus ou moins indépendantes, avec toutefois une entrée principale unique.  
La mosquée, d’une blancheur immaculée, découpe ses contours sur le fond fauve de la montagne. Cet oratoire est sans doute l’un des plus anciens installés dans le Djebel: l’inscription en relief, sur le mur qui fait face à la porte d’entrée, indique une date probable de fondation en 1004/1596. Il se compose de trois étroites travées parallèles au mur de la *qibla*, en direction de la prière, et trois autres perpendiculaires, couvertes de voûtes portées par des piliers en maçonnerie et des arcs en plein cintre. Rehaussé de deux colonnettes et encadré de pierre taillée cernée de dentelures, le *mihrab* se distingue par son bombage accentué. Deux marches adossées au soubassement d’une fenêtre à large embrasure servent de minbar.  
Toujane représente un type particulier d’habitat de montagne. C’est un village déperché qui occupe les deux versants d’une crique, de part et d’autre d’une percée faite par le lit de l’oued. Ses habitations sont construites selon une formule originale, suivant un plan à cour centrale avec des pièces excavées. C’est aussi l’exemple d’un habitat qui exploite les possibilités offertes par la nature, qui apporte des réponses adéquates aux exigences du mode de vie.

en.name: Noria al-Kudhra, al-Dawalik and al-Dasha
names: Noria al Khudra, al-Dawalik and al-Dasha
description: Another set of three water wheels around a dam are found north of the tell upon which the citadel of Hama once towered. These are the Noria al-Khudra and the Noria al-Dawalik, on the left side of the bank, and the aforementioned Noriat al- Dahsha on the opposite side, irrigating the green fields on the lower slopes by the Mosque of Abu al-Fida. The largest of the three, al-Khudra, measures about 17.50 meters with the smaller Noria Dawalik just next by. The Dahsha is smallish in size, but it features some interesting structural peculiarities. For example, the triangle upon which the axle of the wheel rests is actually rectangular in shape and the buckets around its perimeter alternate in size.

en.name: Oršić Castle, Central Hall Frescoes
description: *Trompe l'œil* window frescos articulate the walls of the Central hall. Within the windows are painted landscapes.

ar.name: حقة (نرجيلة)
description: هناك مجموعة صغيرة من الحقق مصنوعة من زجاج بلون أخضر زمردي ذات تزيين مرتبط بهذا الشكل. وفي بعضها تم رسم الصورة مباشرة على الزجاج وفي بعضها الآخر فقد رسمت بشكل معكوس كما في هذه القطعة والذي يعني أن الذهب كان يستخدم كخلفية للصور – الخشخاش والسرو مع الحدود الورقية العديدة ذات بعض التفاصيل بالذهب أو المينا الأصفر.
type: زجاج أخضر زمردي مزين بمينا الذهب ومينا صفراء
dates: النصف الأول من القرن الثاني عشر الهجري / النصف الأول من القرن الثامن عشر الميلادي

en.name: *Huqqa* (water pipe)
description: There is a small group of *huqqa*s made of emerald-green glass with a related decoration. On some, the motif was painted direct on the glass. On others, it was painted “in reserve,” as on this piece, which means that the gold was largely used as the background for the motifs – poppies and cypresses along with various leaf borders with a few details in gold or yellow enamel.
dates: Hegira 1st half of the 12th century / AD 1st half of the 18th century
keywords: Huqqa; Gold; Mughal; Glass
materials: Emerald-green glass decorated with gold and yellow enamel
tags: Emerald-green glass decorated with gold and yellow enamel

ar.name: غطاء قبر.
description: قطعة من الحرير الأحمر مقسمة إلى أشرطة متكسرة عاجية اللون، وهي تؤلف وحدة مكررة من ثلاثة أجزاء. يتألف الجزء الرئيس من الشهادة (لا إله إلا الله محمد رسول الله)، تعلوها آية من القرآن (السورة 2، الآية 144) التي تتحدث عن اتجاه الصلاة، القبلة، وتحتها تضرع ديني "سبحان الله وبحمده، سبحان الله العظيم". يفصل بين هذه الوحدات المتكررة أشرطة تحوي حليات على شكل حجب متقابلة رأساً على عقب، مرتبة بين رصائع دائرية، وتحوي هذه الحجب تضرعات "يا منّان" و"يا حنّان"، أما الدوائر فتحوي "يا سبحان" و"يا سلطان". لقد تم تصنيع هذه المنسوجات خلال الفترة العثمانية لتغطية قبور الشخصيات المهمة، ولما كان المتوفى مدفون باتجاه القبلة، فإن وجود الآية التي تتحدث عن القبلة له معنى خاص. يبدو أن هذا النوع من أغطية القبور قد تمت حياكته بكميات كبيرة، إذ يمكن العثور على الحرير المنقوش بالنماذج نفسها في المجموعات المتحفية حول العالم.

قطعة من القماش الأحمر، المنسوجة من الحرير، والمزخرفة بأشرطة متعرِّجة، تتكرَّر فيها النقوش، من بينها آيات قرآنية تتحدَّث عن طلب الرحمة والمغفرة، من الله عز وجل. تمَّ إنتاج هذه القطعة، وغيرها من الأقمشة، في العصر العثماني، وكانت تستخدم لتغطية القبور، ومن أمثلتها غطاء الكعبة المُشرَّفة، في مكة المكرمة.
keywords: قطعة ذات استعمال ديني؛ الجنائزية

en.name: Tomb cover.
description: A section of red silk divided into ivory-coloured zigzag bands. These bands form a three-part repeat unit in which the main section is a wide band containing the Muslim profession of faith, the Shahada. Above this, a border band contains a verse from the Qur'an (2: 144) which concerns the *qibla*, or direction of prayer. Below, a pious invocation reads 'Praise God and glorify Him; praise God the mighty.' These repeat units are separated by bands in which finial-shaped pendants, facing alternately up and down, are arranged among circular medallions; these shapes contain rhyming invocations: 'O Benefactor (ya mannan)!' and 'O Compassionate (ya hannan)!' in the pendants, and 'O Praise (ya subhan)!' and 'O Authority (ya sultan)!' in the circles. Textiles like this one were made under the Ottomans to cover the cenotaphs of important individuals. Since the deceased is buried facing Mecca, the inclusion of the Qur'anic verse about the *qibla* has special significance. This particular type of tomb cover appears to have been woven in large quantities, as silks with an identical pattern can be found in collections all over the world.

A section of red silk woven with zigzag bands containing several repeating inscriptions, among them Qur’anic verses and rhyming invocations of God. Many similar textiles were made under the Ottomans as tomb covers and as linings for the Ka’ba in Mecca.
keywords: religious object; funerary object

es.name: Cobertor de tumba.
description:
Fragmento de un tejido de seda roja con bandas caligráficas en zigzag, de color marfil. Estas bandas tripartitas repiten los mismos textos: la central es la más ancha y en ella se lee la *shahada*, la profesión de fe musulmana; la superior presenta una aleya coránica (2:144) que habla de la *qibla*; la inferior contiene una piadosa invocación que dice: “Alabad a Dios y glorificadlo, alabad a Dios todopoderoso”. Separan las bandas caligráficas franjas con colgantes en forma de florones, orientados en sentidos opuestos alternativamente y con medallones circulares intercalados. Estas formas contienen invocaciones rimadas: “¡Oh benefactor!” *(ya mannan)* y “Oh compasivo!” *(ya hannan)* en los colgantes; “¡Oh alabanza!” *(ya subhan)* y “¡Oh autoridad!” *(ya sultan)* en los medallones.  
En época otomana, los cenotafios de personas importantes se cubrían con este tipo de mantos. Las inscripciones con versos coránicos sobre la *qibla* tienen un significado especial ya que los fallecidos eran enterrados con el rostro hacia La Meca. Sedas con este mismo diseño pueden contemplarse en colecciones de todo el mundo, lo que indica que probablemente se tejieron coberturas de tumba como esta en grandes cantidades.

Fragmento de tejido en seda roja con bandas en zigzag que repiten las misma inscripciones, entre ellas versos del Corán e invocaciones rimadas a Dios. En época otomana se produjeron muchas telas como esta para cubrir tumbas y la Kaaba de La Meca.
dates: Siglo XII de la Hégira / XVIII d. C.
keywords: objeto religioso; objeto funerário

fr.name: Couverture de tombeau.
description: Panneau de soie rouge compartimenté par plusieurs bandes en zigzag de couleur ivoire. Elles forment un motif répété en trois parties dont la section principale est une large bande contenant la profession de foi musulmane, la *chahadah*. Au-dessus, la bordure reprend un verset du Coran (sourate 2, verset 144) qui concerne la *qibla* ou l'orientation pour la prière. En dessous, une invocation pieuse dit : “Loue Dieu et glorifie-le ; loue Dieu le Tout-puissant.” Ces ensembles répétés sont séparés par des bandeaux à pendants en forme de pinacle, orientés alternativement vers le haut et le bas, répartis entre des médaillons circulaires. Ces formes contiennent des invocations rimées “Ô Bienfaiteur (*ya mannan*) !” et “Ô Miséricordieux (*ya hannan*) !” dans les pendants et “Ô Louange (*ya subhan*) !” et “Ô Autorité (*ya sultan*) !” dans les cercles. Des tissus de ce type furent fabriqués sous les Ottomans pour recouvrir les cénotaphes de personnalités importantes. Comme le défunt est enterré face à La Mecque, l'inclusion de versets coraniques sur la *qibla* présente une signification spéciale. Ce type particulier de couverture de tombeau semble avoir été réalisé en grandes quantités, car des panneaux de soie à motifs identiques figurent dans de nombreuses collections dans le monde.

Section d'un panneau de soie rouge tissée à bandes en zigzag comprenant plusieurs inscriptions répétées, parmi lesquelles des versets coraniques et des invocations rimées du nom de Dieu. De nombreux textiles similaires furent fabriqués sous les Ottomans comme couvertures de tombes ou voiles pour la Kaaba à La Mecque.
dates: XIIe siècle de l’Hégire (XVIIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: Objet religieux ; objet funéraire

en.name: Middle room balcony railings
description: Each room has a different colour scheme and decorative emphasis with multicoloured bookshelves of different lacquered finishes in green, red and black decorated with *chinoiserie* motifs. Each of the rooms is two-storeys high, with a balcony and stairs incorporated into the furniture.
place: Interior, Biblioteca Joanina da Universidade de Coimbra
artist: Design and execution: Francesco Gualdini, João Rodrigues de Almeida; supervisor: Gaspar Ferreira; painting and gilding of woodwork: Manuel da Silva [dates unknown]
partner: Institute for the Administration of Architectural and Archaeological Heritage -  IGESPAR

pt.name: Varandas, estantes e *chinoiserie*
description: As cores (em laca verde, vermelha e negra) variam nas estantes de cada sala, criando um ambiente diferente em cada uma delas. Todas têm dois andares, com um varandim e escadas de acesso aos livros embebidas engenhosamente nas estantes.
artist: Francesco Gualdini e João Rodrigues de Almeida (concepção e execução). Gaspar Ferreira (mestre-de-obras). Manuel da Silva (pintura e douradura)

en.name: Tunic (*'aba'a*)
description: Tunic in cream ground with stencilled decoration in black showing vegetal and geometrical motifs. Fortuny was son of the well-known Spanish painter Mariano Fortuny. He designed one of the early dresses for women without corsets. Some of his designs were inspired in the Orientalism style, he was influenced by his travels and of the historical textiles that he collected.
holder: Museum of Costume, Ethnographical Heritage Research Centre
keywords: Costumes; Design; North African influence; Spanish Muslim influence

ar.name: قطعة من خلفية (ظهر) قفطان
description: هذه اللوحة الرائعة من قفطان هي مثال عن إنتاج السيراسر عالي الجودة جدا في إسطنبول . والسيراسر هي مادة التي كانت مفضلة جدا في البلاط العثماني وهي مكونة من حرير منسوج بخيوط ملفوفة من الذهب والفضة في بنية مركبة من خيطي سداة ولحمتين متتامتين أكثر وتصميم ريش الطاووس يشير إلى طائر الذي سكن الجنة وطرد منها مع آدم وحواء بسبب معصيتهم لأوامر الله والتصاميم كبيرة القياس المتباعدة المركز غالبا استخدمت في أقمشة منتصف إلى أواخر القرن السادس عشر كما كانت ترى عن بعد وتفضل كملابس للاستعراض.
type: لقد كان القماش الحريري المميز ذو النطاق الكبير المصنوع من  نماذج  من المواد المفضلة للملابس الفاخرة بين الطبقة السامية في القرن السادس عشر في إسطنبول وكانت غالبا تستخدم من أجل القفاطين السميكة الملونة بشكل غني للسلاطين العثمانيين وفي هذا المثال النموذج الشاقولي للطبقات مشابه من حيث الطراز لبلاطات الجدار الخزفية في الأبنية في تلك الفترة. والحياكة المشار لها بالتركية باللكمه تتضمن خيوط معدنية في السداة مدخلة في اللامباس أو القماش متعدد الحياكة .وإن أقمشة الكامه العثمانية تجمع عادة أرضية الساتان مع تصميم التويل المحاك الموشى بالذهب وإن نماذج توشيتها تلتقط الضوء وتظهر عائمة فوق الخلفية الوضاءة.
dates: القرن العاشر الهجري / منتصف القرن السادس عشر الميلادي

en.name: Fragment of a kaftan back
description: This magnificent panel from a kaftan is an example of very high-grade *seraser* production in Istanbul. *Seraser*, a material that was highly favoured at the Ottoman court, is composed of gold- and silver-wrapped silk woven in a compound structure of two warps and two or more complementary wefts. The design of peacock feathers alludes to the bird who resided in paradise until he was expelled along with Adam and Eve for failing to follow God's commandments. Eccentric largescale designs were often used on mid- to late sixteenth century textiles, as they were visible from a distance and favoured for parade garments.
keywords: Ottoman; Istanbul; Turkey; Anatolia; textile; silk; caftan; cloth; clothing; dress; fabric; peacock; garment; Ottoman silk; Ottoman textile; silver; textile; zoomorphic imagery

de.name: Seitenaltäre St. Stephanus und St. Sebastian
description: Die Gemälde der beiden mittleren Seitenaltäre repräsentieren als Importe venezianischer Malerei den weltläufigen Geschmack des Propstes Herculan Karg. Pittoni malte den Erzmärtyrer Stephanus, den Pestpatron Sebastian dessen noch berühmterer Kollege Tiepolo. Durch bewußten Verzicht auf eine Retabelarchitektur erscheinen die kostbaren Altarblätter dem Betrachter gleichwohl wie Galeriebilder, die zudem von Putti durch das Beiseiteziehen einer Draperie enthüllt werden. Die Skulpturen sind Teil eines über alle Seitenaltäre verteilten Apostelzyklus.
place: Drittes Kapellenpaar ab dem Chor, davon der Stephanusaltar links und der Sebastiansaltar rechts
artist: Altararchitektur und Skuplturen: Johann Baptist Straub (1704-1784); Altarblätter: Giovanni Battista Pittoni (1687-1767); Giovanni Battista Tiepolo (1696-1770)

en.name: Side altars depicting St. Stephen and St. Sebastian
description:
As imports of Venetian painting, the pictures on the two middle altars embody the cosmopolitan taste of the Provost, Herculan Karg. Giovanni Pittoni painted the Protomartyr Stephen. Likewise, Giovanni Tiepolo, Pittoni’s even more renowned colleague, painted St. Sebastian who is the patron saint of plague victims.  
By intentionally eschewing the typical retable architecture, the sumptuous altarpieces appear to the viewer as being pictures in a gallery, unveiled by puttos through means of sculpted drapery which seems to be pulled aside. The flanking sculptures belong to a cycle depicting the 12 Apostles who are distributed among the side altars.
place: The third pair of altars from the chancel. St. Stephen is on the left and St. Sebastian on the right.
artist: Architecture and sculpture on the altars: Johann Baptist Straub (1704–84);  Altarpieces: Giovanni Battista Pittoni (1687–1767) and Giovanni Battista Tiepolo (1696–1770)
partner: University of Munich, Institute of Art History

ar.name: فأس قتال لعضو لحرس السلطان
description: هذا الفأس ينتمي لعنصر من الحراس الشخصيين للسلطان محمد بن قاتيباي من المماليك البرجية القوقازية وقد حكم المماليك مصر وسوريا اعتبارا من 1250 ميلادي حتى سقوط إمبراطوريتهم لصالح العثمانيين في عام 1517 ميلادي عندما انتقلت غنائم المماليك إلى إسطنبول.
keywords: فأس ، مملوكي
materials: حديد ، ذهب دمشقي ، ملون بالأزرق بشكل ساخن

de.name: Garde-Streitbeil
description: Bei diesem Streitbeil handelt es sich um die Waffe eines Leibgardisten des Sultans Mohammed Ibn Qait Bay (Kait Bey) aus der kaukasisch-turanischen Dynastie der Mamluken. Die Mamluken beherrschten seit 1250 Ägypten und Syrien. Nach der Eroberung ihres Reiches durch die Osmanen im Jahr 1517 gelangte eine reiche mamlukische Beute nach Istanbul.
keywords: Streitbeil; Mameluken

en.name: Battle axe of a member of the Sultan's Guard
description: This axe belonged to a member of the Life Guards of Sultan Muhammad ibn Qaytbay from the Caucasian-Burji Mamluks. The Mamluks ruled Egypt and Syria from AD 1250 until their empire fell to the Ottomans in AD 1517, when a wealth of Mamluk booty was removed to Istanbul.
keywords: Arms; Mamluk arms; Mamluk army; Muhammad ibn Qaytbay; Burji; weapon; axe; Mamluck

en.name: Decorative ivory plaque
short_description: This fragmentary plaque, datable to the late Umayyad period is a superb example of high quality craftsmenship. It is carved in high relief allowing the decoration to stand in depth. Its main decoration consists of a vine scroll with five-lobed leaves and bunches of grapes. The vine stalks curl symmetrically creating three large circles. The central circle contains four smaller ones, two with a five-lobed leave and two with a bird, which turns its head backwards so as to pluck the fruit. The upper and lower circles form a spiral with five-lobed leaves and bunches of grapes. Outside the main scroll there are smaller three-lobed leaves and at the edge a hare and another bird. The object was bought by Antoni Benaki in 1919 from the Cairo dealer Maurice Nahman who provided objects for most of the important collectiors at the beginning of the 20th century.
keywords: collecting; Greeks; dealer; Egypt

en.name: Architectural drawing of Mar Mikhael train station
short_description: This architectural drawing shows the plan of the Mar Mikhael (Saint Michael) train station that was built in 1891. The station served as a terminal for visitors to the city, and was in use until 1976.
keywords: Travel; Train; Trade; Railway

en.name: Emigrant family
short_description: The 1923 population exchange between Greece and Turkey was based upon religious identity, and involved the Greek Orthodox citizens of Turkey and the Muslim citizens of Greece. The "Convention Concerning the Exchange of Greek and Turkish Populations" was signed at Lausanne, Switzerland, on 30 January 1923, by the governments of Greece and Turkey. This photograph belongs to the Luka Likidis family, who migrated from Bodrum to Crete in 1916.
holder: Population Exchange Museum (The Foundation of Lausanne Treaty Emigrants)
keywords: migration; population exchange
partner: Population Exchange Museum (The Foundation of Lausanne Treaty Emigrants)

en.name: Large *khabiya* jar
description: This large jar, *khabiya*, is intended for the storage of grain, semolina, oil, or water. Its motifs are typical of Tunisian craftsmanship, whose main production centre was in the pottery district (Qallaline) of Tunis. These motifs, the *taouq* (rim decoration), the strip of vertical hatching, and the band of ovoid kernels (*qloub*) are linked by similar designs. The composition is arranged in parallel bands, with the repeated use of yellow, green and brown.
holder: Museum of the Arab World Institute
materials: Clay; design painted on opaque glaze
partner: Museum of the Arab World Institute

fr.name: Grande jarre *khabiya*
description: Cette grosse jarre, *khabiya*, est destinée à la conservation du grain, de la semoule, de l'huile ou de l'eau. Ses motifs sont typiques de l'artisanat tunisien, dont le grand centre de production se trouvait dans le quartier des potiers (Qallaline) de Tunis : le *tawq* (collier) décorant le haut de la panse, la bande de hachures verticales, et la frise à noyaux (*qloub*) reliée par les traits. Il en est de même pour la composition, organisée en registres parallèles, et l'emploi des couleurs jaune, verte et brune.
holder: Musée de l'Institut du monde arabe
dates: XIIIe siècle de l'Hégire / XIXe siècle J.-C.
materials: Pâte argileuse, décor peint sous glaçure opaque
tags: Pâte argileuse, décor peint sous glaçure opaque

en.name: Conversation with Nasser at the Royal Palace of Dedinje, Belgrade
description: Josip Broz Tito and Gamal Abdel Nasser are shown in conversation at the Royal Palace of Dedinje in Belgrade on 16 July 1956, during Nasser's state visit to Yugoslavia. The two leaders, both in military uniform, appear relaxed and engaged, an image that also hints at their shared background as soldiers who became heads of state. The meeting came at a decisive moment in the search for a political alternative to the Cold War blocs. Two days later, Tito, Nasser and Indian Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru met on the Brioni Islands, where, on 19 July, they issued a joint statement articulating principles that would later become central to the Non-Aligned Movement, formally launched at the Belgrade Conference in 1961 with the participation of 25 countries. The photograph captures a moment in the deepening relationship between Yugoslavia and Egypt, at a time when states across Asia, Africa and beyond were seeking greater autonomy from the dominant Cold War blocs.

ar.name: قطعة نقدية محفور عليها نقش الشهادة
description: نقش على هذه العملات نقش الشهادتين التي تقرأ (لا إله إلا الله محمداً رسول الله ).وفي القرون قبل الإسلام، 200 قبل الميلاد – 651 ميلادي فإن العديد من الحكّام والأسر الحاكمة والسلطات أصدرت قطعا نقدية التي كان يتم تداولها في عُمان والخليج العربي. والقطع النقدية التي صنعت في عُمان في الفترة 133-906 هجري / 751-1500 ميلادي أظهرت وسائل التعبير عن السلطة والمكانة والاستقلال. وإن الحكّام المحليين أصدروا عملتهم الخاصة اعتبارا من 174 هجري / 791 ميلادي. إن أتباع الإباضية (وهم فرقة إسلامية) أسسوا إمامات (وهي نظم حكم فريدة من نوعها تستند لانتخاب شخص يعرف بعلمه وتقواه) في عُمان وذلك في العام 132 هجري/749 ميلادي. والأئمة الإباضية أصدروا قطعهم النقدية الفضية الخاصة. وقد وجدت العديد من هذه القطع النقدية في المناطق التي استكشفت في عام 1422 هجري/ 2002 ميلادي في ولاية بهلالء.  تحمل القطع النقدية اسم  مصنع صك العملة "" عُمان"" وأسماء الحكام الإباضيين "" الخليل بن شاذان"" و"" رشيد بن  سعيد "" .إن الوجيهيين هم أسرة حاكمة محلية قادها يوسف ابن وجيه وهو حاكم سابق من البوسعيد  الذين حكموا عُمان والذين سيطروا على المناطق الساحلية الشمالية من عُمان خلال القرن الرابع الهجري / العاشر الميلادي وقاموا بإنشاء مدينة صحار في مركز رئيسي من مراكز التجارة الدولية و قاموا بإنتاج عملتهم الخاصة.والقطع النقدية التي أصدرت من قبل الوجيهيين ،المشابهة لما هو مبين هنا ، حافظت على النقش العباسي المعياري مع إضافة اسم الحاكم المحلي أسفل النقش في الجهة المعاكسة.إن العديد من السلالات الحاكمة الإسلامية استمرت في إصدار العملات في وبجوار شبه الجزيرة العربية حيث كانت عملات اليمن وهرمز شائعة في شبه جزيرة عُمان اعتبارا من العام 493 هجري/ 1100 ميلادي وبعد عام 493 هجري/ 1100 ميلادي فإن العملات الذهبية الأيوبية من اليمن و الدنانير الفاطمية من مصر كانت تستخدم بانتظام في موانئ عُمان. والتجارة في جنوب شبه الجزيرة العربية تركزت في ميناء عدن اليمني ومن هناك فإن العديد من الدنانير الأيوبية وجدت طريقها لعُمان. وفي أثناء ذلك فإن ملوك هرمز (فيما يعرف اليوم بعُمان وإيران) تنافسوا على التجارة على طول ساحل إيران. وإن القطع النقدية الذهبية والفضية الهرمزية الصغيرة أصبحت العملة الأكثر أهمية في عُمان خلال هذه الفترة.
dates: القرن الثاني – الثامن الهجري / القرن الثامن – الرابع عشر الميلادي
keywords: قطع نقدية ، عملة ، دراسة العملات ، عباسي ، هرمز
tags: قطع نقدية ، عملة ، دراسة العملات ، عباسي ، هرمز

en.name: Coin Inscribed with Declaration of Faith
description:
The most basic requirement of being a Muslim is to publicly declare one’s faith in Arabic, with sincerity and without reservation. The Declaration of Faith is one of the five pillars of Islam and provides a foundation for all other Islamic beliefs and practices. In translation, it usually reads, "There is no God but Allah and Muhammed is His Messenger". Coins such as those shown here were often used to convey this message.  
  
In the centuries before the arrival of Islam, 200 BC-651AD, many rulers, dynasties and powers issued coins that circulated in Oman and the Arabian Gulf. Coins made in Oman 133-906 AH / 751 - 1500 AD demonstrated a means of displaying power, status and independence. Local rulers issued their own currency from as early as 174 AH / 791 AD.  
  
Followers of Ibadism (a branch of Islam) establish an Imamate (a unique governing system based on electing a person known for his knowledge and piety) in Oman in 132 AH/749 AD. The Ibadi imams issued their own silver coins. Many of these coins were found in a hoard discovered in 1422 AH/ 2002 AD in the Wilayet of Buhla. The coins carry the mint name "Uman", and the names of the Ibadi rulers " al-khalil bin Shadhan" and " Rashid bin Said". The Wajihids, a local dynasty led by Yusuf bin Wajih, a former Abbasaid governor based in Oman, took control of the northern coastal regions of Oman during the 4th century AH/10 century AD, developing the town of Sohar into a major centre of international commerce and producing their own currency. Coins issued by the Wajihids, similar to the coin shown here, kept the standard Abbasid inscription, with the name of their local governor added below the inscription on the reverse.  
  
Various Islamic dynasties continued to issue coins in and around the Arabian Peninsula, with coins from Yemen and Hormuz being popular in the Oman Peninsula from 493 AH /1100 AD onward. After 493 AH / 1100AD, Ayyubid gold coins from Yemen and Fatimid dinars from Egypt were regularly used as trade coinage in the ports of Oman. Trade in southern Arabia centred on the Yemen port of Aden, from where many Ayyubid dinars made their way to Oman. Meanwhile, the kings of Hormuz (in modern- day Oman and Iran) competed for trade along the coast of Iran. Small gold and silver Hormuzi coins became the most important currency in Oman during this period.
artist: Issuing the caliph Abu Ahmad al-Muktafi Bi-Allah
keywords: Coins; Currency; Numismatics; Abbasid; Hurmuz

en.name: *St. Blaise*
description: A freestanding figure of the patron saint of the church and of Dubrovnik itself St. Blaise.

en.name: *Caiques and Sailboats at the Bosporus*
short_description: Felix Ziem was able to produce works in many styles such as portraits, still life, genre scenes and historical depictions, though he is primarily renowned as a landscape artist. He was an active member of the Barbizon school, which primarily focused on the depiction of nature. In the painting, Istanbul is represented through a few mosque silhouettes in the background. Nonetheless, as in his Venetian scenes, the painting emphasizes the picturesque union of the city, the sea and human figures, which have been reduced to mere colour stains. Ziem, who produced his own paints from natural pigments, influenced other artists with the use of colour in his paintings. He is known to have used “lapis lazuli” for the dominant blue colour in this painting.
keywords: Felix Ziem; Orientalism; painting; İstanbul

en.name: Ceramic boat model
description: This is one of many clay models of flat-bottomed boats with vertical sides found at Ur, of varying shapes and sizes. It is among several examples that bear a resemblance to the *isbiya* barge (see item 2024.8.2 in the collection of the Open Museum Initiative for Water Culture), particularly in the lip protruding from the bottom edge of the boat. This feature is called *leffa* in Hit, where *isbiyas* were traditionally made, and is unique to the *isbiya*.
keywords: Ur; Sumerian; ceramic; boat; model

en.name: Cup
description: This refined cup made of greenish tinged glass with slightly curved sides, was initially blown as a thick vessel. Its flowing decoration was then masterfully wheel-cut in relief. This work was carried out in the so-called bevelled technique, where the slanted profile of the decoration blurs the distinction between the pattern and the background. This technique is first seen in profusion in the stucco decoration of the second and third century AH / ninth century AD palace city of Samarra in Iraq, before its spread across the Islamic empire. The manufacture of glass was highly developed in pre-Islamic times in both Iran and Syria, and production continued to develop under Islam. Cut glass was the most luxurious of all, requiring separate skills of hot glass working and wheel-cutting the finished products.
keywords: Glass; Free-blown; Relief-cut; Abbasid; Samanid

en.name: Minorite Church of Eger
description:
The ground plan of the Church merges central and longitudinal types. The nave consists of three sections covered by sail vaults, with an adjoining entrance hall and organ loft on the entrance side, and a rather narrow sanctuary on the other side. The first two sections are extended by altar niches, and the third section widens into a transept with semi-circular ends, giving the monumental longitudinal space – articulated by free-standing columns – a central feel. The two-tower façade gives the building a monumental appeal: standing on a high footing, it is separated into two levels by an emphasised stringcourse. The attic is articulated by outstanding moulding, above which are arched gables and the towers. The mid-section, framed by three-quarter detached Ionic columns, forms a convex arch. On the keystone of the drip moulding above the gate there is an inscription that reads: “PRO DEO NUNQUAM SATIS” (“For God nothing is enough”). On the supraport the year “MDCCLXXI” is inscribed. The attic inscription reads “DEO. O. M. / IN HONOREM / THAUMATURGI / DIVI / ANTONII / PADUANI/ DICATA” (“Deo. O\[ptimo\] M\[aximo\] the God, the Best, the Greatest / dedicated in honour of the Thaumaturgic St. Anthony of Padua”). On the gables a statue of St. Anthony of Padua stands between two angels.  
Inside, the main altarpiece painting the *Virgin Mary Appears to St. Anthony* has statues of St. Louis and St. Bonaventure either side of it; the entirety crowned by an eagle that symbolises St. John. On the ceiling of the nave are scenes from the Life of St. Anthony. The side altars are dedicated to the Holy Cross, Our Lady of Sorrows, St. John of Nepomuk, St. Anne, St. Joseph and St. Florian; the painted architectural elements of the two latter were painted by the local painter Anton Lieb, in 1805. The painting on the Altar of the Holy Cross was replaced in the 1930s. The figure of St. John seen in the pulpit was created by Joseph Moczer from Eger. The interior decoration includes carved pews and other fine furniture, the exceptional carving of which is by the master cabinet maker Benedictus Mönch, who between 1777 and 1779 also carved the choir pews of the organ loft in a Louis XIV style with a hint of Neo-Classicism. The pews in the nave were carved by Joseph Stöckerle.

The Minorite Church of Eger represents Hungarian Baroque art of exceptional quality. The identity of the architect is unclear, for although historically the building design has been attributed to Kilian Ignaz Dientzenhoffer from Prague, more recent research indicates that Matthias Gerl from Vienna was the architect. The model for the building was the Piarist Church of Maria Treu in Vienna, where it is known Gerl worked on the construction. The ground plan, interior design and furnishings all mirror the splendour of religious Baroque architecture; the building is a fine example of the religious culture of the era.
artist: Architecture (attributed to): Matthias Gerl (1712–1765), Kilian Ignaz Dientzenhoffer (1689–1751)(?); master builders: Johann Falk, Johann Nitsmann, Johann Povolni; foreman: Andreas Trethon; stonemasons: Joseph Hagen, Joseph Miller; sculptors: “Öreg” (Old) János Hösz, Joseph Hebenstreit, Joseph Moczer; marbling: Mihály Spórer; master carpenters: György Polereczky; Melchior Máhr; painters: Martin Reindl, Johann Lukas Kracker, Johann Zirckler, Anton Lieb; cabinet makers: Benedictus Mönch, Joseph Stöckerle
history:
The decision to build a Minorite Church and Monastery in Eger was made at a chapter meeting of Hungarian and Transylvanian Minorites in 1745. Having acquired the building plot in 1758, construction began soon thereafter. Guardian Román Jakabfalvy was the patron, and according to the *Historia Domus* the contractors included master masons Johann Falk and later Johann Nitsmann, and the foreman was Andreas Trethon. The carved stone footings of the church were the work of Joseph Hagen in 1759; but work appears to have stopped and started on the project: it is known that that a local master joiner, György Poleczky, stopped work on the roof because his day-labourers had not been paid. The Church was almost ready by 1767 but the foundation stone of the monastery was not laid until 1772. The roof structure (the work of master joiner Melchior Máhr) was not completed until 1777. Johann Povolni began building work on the vestry in 1781. The sculpted decorations of the façade were created by local sculptor “Öreg” (Old) János Hösz.  
Inside, the ceiling paintings were executed by Martin Reindl of Pozsony (Bratislava) between 1769 and 1770; and the main altarpiece holds a painting by the renowned local painter, Johann Lukas Kracker, of 1771.

partner: Eszterháza Centre for Culture, Research and Festivals

en.name: *Stigmata of St. Francis*
description: Central place in the lower part of the composition belongs to the unconscious saint and angels. Separated by light accents on the dark landscape the brother Leon, in the background, witnesses the stigmatisation. Among the clouds in the upper part of the composition a winged Seraphim carries the Crucified Jesus, followed by a group of angels.
place: The painting, made originally for the Altar of St. Frances in the church, is in the monastery corridor in the present day.

en.name: Tray stand
description:
This Mamluk bronze tray stand exemplifies the iconic shape, size and ornamentation characteristic of Mamluk metalwork, with a notable influence from China in the shape of the tray. Originally serving as a portable support for a food tray, it would have been accompanied by multiple table stands.  
Adorned with intricate *thuluth* inscriptions, geometric and floral motifs, and interrupted by cartouches, this stand is a testament to the exquisite craftsmanship of the Mamluk artisans. Distinctive Arabic inscriptions grace the upper and lower parts and the exposed section of the lower rim. Epigraphic analysis reveals that these inscriptions identity of the owner – a high-ranking official (Amir) in the Mamluk court hierarchy who belonged to the second-highest rank. The display of titles underscores the owner’s esteemed position and societal status. One of the inscriptions, “*Al-maqarr al-‘ali al-mawlawi al-amiri al-kabiri al-‘alimi al-‘adili al-ghazi al-mujahidi al-maliki al-nasiri*”, suggests that the owner is a follower of Al Sultan Al-Nasir. While many Mamluk sultans held the title Al-Nasir, it is unclear which one is referred to here. However, the decoration style indicates that it likely belongs to the period of Al-Nasir Muhammad bin Qalawun (1258–1341). Crafted from bronze, this tray stand displays intricate detail achieved through engraving and embossing. The *thuluth* inscriptions, geometric and floral motifs, and cartouches are meticulously executed, reflecting the skill and artistry of Mamluk metalworkers in Egypt during the 14th century.
holder: Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani Museum
His Excellency Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani
keywords: Bronze, Egypt, Mamaluk, Al Sultan Al-Nasir, Al-Nasir Muhammad bin Qalawun, China, Chinese
tags: Bronze, Egypt, Mamaluk, Al Sultan Al-Nasir, Al-Nasir Muhammad bin Qalawun, China, Chinese
partner: Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani Museum (FBQ Museums)

en.name: An Entertainment Scene (Evening entertainment in the Golden Horn) from *Surname-i Vehbi*
short_description: In this miniature we see an evening of rafts and fireworks on the Golden Horn. The grand vizier is seated on the Aynalıkavak quayside in the right frame and the sultan on the palace balcony. On the first of the two rafts in this procession, dancers and musicians perform in a garden of blazing cypress tree and Solomon’s seal fireworks. On the second is a revolving fortress stuffed with fireworks that have been set off while the military band at the stern of the raft plays.
keywords: Levni; miniature; entertainment; Dance

ar.name: قطعة من لوحة
description: ربما أتت هذه اللوحة من نوع من الشرفات. والقطع الأخرى من نفس الحاجز وجدت في العاصمة القديمة للدولة الغزنوية : غزنة. وكلها تظهر أشكالا مترابطة : مشاهد صيد ونساء يرقصن ومشاهد معارك أو منافسات وركوب حيوانات غريبة. وهذا التشكيل من الصور كان يشيع بشكل متزايد في بداية ومنتصف العصور الوسطى في العالم الإسلامي.

en.name: Panel fragment
description: The panel probably comes from a kind of balcony. Other pieces of the same parapet were found in the Ghaznavids’ old capital of Ghazna. All show related motifs: hunting scenes, dancing women, battle scenes or tournaments, and processions of exotic animals. This range of motifs was exceedingly popular in the early and medieval Islamic world.
keywords: Panel; Popular motifs in the early and modieval period; Ghaznavid; Marble; architectural element
tags: Popular motifs in the early and modieval period

en.name: Teatrino Aldrovandi Mazzacurati, Villa Aldrovandi-Mazzacurati, Bologna
description:
The theatre is composed of a small rectangular hall with two orders of boxes supported by 24 sinuous mermaids and caryatids moulded in stucco. All these figures are represented in different attitudes but they only have a decorative function and their elegant arms were used to hold fresh flower wreaths during gala's evenings.  
The statues were moulded by local artists, probably Camporesi or Balugani, following older models by the famous late Baroque Bolognese sculptor Angelo Piò.  
The motif of caryatids, mermaids or tritons mixed together well embodies the fantastic and illusive spirit of theatre and it was often used both in the ephemera and in the theatre decorations all over Europe.

It is one of the most charming surviving private theatres among the many that characterised the aristocracy residences, especially villas.  
Thanks to the presence of the famous architects Bibiena’s, Bologna became an important centre for theatre architecture and even its province was enriched by a lot of small elegant theatres, unfortunately most of them were completely restyled during the XIX century.
artist: Plan of the interior: Gianfrancesco Aldrovandi Marescotti; theatre machines engineer: *Master Bentivoglio*
history:
This small theatre is built inside a villa a few kilometres from Bologna. It was the country residence of the noble Aldrovandi family, later Aldrovandi-Marescotti.  
In 1761, the villa was completely restyled. The construction of the theatre played an important role in the renewing of the residence as the work was carried out according to a specific cultural programme. Although the architecture of the villa reflects the new neo-classical taste the theatre still follows the baroque tradition.  
The plan of this theatre was created by Marquis Gianfrancesco Aldrovandi Marescotti, who can also be considered its patron. It reflects his passion for theatrical representations and theatre literature, both typical of his age.  
The theatre was inaugurated the 24th of September 1763 with the representation of the *Alzira* by Voltaire. Marquis Gianfrancesco Aldrovandi Marescotti and his wife Lucrezia were among the actors, a common practice in private residence theatres. The play was repeated three times.  
At present the theatre is run by a cultural association that opens it to the public organising guided tours (Associazione Cultura e Arte del '700).

it.name: Teatro Aldrovandi Mazzacurati , Villa Aldrovandi-Mazzacurati, Bologna
description:
ll teatro è formato da una piccola hall rettangolare con due ordini di palchi sostenuti da 24 sinuouse sirene e cariatidi modellate in stucco. Tutte queste figure sono rappresentate in attitudini diverse ma hanno solo una funzione decorativa; le loro braccia eleganti erano usate per reggere ghirlande di fiori durante le serate di gala.  
Le statue furono scolpite da artisti locali, forse Camporesi o Balugani, che seguivano i modelli precedenti del celebre scultore tardo barocco bolognese Angelo Piò.  
Il motivo delle cariatidi, delle sirene o dei tritoni mescolati esprime bene lo spirito fantastico e illusivo del teatro ed era spesso usato negli apparati effimeri e nelle decorazioni teatrali in tutta Europa.

E' uno dei più affascinanti teatri privati giunti fino a noi tra i tanti che caratterizzavano le residenze aristocratiche, soprattutto le ville. Grazie alla presenza del celebre architetto Bibiena, Bologna divenne un importante centro per l'architettura teatrale e anche la provincia fu arricchita di tanti piccoli teatri, molti dei quali, sfortunatamente furono interamente ristrutturati del XIX secolo.
artist: Progetto dell'interno: Gianfrancesco Aldrovandi Marescotti; ingegnere delle macchine teatrali: Mastro Bentivoglio
history:
Questo piccolo teatro è costruito all'interno di una  villa, ad alcuni chilometri da Bologna. Era la residenza di campagna della nobile famiglia  Aldrovandi, più tardi  Aldrovandi-Marescotti.  
Nel 1761 la villa fu interamente ristrutturata e la costruzione del teatro giocò un ruolo importante nel rinnovamento della residenza secondo uno specifico programma culturale.  Anche se l'architettura della villa riflette il nuovo gusto neoclassico, il teatro segue ancora la tradizione barocca.  
Il progetto di questo teatro fu creato dal marchese Gianfrancesco Aldrovandi Marescotti, che può essere considerato anche il suo committente, e riflette la sua passione per le rappresentazioni teatrali e la letterartura di teatro, entrambe tipiche di questo periodo.  
Il teatro fu inaugurato il 24  settembre 1763, con la rappresentazione dell' *Alzira* di Voltaire. Il marchese Gianfrancesco Aldrovandi Marescotti e sua moglie Lucrezia furono tra gli attori, una pratica comune nei teatri delle dimore private. La rappresentazione fu replicata tre volte.  
Attualmente il teatro è gestito da una associazione culturale che lo apre al pubblico organizzando visite guidate  (*Associazione Cultura e arte del '700*).
keywords: Teatro; Villa; Aldrovandi; Aldrovandi-Marescotti; Voltaire; Alzira; Scultura barocca; Camporesi; Balugani; Angelo Gabriello Piò; sirena;

ar.name: مدرسة الفردوس.
description:
تعتبر مدرسة الفردوس أحد أعظم المجمعات الدينية التي تم إنشاؤها خلال الفترة الأيوبية، وقد كانت راعيتها امرأة أيوبية قوية هي ضيفة خاتون، ابنة أخ صلاح الدين، وزوجة ابنه الذي حكم حلب مستقلاً عن الدولة الأيوبية لمدة 20 عاماً. ولما كانت مقيمة في قلعة حلب، أرادت ضيفة خاتون أن يكون المجمع بمثابة ضريح ملكي، وزودته بتربة ومسجد ورباط لإقامة الصوفيين، ومدرسة لتعليم علوم الدين، وأوقفت له الكثير من الأملاك.  
تظهر العناية بالنسب والعلاقات الهندسية في أبعاد المبنى، إذ يتم الدخول عبر بوابة تنحرف عن محور الجدار الشرقي، وتفضي إلى ممر طويل يلتف يساراً نحو رواق الفسحة السماوية. البحرة في الفسحة السماوية مثمنة الشكل، لها حنيات ركنية في الزوايا الداخلية وفق الطراز السائد في الفترة الأيوبية. أما الأرضية المرصوفة بالحجر الكلسي والبازلتي على شكل خطوط وأشكال هندسية فقد تمت إعادة رصف أجزاء منها. يحد الفسحة السماوية من الشمال إيوان، وأروقة على الجهات الثلاث الأخرى، ويتألف كل رواق من ثلاث فتحات تفتح على قاعات مستطيلة لكل منها ثلاث قباب. الغرفتان الزاويتان مسقوفتان بقباب هي الأخرى، مما يجعل عدد القباب إحدى عشرة قبة حول الفسحة السماوية. تحوي الصالة الجنوبية منبراً ومحراباً مصنوعاً من الرخام المشقف، يعلوه عنصر نصف دائري، ضمن إيوان مركزي.  
تؤمن النوافذ العديدة ذات القضبان المعدنية المفتوحة ضمن جدران المدرسة كلها رؤية الحدائق المحيطة. ومن أبرز خواص المدرسة إيوانها الخارجي الشمالي، وهي ميزة غير معروفة على الإطلاق في المدارس السورية، ومن المرجح أنه كان له إطلالة رائعة على الحدائق كما يدل على ذلك اسم المدرسة "الفردوس" أي الجنة والحديقة، وهي جزء أساس من رمزية المبنى.  
تم نقش أطول كتابة عربية في العالم على الإطلاق حول كامل المحيط الداخلي للمبنى، ويصل طولها إلى 92م، وهي مكتوبة بالخط الثلث الأنيق والمقروء. يحمل الجدار الشرقي اسم الراعية ضيفة خاتون، أما الجدران الأخرى فتحمل كتابات دينية، ليست بآيات قرآنية كما درجت العادة على المباني الصرحية، ولكنها موزونة ومقفاة، وتحكي وصفاً مؤثراً لتجربة صوفية خلال العبادة.  
تظهر كتابة أخرى على الواجهة الشرقية الخارجية تركز على الهدف من المبنى، وتذكر الحدائق الواسعة، والكتابة تمتد إلى حوالي 40م، وتتضمن آيات من القرآن تصف الدخول إلى الفردوس، وتتابع وصف الشرف والتقوى والألقاب الملكية المؤنثة للراعية، كما تعطي تفاصيل عن إدارة المجمع وصيانته وواجبه تجاه الفقراء، كما تذكر اسم المشرف هو عبد المحسن، وتاريخ 633 (5-1236).

مدرسة الفردوس، وهو اسم من أسماء الجنة، وسُميت به لأن الجنة كانت من أهم المعاني للشخص الذي بناها، وهو حاكمة حلب "ضيفة خاتون"، في فترة منتصف القرن السابع هجرية/ القرن الثالث عشر ميلادية. بُنيت المدرسة توسُّلاً للحصول على التوازن، والتناسق، ومباركة الجنة، وكذلك التمتّع بالحدائق الآمنة والمطمئنة. أنشئت المدرسة لتشجيع التعليم الديني، والنمو الروحي، ليس فقط للعلماء والباحثين، بل أيضاً للمسافرين الذين لا يملكون بيتاً، والمتجولون التائهون. بالإضافة إلى عمارتها الرائعة، فإنها تحتوي على الزخارف والنقوش العربية، والتي تعتبر الأطول في العالم كله، والتي تبيِّن توجُّه صاحب المبنى، وكذلك دوره في مجال الإحسان.
dates: بدأ قبل عام 633 / 1235-6، وانتهى قبل عام 642/ 1240.
artist: ضيفة خاتون، سيدة حلب في الفترة 33-640/ 36-1242.

en.name: Madrasat al-Firdaws.
description:
Madrasat al-Firdaws is one of the greatest religious complexes to be erected during the Ayyubid period. Its patron was a powerful Ayyubid woman, Dayfah Khâtûn. She was Salah al-Din's niece and daughter-in-law who independently ruled Aleppo for nearly 20 years. As a resident of the Aleppo Citadel she intended that the complex be constructed as a royal mausoleum, endowing it with a *turbe*, a mosque, a *ribat* to house Sufis, a *madrasa* for religious education and an abundant *waqf* endowment.  
Careful attention to proportion and geometric relationships are evidenced in the dimensions of the building. Entered by an off-centre *muqarnas* portal on its eastern side, the entrance leads into a long corridor that turns left into the courtyard arcade. The courtyard basin is octagonal in shape with a curvilinear and bracketed inner outline that is typically Ayyubid in design. Portions of the courtyard floor decoration, linear and geometric patterns made of basalt and limestone, have been reconstructed. The courtyard is surrounded by an *iwan* on its northern side and an arcade along its other three sides. Each arcade includes three bays that open up to rectangular halls with three domes each. The two corner chambers are also domed, achieving a total of 11 domes around the courtyard. The southern hall, with its central bay includes the *minbar* and the *mihrab*, made of marble in-lay and capped by a semi-circular design.  
There are numerous grilled windows on all sides of the *madrasa* in order to ensure a view of the surrounding gardens. The most remarkable aspect of the *madrasa* is its exterior northern *iwan*, a highly unusual feature in Syrian *madrasa*s. It probably captured a very pleasing view of the gardens as the word “Firdaws”, means both “Paradise” and “Garden” and is clearly an important part of this building's symbolism.  
One of the longest continuous Arabic inscriptions in the world is carved along the entire periphery of the building's interior, measuring nearly 92 m. It is written in very elegant and clearly legible *thuluth* script. The eastern wall presents the patron Dayfah Khâtûn and the three other walls present religious inscriptions written in a rhyming meter. These do not relay typical Qur'anic verses usually found on monumental buildings. Rather, they offer compassionate descriptions of the Sufi experience of worship.  
Another monumental inscription is located on the eastern exterior façade, emphasising the intended view of the building as well as the expansive garden. The inscription extends to nearly 40 m and it includes Qur'anic verses describing entrance into Paradise and continues with descriptions of grace, piety and other feminine royal titles of the patron. It also gives details of the complex's administration and maintenance and its obligation to the poor. The name of the building's supervisor is mentioned: 'Abd al-Muhsin; and it is dated AH 633 (AD 1235–6).

The name of this *madrasa*, 'al-Firdaws', means Paradise and it was certainly the intention of its patron, the famous mid AH 7th- / AD 13th-century female ruler of Aleppo, Dayfah Khatun, to invoke balance, harmony, heavenly bliss and peaceful gardens. She built this *madrasa* to promote religious education and spiritual growth, not just for scholars, but also for homeless travellers and wandering mystics. In addition to its architectural poise, it contains important Arabic inscriptions – some of the longest in the world – relating the piety of the patron and the charitable purpose of the building.
dates: Begun before hegira 633 / AD 1235–6 and completed before AH 642 / AD 1240.
artist: Dayfah Khatun, Regent of Aleppo from AH 633-40/ AD 1236–42
keywords: Courtyard; garden; Paradise; female patronage; Sufi; mysticism; inscription; mihrab; Minbar; calligraphy; Thuluth script; Dayfah Khâtûn; Aleppo
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Museums and Antiquities

es.name: Madrasa de al-Firdaws.
description:
La madrasa de al-Firdaws es uno de los mayores complejos religiosos construidos en época ayyubí. Su patrocinadora fue una poderosa mujer ayyubí, Dayfah Jatun, sobrina y nuera de Salah al-Din, que gobernó Alepo de forma independiente durante casi veinte años. Residía en la ciudadela de Alepo e intentó otorgar al complejo la función de mausoleo real, por lo que lo dotó de un *türbe*, una mezquita, un *ribat* para albergar sufís, una madrasa para impartir educación religiosa y abundantes *waqf*.  
Las dimensiones del edificio demuestran un especial cuidado por la proporción y la relación geométrica. La entrada, enmarcada en el lado oriental en un portal descentrado con mocárabes, conduce a un largo pastillo a cuya izquierda se abre la arcada del patio. La pila del patio es octogonal y presenta un perfil interior mixtilíneo de diseño típicamente ayyubí. Se han reconstruido partes de la decoración del suelo del patio, de motivos lineales y geométricos en basalto y piedra caliza. En el lado norte del patio hay un *iwan*, mientras que por los demás lados corre una galería. Bajo la arcada de cada lado se abren salas cuadradas cubiertas todas con una cúpula. Las dos salas de las esquinas también están abovedadas, de forma que el patio está rodeado por once cúpulas en total. En la nave central de la sala sur se encuentran el *minbar* y el *mihrab*, decorado con mármol incrustado y abovedado.  
La madrasa tiene numerosas ventanas con celosías en todas las fachadas, desde las que se ven los jardines que la rodean. El componente más destacable de esta madrasa es el *iwan* externo del lado norte, un elemento inusual en las madrasas sirias. Posiblemente tenía unas amenas vistas a los jardines, ya que la palabra *firdaws* significa “paraíso” y “jardín”, parte importante de la simbología del edificio.  
El perímetro interior presenta una de las inscripciones continuas talladas más largas del mundo, de casi 92 m. Está escrita en letra *zuluz* muy elegante y legible. En el muro oriental se menciona a la patrocinadora, Dayfah Jatun, y en los tres restantes se leen inscripciones religiosas rimadas, aunque no se trata de los versículos del Corán que se encuentran normalmente en los edificios monumentales, sino de compasivas descripciones de la experiencia mística sufí.  
En la fachada oriental externa se aprecia otra inscripción monumental, que resalta la vista principal del edificio y su amplio jardín. Dicha inscripción mide 40 m y recoge versículos coránicos que describen la entrada al Paraíso, así como cualidades de la patrocinadora, como su gracia, su devoción y sus títulos reales. También da detalles de la administración y el mantenimiento del complejo, y su compromiso con los pobres. Se menciona el nombre del supervisor del edificio, Abd al-Muhsin, y su fecha de construcción, 633 / 1235-1256.

El nombre de esta madrasa, al-Firdaws, significa “paraíso”; su patrocinadora, la famosa Dhayfa Jatun (regente de Alepo a mediados del siglo VII / XIII), sin duda quiso evocar en ella el equilibrio, la armonía, el gozo celestial y tranquilos jardines. Construyó esta madrasa para promover la educación religiosa y el desarrollo espiritual no sólo de eruditos, sino también de viajeros sin hogar y místicos errantes. Además de su elegante arquitectura, posee importantes inscripciones –algunas de las más largas del mundo–, que mencionan la devoción de la patrocinadora y el fin caritativo del edificio.
dates: Se comenzó antes de 633 de la Hégira / 1235-36 d. C. y se terminó antes de 642 / 1240.
artist: Dayfah Jatun, regente de Alepo en 638-658 / 1242-1260.
keywords: patio; jardín; paraíso; patrocinio femenino; sufí; misticismo; inscripción; mihrab; minbar; caligrafía; escritura zuluz; Dayfah Jatun; Alepo.
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Museums and Antiquities

fr.name: Madrasa al-Firdaws.
description:
La *madrasa* al-Firdaws est l'un des plus prestigieux complexes religieux édifiés au cours de la période ayyoubide. Sa commanditaire était une femme de pouvoir, Dayfah Khatoun, nièce et belle-fille de Saladin, qui gouverna Alep en toute indépendance pendant près de 20 années. Résidant dans la citadelle, elle voulut que ce complexe fût également un mausolée royal et le dota d'un turbé, d'une mosquée, d'un *ribat* pour accueillir les soufis, d'une *madrasa* pour dispenser l'éducation religieuse, l'ensemble bénéficiant d'un important *waqf*.  
L'attention portée aux proportions et aux rapports géométriques est évidente. Signalée par un porche à *mouqarnas* décentré sur sa façade orientale, l'entrée conduit à un long corridor qui tourne à gauche puis débouche sous l'arcade de la cour. Le bassin octogonal de celle-ci est à margelle curviligne et à consoles typiquement ayyoubides. Des parties du décor du sol de la cour ornées de motifs géométriques en calcaire et basalte ont été reconstituées. La cour est entourée par un *iwan* au nord et une arcade sur les trois autres côtés. Chaque arcade comprend trois baies qui ouvrent sur des salles rectangulaires couvertes chacune de trois coupoles. Les deux salles d'angles sont également sous coupole. Onze dômes entourent ainsi la cour. La salle sud, à baie centrale, possède un *minbar* et un *mihrab* à marqueterie de marbre surmonté d'une voûte hémisphérique.  
De nombreuses fenêtres protégées par des grilles ouvrent sur tous les côtés pour offrir une vue des jardins qui entouraient le bâtiment. L'aspect le plus remarquable de ce complexe est son *iwan* extérieur au nord, disposition très originale pour une *madrasa* syrienne. Il bénéficiait sans doute d'une vue très agréable sur les jardins puisque le mot Firdaws signifie à la fois "paradis" et "jardin", ce qui en fait un élément important du symbolisme de ce bâtiment.  
L'une des inscriptions arabes continues les plus longues du monde est sculptée sur la totalité de la périphérie de l'intérieur du complexe. Mesurant près de 92 m de long, elle est rédigée dans une écriture *thoulouth* très élégante, et en même temps très lisible. Le mur oriental est consacré à la commanditaire, Dayfah Khatoun, et les trois autres murs à des inscriptions religieuses rimées. Ce ne sont pas les versets coraniques que l'on trouve habituellement, mais plutôt des descriptions de l'expérience mystique soufie.  
Une autre inscription monumentale figure sur le côté extérieur oriental de la façade, valorisant encore la vue du bâtiment et de son vaste jardin. Le texte, qui s'étend sur près de 40 mètres, comprend des versets du Coran décrivant l'entrée au Paradis et énumérant les qualités de grâce, de piété et les titres royaux de la commanditaire. Il fournit également des détails sur l'administration et l'entretien du complexe, ainsi que ses obligations envers les pauvres. Le nom du responsable des travaux, "Abd al-Moushin", est mentionné ainsi qu'une date, 633 (1236 J.-C.).

Le nom de cette *madrasa,* al-Firdaws, signifie “Paradis”. L'intention de son mécène, la fameuse souveraine d'Alep du milieu du VIIe s. H (XIIIe s. J.-C.), Dayfah Khatoun, était certainement d'évoquer l'équilibre, l'harmonie et la félicité paradisiaques dans ses paisibles jardins. Elle édifia cette *madrasa* pour promouvoir l'éducation religieuse et l'élévation spirituelle non seulement chez les étudiants, mais aussi auprès des voyageurs sans foyer et des mystiques nomades. Outre sa splendeur architecturale, elle contient d'importantes inscriptions arabes – certaines sont les plus longues du monde – sur la piété de sa commanditaire et les fonctions charitables de l'édifice.
dates: La construction a commencé avant l'an 633 de l'Hégire / 1236 J.-C. et a été achevée avant 642 H / 1240 J.-C.
artist: Dayfah Khatoun, régente d'Alep de 633 à 640 H / 1236-1242 J.-C.
keywords: Cours ; jardins ; paradis ; femmes commanditaires ; soufisme ; mysticisme ; inscriptions, mihrab ; minbar ; calligraphie ; écriture thoulouth ; Dayfar Khatun ; Alep.
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Museums and Antiquities

*Pietà*
description:
With a preference for sculpture of enormous dimensions that entirely occupy the grand gilded altarpieces of the period, Frei Cipriano da Cruz is considered to be the most extraordinary representative of the National Baroque style.  
His sculpture was generally based on models that circulated throughout Europe and can be considered within the context of other depictions of the Crucifixion and Passion of Christ. A monk-sculptor, the *Pietà* is one of Frei Cipriano's greatest achievements. It exemplifies a theme widespread in Portuguese art in the 16th and 17th centuries, meeting most of the essential Tridentine ideals.  
The *Pietà* belongs to an ensemble of pieces made by Frei Cipriano for the S. Bento Church, which belonged to the college of the Benedictine order in Coimbra and was demolished in 1932.  
This ensemble features anatomical details that are typical of Frei Cipriano, in particular the hands and faces. In the *Pietà* Christ's hands are rough with square-shaped finger nails. His face is framed by abundant curly hair; the S-shaped curls are also present in the beard. The Virgin displays a heavy look; she has high symmetrical eyebrows, a long triangular-shaped nose, and thin defined lips.  
The heavy and pyramidal structure of the *Pietà* is accentuated by the drapery: the red, blue and gold cloak that completely wraps the figure. The drapery is notable in that its decorative motifs correspond with textiles of the period – elaborate brocades and oriental silks. The drapery and embroidery, generally designated as “upholstery”, were pre-made in resin-wax and were applied to the figure later after painting and finishing.  
The motif of the artichoke particularly stands out. It imitates the three-bordered brocade of Spanish and Italian origin and is strategically placed on the Virgin's knee to have the greatest visual impact.  
According to recent research (Alcoforado and Le Gac, 2003) Manuel da Costa Pereira, who was responsible for painting and gilding the *Pietà*, often worked with other painters. Further research about them will bring us closer to understanding the originality of Frei Cipriano da Cruz's sculpture.

With a preference for sculpture of enormous dimensions that entirely occupy the grand gilded altarpieces of the period, Frei Cipriano da Cruz is considered to be the most extraordinary representative of the National Baroque style. The Pietà represents one of his greatest achievements.

pt.name: *Pietà*
description:
A preferência por esculpir imagens de grandes dimensões, para ocuparem retábulos imponentes, inteiramente dourados, revela Frei Cipriano da Cruz como o mais notável monge-escultor português e um dos melhores representantes da escultura barroca nacional.  
Baseada em modelos que circulavam por toda a Europa, e integrada no contexto da Crucificação e Morte de Cristo, a *Pietà* é uma das suas melhores realizações. Representa um tema amplamente difundido a partir do século XVI e bastante explorado na arte portuguesa de seiscentos, que revela o essencial do pensamento tridentino.  
Faz parte do conjunto de obras que o monge realizou para decorar a igreja do colégio da sua Ordem, em Coimbra, a Igreja de S. Bento, demolida em 1932.  
Este conjunto escultórico apresenta pormenores anatómicos característicos do escultor, essencialmente nas mãos e nos rostos – mãos grosseiras com unhas quadradas, rostos marcados por cabelos e barbas fartos e encaracolados em SS, no caso de Cristo, e na Virgem, o olhar pesado, as sobrancelhas altas e simétricas, o nariz comprido e triangular, os lábios pequenos, finos e bem definidos.  
A composição, maciça e de estrutura piramidal, é marcada pelos largos panejamentos, em tons de vermelho, azul e ouro, com destaque para o manto, que constitui um dos maiores interesses da obra, dado que apresenta motivos decorativos que reproduzem os têxteis da época – ricos brocados ou sedas orientais, geralmente designados por “estofado”. Destaca-se o motivo da alcachofra, imitando o brocado de três altos, de origem italiana ou espanhola, colocado estrategicamente no joelho da Virgem e na parte superior do manto, zonas de maior impacto visual para o observador. Os bordados eram pré-elaborados, em cera-resina, e aplicados após a realização da policromia das superfícies.  
Esta obra foi recentemente atribuída a Manuel da Costa Pereira, num estudo (Alcoforado, A. e Le Gac, A., 2003) que aponta as características comuns e inconfundíveis da produção do escultor, identificando igualmente os pintores que trabalharam naquela empreitada.

Esta *Pietà* foi concebida à escala da estrutura arquitectónica em que se inseria. Tendo como fundo os elementos tradicionais da Descida da Cruz, bem como construções alusivas a Jerusalém, facilmente deduzimos que a Cruz teria proporções imponentes e a visão do conjunto seria cenograficamente monumental.
type: Conjunto escultórico pertencente a estrutura retabular.
holder: Museu Nacional de Machado de Castro

place: Igreja e Colégio de S. Bento, Coimbra.
artist: Frei Cipriano da Cruz (escultor) (1645?, Braga–1716, Braga); Manuel da Costa Pereira (pintor e dourador).
keywords: Conjunto escultórico; estrutura retabular; panejamentos; estofado; brocado de três altos; policromia / repolicromia; Coimbra; Museu Machado de Castro.

de.name: Hauptfresko
description: Die Langhausfresken der Klosterkirche zeigen typologisch miteinander verwoben das Leben des Ordensgründers Bernhard von Clairvaux und dasjenige Christi anhand der Hochfeste des Kirchenjahres von West nach Ost, um damit eine sinnvolle Position der Zisterzienser innerhalb des göttlichen Heilsplanes zu reklamieren: Die Geburt Christi und die Vision derselben durch den hl. Bernhard, die Auferstehung mit dessen Predigt vor dem Herzog von Aquitanien, die Himmelfahrt mit dem Eintritt des Heiligen in das Kloster Citeaux sowie die Aussendung des Hl. Geistes mit den Visionen Bernhards vom Gekreuzigten und von Maria.

en.name: Main fresco
description: The nave frescos of the monastery church are typologically woven into one another, depicting the life of the founder of the Cistercian Order, Bernhard of Clairvaux, and likewise, the Life of Christ. Using the solemnity of the church year from west to east the position of the Cistercians within God’s divine plan for salvation is accented: the Birth of Christ and Saint Bernhard’s vision of it; the Resurrection with its sermon for the Duke of Aquitaine; the Ascent to Heaven with the entrance of the saint into the Citeaux Monastery as well as the despatch of the Holy Ghost with Bernhard’s visions of Christ Crucified and the Virgin Mary.
partner: University of Munich, Institute of Art History
