en.name: Oasis of Madkhal Meski
description: The subject of this image is 'The Blue Source' in the oasis of (Madkhal) Meski, near Er-Rachidia, in Morocco, distinguished by its expansive body of water encompassed by palm trees. This oasis is a paradigm of the urban landscape in desert regions, where water functions as a nexus for communities and urban life. It is enveloped by residential dwellings and commercial establishments.
keywords: Water; Oasis; Madkhal Meski; Morocco.

ar.name: قنديل مسجد.
description: قنديل مسجد من الزجاج المذهب المطعم بالمينا ذو عنق قمعي الشكل، وشفة مستديرة، وجسم مربع، وكتف منحدر، وساق طويلة تنتهي بقاعدة مسطحة تحمل علامة مميزة في الأسفل، وقد تم تزويد الجسم بست حلقات للتعليق على مسافات مساوية. القنديل مزين بشكل كامل بالمينا المذهبة المنفذة باللون الأحمر والأزرق والأخضر الفاتح. يدور حول العنق شريط ذو حدود بزخارف زهرية، مؤلف من نقش منفذ بالمينا الزرقاء بالخط الثلث. النقش هو الآية 256 من سورة البقرة، تقطعها حليات دائرية ملونة بالذهبي والأحمر والأخضر، وتتضمن كل منها كأساً صغيرة في المركز. لقد تم تزيين الجزء الأسفل من العنق والجزء الأعلى من الجسم بأشرطة زهرية تقطعها حليات ذات زخارف زهرية أحادية، وعلى القسم الرئيس من الجسم،يظهر نقش آخر بالخط الثلث يتضمن ألقاب الضابط الذي أمر بصنع القنديل زين الدين مبارك الذي كان، كما يدل عليه الشعار في الأعلى، حامل كأس السلطان الملك الصالح الذي ذكر اسمه هو الآخر. حمل هذا الاسم حاكمان كانا ابني ناصر الدين محمد بن قلاوون، الأول هو الملك الصالح إسماعيل الذي حكم في الفترة 742-45/ 1342-45، والثاني الملك الصالح صالح الذي حكم في الفترة 751-4/ 1135-4.

كانت مصابيح المساجد الزجاجية المُطعَّمة بالزخارف، تُصنَّع بأعداد كبيرة، تلبيةً لطلبات النخب المملوكية، في مصر وسورية. وقد كانت، وهي المُزيِّنة بنقوش قرآنية، وألقاب أولياء النعمة، تُخصَّص للأعداد الكبيرة من المساجد، والمدارس الموقوفة من قبل المماليك، في أرجاء القاهرة، كما في طول البلاد وعرضها.
holder: المتحف الملكي، المتحف الوطني في اسكتلندا NMS.
keywords: خط ثلث؛ زجاج مطعم.

en.name: Mosque lamp.
description: An enamelled glass and gilt mosque lamp with a wide funnel-shaped neck and a rounded rim. The lamp has a squat body, steeply sloping shoulder and a flattened base, and a tall pedestal foot with a pronounced pontil mark on the underside. Six trailed suspension loops are placed around the body at regular intervals. The lamp is decorated comprehensively with enamel decoration executed in red, blue and light-green, embellished with gilding. Around the neck is a wide band of *thuluth* script executed in blue enamel, surrounded by a floral border. An excerpt from the Qur’an (*Sura* 2; verse 256), the inscription is interrupted by decorative roundels rendered in gold, red and green, each of which contain a little cup in the centre. The lower neck and upper body are decorated with floral bands interrupted by roundels with individual floral motifs. On the main body, another inscription in *thuluth* script gives the titles of the official who commissioned the lamp: Zain al-Din Mubarak who, according to the blazon above, was cupbearer to the sultan, al-Malik al-Salih, who is also named in the inscription. There were two rulers with the same titulature, both of whom were the sons of Nasir Nasir al-Din Muhammad ibn Qalawun: the first, al-Malik al-Salih Isma’il (r. AH 742–5 / AD 1342–5); the second, al-Malik al-Salih Salih (r. AH 751–4 / AD 1351–4).

Glass mosque lamps with enamelled decoration were commissioned in large numbers by the Mamluk elite in Egypt and Syria. Decorated with Qur’anic inscriptions and the titles of the patron, they were destined for the numerous mosques and *madrasas* endowed by the Mamluks throughout Cairo and the empire.
keywords: Thuluth; mosque lamp; enamelled glass; Zayn al-din Mubarak; al-Malik al-Salih Isma’il; al-Malik al-Salih Salih; Mosque interior decoration; calligraphy; emblems; blazons; coat of arms

es.name: Lámpara de mezquita
description: Lámpara de mezquita en vidrio esmaltado y dorado con cuello en forma de embudo y boca redonda, cuerpo achatado, hombro pronunciado y pie alto con marca del puntil en su parte interna. Tiene siete asas para colgarla dispuestas a intervalos regulares en la parte central del cuerpo. Está profusamente decorada con esmaltes rojo, azul y verde claro, embellecidos con el dorado. Ocupa el cuello una ancha banda epigráfica en caligrafía *zuluz* (Corán 2, 256) esmaltada en azul y enmarcada por bandas de motivos florales; está interrumpida por círculos concéntrico en oro, verde y rojo, con una pequeña copa en el centro. La parte superior del hombro y el arranque del cuello están decorados con bandas de motivos florales y medallones que encierran flores también. Otra inscripción *zuluz* llena la parte más ancha del cuerpo, y en ella se leen los nombres de quien mandó hacer la lámpara, Zain al-Din Mubarak, que, según el blasón, era copero del sultán al-Malik al-Salih, también mencionado en la inscripción. Hubo dos gobernantes con el mismo título, ambos hijos de Nasir Nasir al-Din Muhammad ibn Qalawun: al-Malik al-Salih Ismail (r. 742–45 / 1342–45) y al-Malik al-Salih Salih (751–54 / 1351–54).

La élite mameluca de Egipto y Siria encargaba muchas lámparas de mezquita como esta, de vidrio esmaltado. Se decoraban con inscripciones del Corán y los títulos de quien la encomendaba y se destinaban a las numerosas mezquitas y *madrasas* que los mamelucos construyeron en El Cairo y el resto del imperio.
keywords: escritura zuluz; lámpara de mezquita; vidrio esmaltado; Zayn al-din Mubarak; al-Malik al-Salih Ismail; al-Malik al-Salih Salih

fr.name: Lampe de mosquée.
description: Lampe de mosquée en verre émaillé et doré à large col en entonnoir et rebord adouci. Elle présente un corps ramassé, une épaule fortement incurvée et une base aplatie sur haut piédouche à pontil prononcé sous le pied. Six anneaux de suspension sont disposés autour de la panse à intervalles réguliers. La lampe est entièrement ornée d'un décor émaillé en rouge, bleu et vert pâle, rehaussé de dorures. Autour du col, un large bandeau en écriture de style *thoulouth* en émail bleu est entouré d'une bordure florale. Un extrait du Coran (sourate II, verset 256) est rythmé par des rondeaux or, rouge et vert, chacun contenant en son centre une petite coupe. Le bas du col et le haut de la panse sont décorés de bandeaux floraux interrompus par des rosettes à motifs floraux. Sur la panse, une seconde inscription en écriture *thoulouth* donne les titres du haut personnage commanditaire de l'objet : Zayn al-Din Moubarak qui, selon le blason mentionné plus haut, était échanson auprès du sultan al-Malik al-Salih, également nommé dans l'inscription. Deux autres souverains portent le même titre, tous deux fils de al-Nasir Nasir al-Din Muhammad ibn Qalawun : le premier, al-Malik al-Salih Isma'il (r. 742-745 H / 1342-1345 J.-C.), le second, al-Malik al-Salih Salih (r. 751-754 H / 1351-1354 J.-C.).

Les lampes de mosquée en verre émaillé étaient commanditées en grand nombre par l’élite mamelouke d’Égypte et de Syrie. Ornées d’inscriptions coraniques et des titulatures de leurs donateurs, elles étaient destinées aux nombreuses mosquées et *madrasa* fondées par les Mamelouks à travers Le Caire et l’empire.
keywords: écriture thoulouth ; lampe de mosquée ; verre émaillé ; Zayn al-Din Moubarak ; al-Malik al-Salih Isma’il ; al-Malik al-Salih Salih

The church was meant to house the tombs of the Luxembourg dynasty, but only Jan Jindřich and his son, Jošt, are buried here; their statues flank the entrance to the prefecture. It is the only five-axis palace portal in Moravia.

en.name: Noudar Castle
description:
At the start of Islamic presence in the Iberian Peninsula, Noudar, which was situated at the limits of the *cora* of Beja, would have been little more than a small settlement. Towards the end of the 4th/10th and the beginning of the 5th/11th century, it strengthened its defences by building a humble *hisn* or *burj* made of dried mud. Some remains of this wall are still visible in the area around the castle’s citadel, although largely concealed by the schist wall built in the 14th century.  
Overlooking the road that connected the region of Beja and Moura to the old “Silver Route” through Jerez de los Caballeros, the castle served as a watchtower. This function was suggested by its location and by the synonym of the place’s actual name (the Arabic word *nadara* means “to see” or “to watch”). The fortified structure stood at the highest point of an extensive rocky outcrop between the Múrtega and Ardila Rivers, where previously there had been a small early Christian basilica, whilst the residential quarter spread around the whole of the hillside except the southern slope.  
Several artefacts that originate from here suggest the strategic importance of the area. For instance, the two tombstones bearing Arabic writing, a collection of 5th/11th-century silver coins, a tip of a dagger sheath and a large collection of 7th/13th-century ceramics. Evidently this was an important site in a territory that borders on the district of Badajoz, whose uninterrupted occupation only came to an end in the mid-19th century.  
Conquered in the first half of the 7th/13th century, Noudar was given to the Order of Avis, which built the present-day walled fortress with an enclosed area of roughly 12,000 sq. m. The town received a charter in 1295 from D. Dinis and in 1308 it became the first refuge for fugitives in Portugal.

es.name: Castillo
description:
Noudar, en el límite de la cora de Beja, sería un pequeño pueblo en los inicios de la presencia musulmana en la Península Ibérica. A fines del siglo IV/f. X y principios del V/p. XI, su defensa se reforzó con la construcción de un humilde *hisn* o un *borsh* en *tapial*. Por lo demás, quedan aún restos visibles en la zona de la *alcazaba* del castillo, a pesar de que fueron revestidos con la muralla de pizarra del siglo XIV.  
Dominando la vía que unía la región de Beja y Moura con la antigua Vía de la Plata pasando por Jerez de los Caballeros, el castillo cumplía las funciones de atalaya, según indican su localización y el nombre del lugar, que significa “mirar, ver” (ár. *nadara*). La estructura fortificada se alzaba en la parte más alta de un gran espolón rocoso entre las riberas del Múrtega y el Ardila, donde antes habría una pequeña basílica paleocristiana, mientras que el arrabal de viviendas rodeaba toda la cima del cerro, salvo la vertiente sur.  
Las dos lápidas funerarias con caracteres árabes y la colección de monedas de plata del siglo V/XI y, ya de los siglos VII/XIII, la punta de vaina de daga y la extensa colección de cerámica que de aquí provienen sugieren que se trata de un lugar importante en este territorio de frontera con el término de Badajoz, ocupado de forma ininterrumpida hasta mediados del siglo XIX.  
Conquistado en la primera mitad del siglo VII/p.m. XIII, el pueblo de Noudar fue donado a la Orden de Avís, que creó la actual fortaleza amurallada de 12.000 m2 de superficie. En 1295, D. Dinis otorgó a la villa sus fueros y, en 1308, se convirtió en el primer *Couto de Homiziados* (refugio de fugitivos) de Portugal.

en.name: Hat (*Cuculj*)
names: Bridal ornament worn on the head
short_description: In the 19th century and the beginning of the 20th century, metal jewellery and other articles of adornment in Macedonia were made by goldsmiths. They were distinguished with exceptional diversity reflecting the skill and creativity of artisans. This versatility applies particularly to headdresses. The bridal hat is made of broadcloth – *klashna* – which is decorated with small silver coins reminiscent of fish scales. This particular headdress is part of a jewellery set that goes with a piece worn on the breasts, which was called *mingjuska so vot*.
keywords: Headdress; coin; coinage; currency; numismatics; marriage; wedding; costume; textile; fashion
materials: Klashna – thick woollen fabric, silver coins, silver alloy. Silversmith's production

en.name: Aş Evi (Bektashi Kitchen)
description:
The most significant part of the Hacı Bektaş Velî Dervish lodge is the Aş Evi (kitchen), which is accessed via a large door with two wings. After traversing two corridors, one reaches the location of the main Aş Evi. On the right side of the first corridor is the grave of the father of the Ash House, which is marked by an inscription dated 1560 on the door of the second corridor. To the right of this corridor is a window that opens to the room of the Father of the House, while to the left is the Pantry Room, where meat is cooled.  
The main hall of the house is entered through an arched doorway and is divided into two parts by a large arch based on the north and south walls. In the centre of the hall is the stone where meat was chopped and fat was drained. On the south, north and east walls there are six large and small hearths where food was cooked.

en.name: House
short_description: The construction trade has an exceptionally long tradition in the Reka Area. The artisan school in the Debar-Reka area, with its centre in Galichnik, was mentioned in sources from as early as the 10th century. People from this area – the Miyaks – have given birth to numerous generations of construction masters throughout the centuries. Construction *tajfas* from the Reka Area were widely known and used to build houses, churches, mosques and other structures throughout the Balkans, even in Asia Minor. This three-storey house was built completely of stone. It is the type of tower house of asymmetrical lay out distinctive to the Reka Area. Construction of tower houses developed in this area for the purpose of defence and protection from intruders in the turbulent times of the 18th and 19th centuries.
dates: End of 19th – beginning of the 20th century
history: *Tajfas* were very well organized and had extremely professional approach to their work. These construction masters developed a secret construction language which they used for communication among themselves. There were even variants of the secret construction language, depending on the local dialects and the origin of the members of the *tajfa*. The best known artists of the woodcarving craft in Macedonia came from the Reka Area, including Makarija Frchkovski, Petre Filipovski Garkata and his brother Marko Filipovski – as well as many others.
keywords: secret construction language

en.name: National Museum of Machado de Castro
description:
The Museum is installed in the old Episcopal Palace, which in turn rests on a large, imposing Roman *cryptoporticus*. This artificial platform was used in the 12th century for the building of the Church of São João de Almedina, with its respective cloisters and annexes. The last work was carried out at the end of the 16th century, and the portico and courtyard with its large terrace overlooking the river, still exist from this time. The Museum contains a comprehensive collection dating from the High Middle Ages up to the present day.  
One of the most important sections is that consisting of the Treasury of the Cathedral, which dates back to the 12th century and has been progressively enriched by valuable items. A very fine example of the Late Gothic, typical of the Manueline period, is to be seen in the superb, silver-gilt monstrance donated to the Cathedral by D. Jorge de Almeida in 1527. Its structure is reminiscent of a Manueline edifice with three registers, set on a broad base supported by lions. A legend around the base refers to its donation and it also bears the coat of arms of the bishop-count. The wafer box is in the shape of a small temple, and the Host can be seen through a very fine grid.  
Among a number of silver-gilt chalices are fine examples from the Monastery of Santa Clara, and the Treasury of D. Catarina de Eça, Abbess of Lorvão.  
The collection contains important 16th-century Portuguese and imported paintings, a number from the most traditionalist workshop in the Manueline period, probably situated in Coimbra. From the *Assumption of the Virgin*, *St Bartholomew* and the six panels from the Monastery of Celas *polyptych*, it is possible to pick out characteristics that define all the workshop’s production.  
Despite the superior quality of some of the paintings, as in the case of the *Assumption of the Virgin*, the arrangement of figures tends to be rigid. There is difficulty with composition; faces are simplified and repetitive with little character, while the anatomical structure of the figures is deficient, with recourse to traditional angular folds of drapery. The superb treatment of brocade, ornamented with precious stones and pieces of jewellery, must be highlighted, however, in a finely detailed work of great density. It seems to be the result of a traditionalist concept of painting, conceived as a materially valuable object.  
What is today called the “Masters of Coimbra” corresponds to the former designation the “School of the Master of Sardoal”, a name derived from the fact that the Parish Church there contained a valuable group of paintings, the origin of all the surviving school’s production, some 40 in all. It seems likely that Vicente Gil, painter to D. João II, active in Coimbra between 1498 and 1525, and his son Manuel Vicente, who worked in the city from 1521 to 1530, headed a workshop operating in this region.  
The museum also contains an admirable collection of sculpture including works by the master, Oliver of Ghent (Olivier de Gand) and those within his circle. Sculptures such as *St Barbara*, *St Jerome* and *St Gregory*, although miniature and belonging to the imposing altarpiece in the old Cathedral, the Sé Velha, are highly representative of his aesthetic. A monumental *Prophet* although incomplete, *Our Lady* and *St John*, as well as a remarkable *St Matthew* from the Parish Church in Botão, are other examples of this Flemish master’s influence on the Coimbra area. The magnificent *Nativity* altarpiece is representative of the large number of sculptural works imported from Northern Europe in Manueline times. The quality of the retable, in carved polychrome wood, indicates that it came from one of the most important workshops in Antwerp at the beginning of the 16th century.

ar.name: طبق كبير.
description: طبق عريض مسطح وملون تحت التزجيج مزين بزخارف بالأسود والأزرق. تتألف الزخارف من فروع ملتفة من الأرابيسك والنماذج المتموجة المتعرجة، وهي تشكيلات متميزة للأرابيسك التقليدي (الرومي) والصيني (الحتاي)، وقد أعطيت هذه النماذج اسم الرومي-الحتاي، ويميز هذا الطراز المرحلة المبكرة من الخزف الإزنيقي، عندما كان الخزافون يبتدعون نماذجهم الزخرفية باستلهام الفنون الإيرانية والصينية، والأعمال المعدنية العثمانية المعاصرة وزخارف المخطوطات وغيرها. لقد تم ترك الجزء الواصل بين الحافة والقعر فارغاً مما خلق منطقة انتقالية أبرزت زخارف الحافة.

صحن عريض، مُسطَّح، مُصمَّم بما يشبه تصميم الطبق، مُزخرف بنقوش أرابيسك، كروية الشكل، وزخارف نباتية، ومناظر لغيوم متلاصقة. يعود هذا الطراز إلى أوائل صناعة فخار إزنيق، حيث كان الصانعون يستوحون الزخارف من الفنون الإيرانية والصينية.
keywords: زخرفة زهرية.

en.name: Dish (charger).
description: A wide flat dish in a form known as a charger, with decoration painted under the glaze in black and blue. The decorative motifs, which include scrolling arabesque stems and sinuous cloud motifs, are a distinctive combination of traditional arabesque (*rumi*) and Chinese (*hatayi*) styles, so this style has been dubbed *rumi-hatayi*. This style characterises the early phase of Iznik ceramics, when the potters were forging their own decorative idiom out of influences from Iranian and Chinese art, contemporary Ottoman metalwork and manuscript illumination, and others. The *cavetto*, or curve of the dish between the rim and the bottom, has been left blank, creating a zone of transition which sets off the decoration of the rim.

A wide flat dish in a form known as a charger, decorated with scrolling arabesques, floral motifs and cloud-bands. This style characterises the early phase of Iznik ceramics, when the potters were forging their own decorative idiom out of influences including Iranian and Chinese art.
keywords: floral decoration

es.name: Fuente
description: Fuente llana con decoración pintada en negro y azul bajo vidriado. Los motivos decorativos incluyen tallos enroscados formando arabescos tradicionales *(rumi)* y sinuosas nubes tomadas del arte chino *(hatayi)*, en un estilo que se ha denominado *rumi-hatayi*. Este estilo caracterizó la primera fase de las cerámicas de Iznik, cuando los alfareros trataban de forjar su propio estilo a partir del arte iraní y el chino, y de la metalistería contemporánea y las iluminaciones de los manuscritos otomanas. El galbo –la curva entre el vuelo y el fondo del plato– se dejó sin decorar, como zona de transición que hace resaltar la ornamentación del vuelo.

Fuente decorada con arabescos, motivos florales y nubes. Este estilo caracterizó la primera etapa de las cerámicas de Iznik, cuando los alfareros trataban de forjar su propio estilo a partir de sus influencias, entre ellas la del arte iraní y la del chino.
dates: Alrededor del año 916 de la Hégira / 1510 d. C.
keywords: decoración floral

fr.name: Plat de service.
description: Grand plat de service de forme plate, à décor noir et bleu peint sous glaçure. Les tiges en volutes d'arabesques et de rubans de nuages sinueux combinent clairement les styles traditionnels d'arabesques (*rumi*) et chinois (*hatayi*). Ce style, que l'on appelle donc *rumi-hatayi*, caractérise la première phase du développement des céramiques d'Iznik, lorsque les potiers de ce centre se forgeaient leur propre vocabulaire décoratif à partir d'influences, entre autres, de l'art iranien et chinois, du travail du métal ottoman de l'époque et d'enluminures de manuscrits. Le marli – entre l'aile et le fond du bassin – laissé en blanc crée une zone de transition qui met en valeur le décor de l'aile.

Grand plat de service de forme plate orné de volutes d'arabesques, de motifs floraux et de rubans de nuages. Ce style caractérise la première phase des céramiques d'Iznik, lorsque les artisans se forgeaient leur propre vocabulaire décoratif à partir notamment d'influences de l'art iranien et chinois.
keywords: Décoration florale

ar.name: وعاء نحاسي مُطعم بالذهب والفضة
description: يُمثل هذا الوعاء الأنيق الأعمال المعدنية العالية الجودة التي أُنتجت في العراق بعد تأسيس الحكم المغولي. ويُظهر ستة أشكال دائرية تصور فرسانًا متوَّجين، حيث استُلهم تصميمها من فن الرسم المصغر المعاصر لها. وهي منظمة في نسق تبادلي مع خراطيش زخرفية كبيرة تُظهر نقوشًا خيالية على طراز خط الثلث.
dates: القرن الثامن الهجري/ القرن الرابع عشر الميلادي

en.name: Gold- and silver-inlaid brass bowl
description: This elegant bowl exemplifies the high-quality metalwork produced in Iraq and Iran after the establishment of Mongol rule. It shows six roundels showing crowned horse riders, their style influenced by contemporary miniature painting. These alternate with large cartouches which appear to show pseudo-inscriptions in a *thuluth* style.
keywords: Bowl; thuluth; gold; silver; metalwork; inlay; pseudo inscriptions; calligraphy; human representation

en.name: Rome Exhibition 1911 (Piazza d'Armi) – Sicilian Pavilion
short_description: Within the International Exhibition of Rome in 1911 and related to the celebrations for the 50th anniversary of the Unification of Italy, a "Forum of Regions" was arranged in the Piazza d’Armi. The architect Ernesto Basile (1857–1932), author of the project for the Sicilian Pavilion, took inspiration from the Arab-Norman architecture in Sicily, in particular from Zisa Palace, the church of Saint John of the Hermits and the Cathedral of Monreale. On the outside, the building looked like a cube with plain walls decorated with blind pointed arches and battlements on top. Doors and windows show pointed arch as well. At the sides of the facades two small towers topped by a small small dome give to the palace a striking oriental look. On the inside, there was an open space with columns topped by capitals, walls decorated with mosaics and majolicas, and fountains.
holder: Central Institute for Ethno-Anthropology, National Museum of Arts and Popular Traditions
keywords: Universal exposition; Esposizione universale di Roma; exhibition building; exhibitions and urban spaces; model; reproduction; Modernism; Art Nouveau; Moorish style; Norman; San Giovanni degli Eremiti; Islamic art; Islamic influence; applied arts
partner: MIBACT | Central Institute for Ethno-Anthropology, National Museum of Arts and Popular Traditions

ar.name: مرشِّح لجرَّة ماء.
description: مرشِّح لجرَّة ماء، مصنوع من الطين، مخرَّم على شكل زخرفة كتابية بخط عربي. ومنشأ هذه القطعة هو الفسطاط، العاصمة القديمة لمصر. كان المرشَّح عبارة عن سدادة توضع على فوهة جرَّة ماء صغيرة بلا قبضة؛ وتنبع وظيفته من دوره كغطاء لحماية محتويات الجرَّة من الذباب والحشرات والغبار على سبيل المثال. كما أن الجرَّة والمرشَّح غير مزجَّجين، وذلك بغية السماح للماء بالتبخُّر عبر مسامات الجرَّة ببطء، مما يساعد على إبقاء الماء بارداً فيها. أما الخطوط المخرَّمة التي تخترق سطح المرشِّح وقاعدته فهي تكرار لحرفي الألف ( ا ) واللام ( ل). وقد كُتبت هنا بخط كوفي تيمُّناً بمدينة الكوفة في العراق. ونمط الخط الكوفي يتميز بأشكاله الهندسية وزخارفه المُضافة إلى الاستطالات الأخيرة لأذيال الكلمات ( أنظر إلى الأطراف العمودية المستدقة للأحرف في الصورة). لم يكن خط اليد هو الوسيلة الوحيدة للزخرفة المستخدمة في تزيين الأواني، فقد استخدمت أيضاً الحيوانات والرسوم الهندسية والنقوش الوردية؛ حتى أنه لم يتكشَّف عن ظهور آنيتين متطابقتين تماماً، على الرغم من الاستخدام المتكرر لحيوانات مثل الفيلة والأرانب الوحشية والطيور.

جرى توظيف الخطّ العربي لزخرفة العديد من الأشياء في العالم الإسلامي، بدءاً بالأشياء العادية اليومية، مثل مصفاة جرّة الماء الفاطمية هذه، وانتهاءً بحاجات خاصة، مثل تلك الموجودة على الأواني المعدنية المُرصَّعة. ومثل هذه المصافي كانت مزينة إفرادياً، إذ لم يتمَّ العثور على اثنتين متطابقتين.
holder: متحف وصالة فنون كيلفينغروف، متاحف غلاسكو.
dates: القرن الرابع- الخامس / العاشر- الحادي عشر.
keywords: آنية فخارية منزلية؛ زخرفة كتابية؛ ماء.
materials: قطعة فخارية غير مزجَّجة؛ مدوَّرة ومخرَّمة.

en.name: Filter for a water-jar.
description: A clay water-jar filter perforated with Arabic calligraphic decoration that originates from Fustat, the old capital of Egypt. The filter once sealed the mouth of a small water-jar without a handle; functioning as a lid to protect the contents of the jar from, for example, flies, insects and dust. Neither the jar or its filter are glazed, allowing the water inside the porous body to evaporate a little, thus helping to keep the water in the jar cool. The incised calligraphy that pierces right through the base of the filter is a repetition of the two letters *Alif* (A) and *Lam* (L). They are written here in *kufic* script, a style named after the city of Kufa in Iraq. The *kufic* style is characterised by its geometrical shapes and decoration on the ends of the elongated parts of the words (see the vertical tips of the letters here). Calligraphy was not the only decorative device used to embellish such vessels: animals, geometric patterning and floral designs were also employed. No two vessels appear to be identical, despite the frequent use of animals such as elephants, hares and birds.

Arabic calligraphy has been employed to decorate many objects in the Islamic world, from the commonplace, like this Fatimid water-jar filter, to the special, such as that found inlaid on metalwares. Such filters were decorated individually, whereby no two identical ones have been found.
holder: Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum, Glasgow Museums.
keywords: Water; domestic pottery; calligraphic decoration; earthenware

es.name: Filtro para vasija de agua.
description:
Filtro de arcilla para vasija de agua procedente de Fustat (Egipto), con perforaciones en forma de caligrafía arábiga. Este filtro se colocaba en la boca de una pequeña vasija de agua sin asas y protegía su interior de polvo, moscas y otros insectos. La vasija y el filtro no se vidriaron para que el interior fuera poroso, de este modo se facilitaba una pequeña evaporación y el agua se mantenía fresca. La caligrafía que constituye el calado del filtro repite dos letras: *alif* (a) y *lam* (l) en escritura cúfica, caligrafía que debe su nombre a la ciudad de Kufa (Irak). El estilo cúfico se caracteriza por su forma geométrica y por la decoración de los extremos de las partes alargadas de las letras (véanse los extremos de los trazos verticales en esta pieza).  
La caligrafía no es el único recurso decorativo en este tipo de objetos, que también se adornaban con animales, diseños geométricos y florales. No hay dos filtros iguales, pese al uso continuado de animales tales como elefantes, liebres y aves en su decoración.

La caligrafía arábiga se utilizaba para decorar todo tipo de objetos, desde los más comunes, como este filtro fatimí para una vasija de agua, hasta otros más exquisitos como piezas de metal con incrustaciones. Cada filtro presenta una decoración diferente, por lo que no hay dos idénticos.
holder: Galería de Arte y Museo Kelvingrove, Museos de Glasgow.
dates: Siglo IV o V de la Hégira / X-XI d. C.
keywords: agua; alfarería de uso doméstico; decoración caligráfica.
materials: Arcilla sin vidriar, torneada e incisa.
tags: Arcilla sin vidriar, torneada e incisa.

fr.name: Filtre à gargoulette.
description: Filtre à eau en argile perforé à décoration calligraphique arabe, originaire de Fustat, l'ancienne capitale de l'Égypte. Ce filtre était jadis placé sur l'ouverture d'une petite gargoulette sans poignée et servait de couvercle pour protéger le contenu du récipient des mouches, insectes divers et de la poussière. Ni la gargoulette ni le filtre n'étaient vernissés, ce qui permettait une légère évaporation de l'eau contribuant au maintien d'une certaine fraîcheur. La calligraphie gravée qui traverse le fond du filtre est une répétition des deux lettres Alif (A) et Lam (L). Elle est de style coufique, ainsi nommé d'après la ville de Koufa, en Irak. Ce style se caractérise par des formes géométriques et l'ornementation de l'extrémité des parties allongées (voir ici la tête des lettres). La calligraphie n'était pas le seul procédé décoratif utilisé pour embellir ce type d'objet, puisque l'on trouvait également des animaux, des motifs géométriques et floraux. Il semble qu'aucun filtre n'ait été identique malgré l'utilisation fréquente de représentations animalières comme éléphants, lièvres et oiseaux.

La calligraphie arabe a été employée dans le monde arabe pour décorer de nombreux objets, du plus banal, comme ce filtre à gargoulette fatimide, à l’exceptionnel, comme les exemplaires incrustés sur des ustensiles en métal. De tels filtres étaient décorés un par un, c’est pourquoi il n’en a pas été trouvé deux identiques.
holder: Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum, Glasgow Museums.
dates: IVe-Ve siècle de l’Hégire (Xe-XIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: eau ; poterie domestique ; décoration calligraphique
materials: Céramique non vernissée, tournée et incisée.
tags: Céramique non vernissée, tournée et incisée.

en.name: Grão Vasco Museum
description:
The Museum, installed in a late 16th-century building that was originally intended as a seminary, completes the visit to the cathedral, from which a substantial part of the museum’s extraordinary collection originates, namely the best known of all the paintings by Vasco Fernandes.  
The 14 panels of equal size that make up the first part of the collection were part of the retable commissioned for the chancel in 1506 by the Bishop D. Fernando Gonçalves de Miranda, and concluded by his successor D. Diego Ortiz de Villegas. Overall the panels appear to have a direct relationship and to display appropriation of processes in vogue in Flemish workshops in Ghent and Bruges at the time. These range from the general structure of each panel, the most diverse elements and figurative strategies, the sometimes bizarre perspectives, anatomical structure (conceived in baggy drapery), the physiognomy of figures, types of apparel and ornaments and the superb technique with which the details are transcribed. This must be related not only to the prevailing trend and its influence on Portuguese artists, but also to the direct participation of Flemish artists. The Master craftsman, possibly Vasco Fernandes, who was resident in the city at that time, also called on a woodcarver and sculptor, Arnau de Carvalho and João de Utreque, respectively, to create the carved, gilded-wood structure that held and framed the panels of this collective work of art.  
The didactic and liturgical elements within the pictorial scheme include one of the most important narrative scenes alluding to the Life of the Virgin and the Childhood and Passion of Christ. The most relevant detail, which greatly contributed to the popularity of this work, is that of the Brazilian Amerindian substituting the traditional black figure of Balthazar in the *Adoration of the Magi*. This is, in fact, the first Western representation of a native of Brazil, two or three years after the region’s discovery by the Portuguese.  
Another example of the expressive resources of Grão Vasco in his first phase, is the well identified work representing the *Assumption of the Virgin*, c. 1515.  
The two panels from the Chapel of the Episcopal Palace at Fontelo, *Christ in the House of Martha* and *The Last Supper*, produced in his workshop in the 1530s, reveal a significant increase in formal repertoires and a gradual moving away from the Flemish processes dominant in his early work. The iconographic complexity of *The Last Supper* seems to indicate that D. Miguel da Silva, both masterminded and commissioned it. Indeed the portrait of this patron in *Christ in the House of Martha*, where he is seated at the table, to the right of Christ, a presence emphasised by his coat-of-arms on the plinths of the columns, seems to suggest a direct relationship with the painter.  
The very large paintings that Fernandes produced, under the patronage of D. Miguel, for the apse chapels and the cloister of Viseu Cathedral, of which five large retables remain in this collection, are centred on the expressive potentialities of form, and experiment with new methods of organising space and composition.  
In the famous *St Peter*, one of the high points of his creative achievement, the expressive strength of the work is concentrated in the monumental, austere gravity of the Holy Patriarch, seated on an Italian-style throne, severe and firm, almost intimidating. The light coming from the right plays a determinant role in the sculptural modelling of the figure and its autonomy in relation to the throne, which is basically underpinned by the projected shadow and the vigorous triangular structure.  
In *Calvary*, representing a spectacle of dramatic pain and grief, among other strategies, the artist significantly elevates the composition in relation to the spectator, opting for theatrical concentration and a greater monumentality of the figures, spacing them with patches of colour, burnished by the light.  
*St Sebastian*, a poetic nude representation, is the perfect expression of his approach to the expressive methods of Italian painting.  
The *Pentecost* panel, similar, with few variations, to that in the Sacristy of the Church of Santa Cruz in Coimbra and signed “Velascus”, is also worthy of note. With the representation of the Manueline vaulting of the cathedral, he seeks to accentuate the relationship between the spectator and the painting, between real, and virtual space.  
In the miniature paintings of the *predella* of these huge retables in the form of a pall, the form of which highlights the transition from the Nordic to the Italian, a synthesis can be identified between a language that does not hide either the teachings of the Flemish school or the assimilation of the Italian style.  
Among the remaining Manueline works of art in the Museum, there are some sculptures in Ança limestone from workshops in Coimbra, today minus their original polychrome. There is also a 15th-century relief plaque in alabaster imported from Nottingham, and a very rare 16thcentury Afro-Portuguese ivory *pyx*made in Sierra Leone where local craftsmen copied a Portuguese model, almost certainly in silver. The iconography, however, is taken from engravings from a Book of Hours printed in France in 1498. Note also the Portuguese Royal coat of arms, the cross of the Order of Christ and the inscription *“Ave (Maria) Gratia Plena”*.

en.name: Parish Church of St. Mary Magdalene
description:
For Croatian architecture, the Church of St. Mary Magdalene is a unique Late Baroque interpretation of the specifically Baroque oval ground plan. The exceptional form of the plan, and the high quality of the church, are in line with the social position of those who commissioned it. The building also sets itself apart by its position on the planes of the Sava Valley where, with its striking façade, it towers over the landscape. Positioned on one of the most important approach roads to the centre of Croatia's largest diocese, it also marks the frontier zone of Croatia proper.  
Composed of an oval nave with a high cupola – continued along the longitudinal axes on the one hand by a square sanctuary, and on the other by an ellipsoidal forecourt – the church follows the paradigmatic approaches of Fischer von Erlach and Johann Lucas von Hildebrandt, which was transformed during the 18th century within their wide circle of Austrian disciples. In this context there is an obvious divergence from the Styrian influences that prevailed in the area – the usual and widespread dynamism given to the oval ground plan with wide side-chapels and narrow diagonal chapels –  is reduced here to the diagonal ones only, by which a stronger spatial cohesion is achieved, heightened by the omission of the tambour. At the same time, in the articulation of the walls, the usual wall pillars with sections of beams, give way to double pilasters and a continuous trabeation, once again brought to life in the contemporary Viennese Rococo-Classical architecture of Franz Munggenast (1724–1748) and Nicolò Pacassi (1716–1790). Also belonging to the Rococo is the refined transparency and airiness of the interior, created here by the light from the great window-cartouches in the chapels and the oval skylights in the dome. Apart from the realisation of a dominant oval space with a dome, clearly expressed on the plastic body of the church, this building opens up one more important topic in Late Baroque architecture, and that is the dynamically mobile façade with two bell towers. An effective contrast to the convex central-façade zone is achieved by the concave surfaces of the bell towers detached from the body of the church. This composition of volumes, supplemented by well worked-out architectural sculpting, goes beyond many contemporary Central European works and suggests an excellent architect at work, trained in the foundations of the highest achievements of Viennese Baroque architecture, and clearly a member of the Maria Theresia court style.

Within the framework of relatively few Late Baroque central-oval churches in Croatia, the Parish Church of St. Mary Magdalene in Sela by Sisak is the most monumental creation, brought into being by the Zagreb chapter on the estate where it stands. The quality of the church is evident in the elegant oval nave with a dome, and in the distinctive convex-concave façade with its two bell towers. Its stylistic characteristics, which as well as being Late Baroque also take in Rococo and Classical architecture, tell of a well-informed practitioner who was inspired by the leading architects in Austria at the time – Fischer von Erlach and Johann Lucas von Hildebrandt – while also acquainted with contemporary architecture in Vienna.
type: Religious, Baroque central oval church with dome
artist: Zagreb chapter and the parish priest, Matija Šantek
history: The Parish Church of St. Mary Magdalene in Sela by Sisak, founded by Bishop Stjepan Selišević in 1701 on an estate belonging to the Zagreb chapter, was originally made of wood. The parishioners comprised largely the canons of Zagreb, and included the well-known historian, Baltazar Krčelić, who had a prestigious position in Vienna and may have had a hand in the selection of the architect and initiated the construction of this monumental brick-built church. The foundation stone was laid in 1759 and building was complete by 1786.
keywords: Sela by Sisak, Parish Church of St. Mary Magdalene, Zagreb chapter, Late Baroque, oval-church with dome, façade with two bell towers
tags: Sela by Sisak, Parish Church of St. Mary Magdalene, Zagreb chapter, Late Baroque, oval-church with dome, façade with two bell towers

cs.name: *Poprsí světce*
description:
Busta na původním volutovém podstavci vyrůstá z poměrně úzké základny a rozšiřuje se do uzavřeného, kompaktního tvaru hrudníku. Jde o stařeckou prostovlasou a vousatou hlavu s draperií volně přehozenou přes pravé rameno, zřejmě o jednoho z církevních otců, sv. Jeronýma. Pojednání podstavce svědčí o tom, že šlo o relikviář.  Drahocenný charakter plastice dodává povrchová úprava – precizně provedené stříbření, jenž bohatou světelnou škálou umocňuje vizuální působení díla.  
Poprsí světce představuje sochařovo široké rozpětí své tvůrčí dovednosti nejen řezbář­ské, ale především zachycení duševního hnutí.  Extatický výraz touhy a odevzdání se Bohu se neprojevuje hrubou expresí, nýbrž má elegantní, dvorský charakter, vyjádřený esovitým pohybem figury a měkkým tvarováním objemu.  
Poučení o pojetí bust mohl Lengelacher získat již v rodném Bavorsku, ale i během svého vídeňského pobytu – prostřednictvím Giovanni Giulianiho, který opatřil chórové lavice v dolnorakouském klášteře Heiligenkreutz celým  souborem bust. S Giulianim se seznámil zřejmě při výzdobě vídeňského Belvederu.  
R. 1719 se Lengelacher usadil v Mikulově a jako dvorní sochař Waltra Františka  
z Dietrichštejna a vytvořil plastickou výzdobu několika interiérů jihomoravských kostelů. Lengelacherovo *Poprsí světce* je částí početnější řady související  
s původní výpravou oltářních mens kostela sv. Michaela v Dolních Věstonicích, který Lengelacher sochařsky vybavil ve štuku i řezbě. Pracoval tam od konce dvacátých let v časové souvislosti s jednou ze svých prvních velkých zakázek, výzdobě benediktinského kostela v Rajhradě (1727–1734).

Poprsí světce představuje umění nejen řezbářské, ale především schopnost zachycení duševního hnutí.  Extatický výraz touhy a odevzdání se Bohu se neprojevuje hrubou expresí, nýbrž má elegantní, dvorský charakter. Relikviářová busta je součástí větší řady původní výzdoby oltářů v Dolních Věstonicích.
keywords: Busta; relikviář

en.name: *Bust of a Saint*
description:
The bust, on an original volute pedestal, arises out of a relatively narrow base widening into a compact chest. The bearded head is that of an old man, with a cloak thrown loosely over the right shoulder. The figure might be St. Hieronymus, one of the church fathers. The pedestal shows that the object was a reliquary.  
*Bust of a Saint* demonstrates the artist's broad creativity seen not only his technical craft but also in his ability to capture mental states. The ecstatic expression of desire and submission to God is not rough-hewn, but has an elegant, court-like nature manifest in the figure's S-shaped movement and the soft shaping of the volume.  
Lengelacher may have familiarised himself with bust-making in his native Bavaria, or during a stay in Vienna through Giovanni Giuliani, who provided the gallery pews in the Heiligenkreutz Monastery, Lower Austria, with a whole series of busts. Lengelacher probably met Giuliani while working on the decorations of the Belveder in Vienna.  
In 1719 Lengelacher settled in Mikulov, where as sculptor to Walter František of Dietrichstein, he created sculpted interior decorations for several south Moravian churches. Lengelacher's *Bust of a Saint* is part of a series of original decorations for altar tables in the Church of St. Michael, Dolní Věstonice, which Lengelacher embellished with stuccoes and carvings. The artist worked there from the 1720s in relation to one of his first major commissions, the Benedictine church in Rajhrad (1727–1734).

*Bust of a Saint* demonstrates both the artist's skill as a sculptor and his ability to capture mental states. The ecstatic expression of desire and submission to God is not rough-hewn but has an elegant, court-like nature. The reliquary bust is part of the original altar decorations in Dolní Věstonice.
keywords: Bust; reliquary; religious object; sculpture; sculpted wood

en.name: Tile panel
description: Each tile of this large stair-shaped panel is ornamented with moulded octagons and partial hexagrams such that one corner is cut out to fit a separate spherical knob. This group of tiles is similar to a well-known group of tiles that once ornamented the exterior of Takht-i Sulaiman (c. 1270), which was the summer palace of the Ilkhanid ruler Abaqa (r. 1265–82). When Doris Duke purchased the tiles in Iran in 1938, they were said to have been excavated from a site called Sanek.

ar.name: طالع دمشق (نظام الماء).
description:
يعتبر نظام توزيع الماء في سوريا هاماً لنجاح المنطقة كمركز للحضارة، ويرتبط توفر المياه الجارية التي تغذي كلاً من المنازل الخاصة والمباني العامة بالإرث الحضاري الدمشقي القديم في السقاية والقنوات تحت الأرضية التي ما تزال قائمة حتى يومنا هذا. ويعرف أحد أحياء دمشق الشهيرة باسم القنوات نسبة إلى القنوات الرومانية التي كانت تغذيه، والتي تمت صيانتها بشكل جيد خلال الفترة الإسلامية.  
خلال فترة النهضة العمرانية التي بدأها نور الدين بن زنكي، المتوفى عام 569/ 1174، عرفت دمشق بحماماتها، وسبلها، وسهولة وصول المياه إلى جوامعها ومدارسها وبيمارستاناتها. ويعتبر السبيل والساقية الجارية المتصلين بالحوض في المدرسة النورية التي تم بناؤها عام 563/ 7-1168 مثالاً على إبداع نور الدين في تأمين المياه، فهذه الوفرة في المياه دليل على الحكم الجيد.  
المصدر الرئيس للمياه في دمشق هو نهر بردى الذي ينبع من جبال لبنان الشرقية قرب الزبداني على ارتفاع 1100م، وتصل المياه إلى دمشق عبر ست قنوات رئيسة على الرغم من وجود أكثر من 40 فرعاً. وقد تم استخدام قنوات الماء تحت الأرضية بعبقرية خلال التاريخ لتحويل المنطقة شبه الصحراوية إلى واحة خضراء.  
يوجد في المدينة نظام لتوزيع الماء يدعى الطالع مهمته توزيع حصص المياه على الأحياء حسب القراريط، والقيراط هو وحدة قياس تعادل 1 من 24، أي أن مجموع المياه الموجودة في الطالع هو 24 قيراط، وحسب ما هو مذكور في كل صك ملكية، يحدد حق المياه لكل مبنى بنسبة معينة من المياه التي يؤمنها نظام الطالع، ويقاس بعدد القراريط. وقد كان هذا النظام ترتيباً عمرانياً ميز دمشق في الفترتين الأتابكية والأيوبية. لقد تم بناء حمام نور الدين على سبيل المثال قرب طالعه، والمدرسة العادلية تقع قرب السبع طوالع، وهو حي سمي نسبة للسبع طوالع التي تزوده بالمياه.  
يعرف المشرف على عملية التوزيع باسم الفرضي (أي العالم بالفرائض و ما يتبعه من تقدير المقادير في الحقوق، وهو أيضاً الذي يوزع كلف تنظيف الأنهار…الخ)، وهو بالنسبة لتوزيع الماء نظير المحتسب الذي يتأكد من حسن توزيع المياه بالعدل والقسطاس. وكنتيجة لنظام الطالع، كان الماء من نهر بردى يصل إلى كل منزل، والبيوت الدمشقية معروفة حتى اليوم، على عكس البيوت الأخرى، بالحوض في فسحتها السماوية المركزية ونافورتها، فمنظر المياه وصوتها كانا على الدوام رمزاً للحياة الرغيدة.  
يوجد في حلب أيضاً نظام هام لتوزيع الماء ضمن القنوات معروف باسم القسطل، وقد أنشأ نور الدين المدرسة الشعيبية عام 545/ 1150 قرب القسطل الشعيبي الذي ما يزال يحمل اسمه، ويحدد الامتداد الذي وصل إليه عمله في توزيع المياه، كما تشتهر حماة بنواعيرها التي تم بناؤها خلال حكم نور الدين.

اعتبر نهر بردى المصدر الرئيسي المُزوِّد بالماء لمدينة دمشق، والذي ينبع من جبال على الحدود مع لبنان، ويصل دمشق عن طريق ست فروع رئيسية، بالإضافة الى قنوات المياة الصغيرة العديدة. كان الفضل الأكبر في التصميم الذكي لهذا النظام المائي، والذي كان يمتد ليزود منازل دمشق للحاكم نور الدين محمد بن زنكي (المُتوفَّى عام 569 هـ/ 1174 م). وقد شمل هذا النظام أيضاً المناطق المجاورة عن طريق ما يسمى "طالع، والذي كان يقيس منسوب المياه ويوزعها على المقاطعات المجاورة.
dates: أواسط القرن السادس/ أواسط الثاني عشر.
keywords: سبيل؛ سقاية؛ طالع؛ قسطل؛ قناة؛ ماء؛ نهر بردى.
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Museums and Antiquities

en.name: The *tali'* (water system) of Damascus.
description:
The water-distribution system in Syria is important for the region's success as a centre of civilisation. The availability of running water nourishing both private houses and public buildings is tribute to the ancient Damascene heritage of irrigation and underwater canals that survives to this day. One of Damascus's most famous neighbourhoods is known as 'Hayy al-Qanawat' after the Roman water canals that supplied it, and which were well maintained under Islamic rule.  
During the period of prolific construction begun by Nur al-Din Mahmud bin al-Zangi (d. AH 569 / AD 1174) Damascus was renowned for its luxurious bathhouses (*hammams*), its public drinking fountains(*sabils*), andthe accessibility of running water within its mosques, *madrasas* and hospitals (*bimaristans)*.The water fountain and running stream attached to the courtyard basin at the Madrasa Nuriyya, built in AH 563 / AD 1167–8, is an example of the Nuri creativity in water provision, for this visible abundance of water was a mark of good governance.  
The Barada River is the main water source, springing from the Anti-Lebanon Mountains near the Zabadani district at an altitude of 1100 m. Water reaches Damascus via six main channels, although the total tributaries are around 40. The underwater canals of Syria have been ingeniously used throughout history to transform a dry and desert-like region into a green one.  
There is a system of water distribution in the city called a *tali'*, which distributres a share of water to each neighbourhood based on a unit known as a *qirat*. The *qirat* is a unit of measurement equalling 1 out of 24. The total water supply in a *tali'*' is therefore 24 qirats and, as stated in the lease of any given property, each building has the right to a ratio of this water allocated by the *tali* system and measured as a number of *qirats*. This system of water distribution withan an urban setting was the hallmark of Atabeg and Ayyubid Damascus. Hammam Nur al-Din, for example, was constructed adjacent to its *tali'* and the Madrasa Adiliyya is located near Hayy al-Sabi' Tawali', a neighbourhood named after the seven *tali*'s supplying it.  
The official controller who oversees the distribution process is known as *al-faradi*, an aqua-specific counterpart to the *muhtasib* who ensures that water distribution is fair and legal. As a result of this *tali*' system, water from the Barada River reaches every home; the Demascene home, unlike any other, is known to this day for its central courtyard basin and sprinkling fountain, the sight and sound of water always symbolic of good living.  
Similarly, in Aleppo, there is an important system of channelled water distribution known as *al-qastal*. The Madrasa al-Shu'aybiyya, built by Nur al-Din in AH 545 / AD 1150 was erected next to the Qastal al-Shuaybiyy which still carries his inscription and marks the extent of his work in water distribution. Also, the city of Hama is famous for its waterwheels or *noria*s, a number of which were built during Nur al-Din's reign.

The supply of water for the city of Damascus relies on the River Barada, which springs from the Anti-Lebanon mountain range and reaches Damascus via six main channels and numerous minor ones. The expert manipulation of these precious waters to ensure water supply for every public institution and private house of the city was the hallmark of the rule of Nur al-Din Mahmud bin Zangi (d. AH 569 / AD 1174). Each neigbourhood was equipped with a *tali'* through which water was measured and distributed to the surrounding properties.
dates: Hegira mid-6th century / AD mid-12th century.
keywords: Water; sabil; fountains; water channels (qanat); irrigation; Barada River; tali, qastal
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Museums and Antiquities

es.name: Sistema de distribución de agua *(tali')* de Damasco.
description:
Los sistemas de distribución de agua de Siria resultan muy importantes para la prosperidad de una región como centro de civilización. En Damasco, la disponibilidad de agua corriente para casas particulares y edificios públicos es herencia de los antiguos canales para riego encauzamiento de aguas subterráneas que ha llegado hasta nuestros días. Uno de los barrios más famosos de Damasco se llama Hayy al-Qanawat por los canales romanos que le suministraban agua y que se mantuvieron en la época islámica.  
Durante el prolífico periodo de construcción que inició Nur al-Din Mahmud ibn al-Zangi (m. 569 / 1174), la ciudad de Damasco se hizo famosa por sus lujosos baños *(hammam)* y fuentes *(sabil)*, y por el acceso al agua corriente dentro de mezquitas, madrasas y hospitales *(bimaristan)*. La fuente y la corriente de agua del patio de la madrasa Nuriyya, construida en 563 / 1167-68, son un ejemplo de la creatividad que llegó a alcanzarse en el suministro de agua, ya que una patente abundancia de agua era señal de un buen gobierno.  
El río Barada, que nace en la cordillera del Antilíbano, cerca del distrito de Zabadani, a 1.100 m de altitud, es la principal fuente de suministro. El agua llega a Damasco por seis canales principales, aunque existen cerca de 40 canales secundarios. Los canales subterráneos de Siria se han usado a lo largo de la historia de formas muy ingeniosas para transformar en vergeles zonas áridas y desérticas.  
La ciudad posee un sistema de distribución de agua, denominado *tali’*, que reparte el agua por los barrios basándose en una unidad de medida, el *qirat*, equivalente a 1/24. Por tanto, el suministro de agua total de un *tali'* es de 24 *qirat*, y cada edificio tiene derecho a una proporción de agua medida en *qirat*, asignada por el sistema de *tali'* y establecida como en cualquier arrendamiento de una propiedad. Este sistema de distribución incluido en la red urbana era el sello distintivo del Damasco atabeg y ayyubí. El *hammam* de Nur al-Din, por ejemplo, se construyó a su *tali’*, y la madrasa Adiliyya se encuentra cerca de Hayy al-Sabi’ Tawali’, un barrio que se llama así por los siete *tali’* que lo abastecían.  
El funcionario que supervisa el proceso de distribución se llama *al-faradi* y es el homólogo del *muhtasib*, que garantiza un reparto del agua justo y legal. Gracias al sistema de *tali’*, el agua del río Barada llega a todas las casas. Los hogares damascenos, a diferencia de otros, son célebres aún hoy por tener una pila y una fuente en el patio central. La visión y el sonido del agua siempre han sido símbolo de una buena vida.  
El Alepo existe, igualmente, un importante sistema de distribución de agua canalizada que se denomina *al-qastal*. La madrasa al-Shu'aybiyya, construida por Nur al-Din en 545 / 1150, se erigió junto al *qastal* al-Shuaybiyy, que sigue llevando su inscripción y deja constancia del alcance de sus obras en el suministro de agua. Por otra parte, la ciudad de Hama es famosa por sus norias, varias de las cuales se construyeron durante el reinado de Nur al-Din.

El suministro de agua de Damasco procede del río Barada, que nace en la cordillera del Antilíbano y llega a la ciudad por seis canales principales y numerosos conductos menores. El gobierno de Nur al-Din Mahmud ibn Zangi (m. 569 / 1174) se caracterizó por una sabia manipulación del agua —un bien escaso— que aseguraba el suministro a instituciones públicas y casas particulares. Cada barrio disponía de un *tali'* por medio del cual se dividía el agua por peso y se repartía entre los edificios vecinos.
dates: Mediados del siglo VI de la Hégira / XII d. C.
keywords: agua; sabil; fuentes; canales de agua (qanat); riego; río Barada; tali'; qastal.
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Museums and Antiquities

fr.name: Système de distribution d'eau de Damas (*tali‘*).
description:
Le système de distribution de l'eau en Syrie est particulièrement important pour assurer la réussite d'une région comme centre de civilisation. La disponibilité d'eau courante pour alimenter aussi bien les maisons privées que les bâtiments publics est un héritage de l'ancien système d'irrigation et des canaux souterrains de Damas, système qui a subsisté jusqu'à aujourd'hui. L'un des quartiers les plus célèbres de la ville est appelé "Hayy al-Qanawat" d'après les canalisations romaines qui l'alimentaient et qui ont été conservées sous l'administration islamique.  
Au cours de la prolifique période de constructions de Nour al-Din Mahmoud bin al-Zangi (m. 569 H / 1174 J.-C.), Damas était réputée pour le luxe de ses hammams, de ses fontaines publiques et la disponibilité de l'eau courante dans ses mosquées, ses *madrasa* et ses hôpitaux (*bimaristan*). La fontaine et le petit canal reliés au bassin de la cour de la *madrasa* Nouriyya, construite en 563 H / 1168 J.-C., sont un exemple de la créativité dans l'adduction d'eau car cette abondance visible était la marque d'une bonne administration.  
Le fleuve Barada, qui naît dans les montagnes de l'Anti-Liban vers Zabadani à 1 100 m d'altitude, était la principale source d'approvisionnement. L'eau atteint Damas par six canaux principaux et plus d'une trentaine d'ouvrages secondaires. Les canaux souterrains de Syrie ont été utilisés tout au long de l'histoire et ont contribué à transformer ce paysage désertique en région agricole.  
La ville bénéficie d'un système de distribution, le *tali'*, qui répartit l'eau entre les quartiers selon une unité de calcul appelée *qirat* et représentant 1/24e de *tali'*, comme précisé dans les baux de nombreuses propriétés. Chaque bâtiment a droit à un certain nombre de *qirat*. Ce système de distribution de l'eau à l'intérieur du réseau urbain porte le sceau des Atabegs et des Ayyoubides damascènes. Le hammam Nour al-Din, par exemple, fut construit à proximité de son *tali'* et la *madrasa* al-Adiliyya édifiée près de Hayy al-Sabi' Tawali', quartier ainsi nommé d'après les sept *tali'* qui l'approvisionnent.  
Le contrôleur officiel qui surveille la distribution est appelé *al-faradi*, équivalent du *mouhtasib* qui contrôle l'équité et la légalité de la distribution de l'eau. L'eau du Barada dessert ainsi chaque foyer damascène, où le bassin central dans la cour et la fontaine, la vue et le bruit de l'eau continuent à symboliser les agréments de la vie.  
Il existe de même à Alep un important système de distribution canalisée de l'eau appelée *al-qastal*. La *madrasa* al-Shuaybiyya, édifiée par Nour al-Din en 545 H / 1150 J.-C., a été construite près du *qastal* al-Shuaybiyy qui comporte encore des inscriptions et des marques de son rôle majeur dans la distribution de l'eau. La ville de Hama est également fameuse pour ses norias dont un certain nombre ont été construites sous le règne de Nour al-Din.

L'alimentation en eau de Damas dépend du Barada qui prend sa source dans l'Anti-Liban et dessert la ville au moyen de six canalisations principales et plusieurs conduites secondaires. La gestion experte de ces eaux permettait d'alimenter toutes les institutions publiques et les maisons de la ville et fut une des grandes réussites du règne de Nour al-Din Mahmoud bin Zangi (m. 569 H / 1174 J.-C.). Chaque quartier était équipé d'un *tali'* où l'eau était jaugée avant d'être distribuée aux propriétés avoisinantes.
dates: Milieu du VIe siècle de l'Hégire (milieu du XIIe siècle J.-C.)
keywords: Eau ; sabil ; fontaines ; canalisations d'eau (qanat) ; irrigation ; Barada (fleuve) ; tali‘ ; qastal
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Museums and Antiquities

en.name: The way to Calvary
description:
This crowded and airless way to Calvary with soldiers and executioners all around Christ is in the typical caricature style of Francesco Brizio (c. 1574–1623).  
He most likely developed this style in the workshop of Bartolomeo Passerotti (1529–1592), a specialist in genre scenes with caricatures.
place: Oratory of the Madonna dell’Orazione, entrance wall
partner: Musei Civici d’Arte Antica di Bologna in cooperation with the Province of Bologna

it.name: La Salita al Calvario
description:
Questa affollata *Salita al calvario*, con soldati e aguzzini che si accalcano attorno a Cristo, quasi a togliergli l'aria, appartiene allo stile quasi caricaturale di Francesco Brizio (1574 ca. – 1623).  
Brizio sviluppò questo linguaggio nella bottega di Bartolomeo Passerotti (1529–1592), specializzato in scene di genere con figure dai tratti molto caricati.
place: Oratorio della Madonna della Consolazione, parete d'ingresso

ar.name: حوض نحاسي (زبدية).
description: حوض ماء نحاسي مرصَّع بالفضة في الأساس، ومقسَّم إلى ستة أقسام تفصل بينها ست دوائر. مزخرف بخط يد أسود عريض ومنقوش؛ نقرأ فيه: 'هذا واحد من الأشياء التي صنعت لصاحب السموِّ، العظيم، الجليل، العالم، العزيز صاحب الفخامة، العادل، الفاتح، المحارب، المدافع، حامي الحمى، المعزَّز بقوة الله، المنتصِر، المدبِّر، حسَن التوجيه، القادر، الكامل، المؤيِّد للسلطان، حامل الختم، الملك الناصري'. وفي هذا إشارة إلى موظف رسمي ذي مرتبة رفيعة، مسؤول عن مراسلات السلطان ومهامه الحكومية. فالملك الناصر (الذي حكم لثلاث فترات ما بين 692- 740 / 1293- 1340) هو من وهب الحوض. ثمة ثلاث دوائر تحتوي على رسم شعار النبالة؛ أما الثلاث الأخرى فتضم تشكيلة متناسقة لستة طيور: اثنان متقابلان؛ واثنان ينظر كلٌّ منهما في اتجاه مغاير؛ واثنان متباعدان عن بعضهما بعضاً، لكنهما ملتفتان أحدهما إلى الآخر. إن تشكيلات هذه الدوائر بطيورها، أو بطيور الماء المؤطَّرة فيها، تعتبر ملمحاً بارزاً في الأشغال المعدنية المصرية خلال العهد المملوكي وتميِّزها عن الأشغال المعاصرة في كل من سوريا والعراق وإيران.

كانت الأواني المشابهة لهذا الطست، باهظة الثمن إلى حدّ كبير. والنقش الذي يطوّق الطست، هو من نمط خطّ **الثلث**، ويقوم بوصف ألقاب المسؤول المملوكي الكبير الذي كان يملكه. أما الشعار المحفور في الكوى الفاصلة للنص، فيشي بأن المالك كان مسؤولاً عن مراسلات السلطان.
holder: متحف وصالة فنون كيلفينغروف، متاحف غلاسكو.
keywords: رعاية؛ زخرفة كتابية؛ طبقة حاكمة؛ ماء.

en.name: Water-basin.
description: A brass water-basin originally inlayed with silver and divided into six sections with the aid of six roundels. Decorated with a band of bold calligraphic inscription, the text reads: 'This is one of the things made for his highness, the lordly, the kingly, the learned, the treasure house of excellence, the just, the conqueror, the warrior, the defender, the protector of frontiers, the fortified by God, the victorious, the planner, the well-ordered, the masterful, the complete, supporter of the khan, the Seal Bearer, the king the Nassiri.' The inscription indicates an official of high rank in charge of the Sultan Al-Malik Al-Nasir's correspondence and other administrative responsibilities. Al-Malik Al-Nasir (who ruled during three phases between AH 692 and 740 / AD 1293 and 1340) commissioned the basin. Three of the roundels enclose the design of a blazon. The other three roundels have a symmetrical composition of six birds: two facing each other, two looking away from each other; and two moving away from each other but looking back at each other. The compositions of these roundels with their birds or waterfowl are a distinctive feature of Egyptian Mamluk metalwork, distinguishing it from contemporary Syrian, Iraqi and Iranian work.

Vessels like this one were quite expensive. The script round the basin is in the *thuluth* style, and describes the titles of the high-ranking Mamluk official who owned it. The blazon incised in the roundels that divide the text indicates that the owner was in charge of the sultan’s correspondence.
holder: Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum, Glasgow Museums
on temporary display at Glasgow Central Mosque.
keywords: Water; Ruling classes; patronage; calligraphy; coat of arms
materials: Brass; beaten and inlayed with silver.

es.name: Jofaina.
description: Jofaina de latón, originalmente con incrustaciones de plata. Su cara externa está decorada con una banda dividida en seis partes por seis medallones, con una inscripción caligráfica que reza: “Este es uno de los objetos hechos para su alteza, el señorial, el regio, el sabio, el albergue del tesoro de la excelencia, el justo, el conquistador, el guerrero, el defensor, el protector de las fronteras, el que obtiene su fuerza de Dios, el victorioso, el estratega, el poderoso, el completo, el sostenedor del *jan*, el portador del sello, el rey al-Nasiri”. El personaje en cuestión era un oficial de alto rango al servicio del sultán al-Malik al-Nasir, respomsable de la correspondencia y otras tareas administrativas. Al-Malik al-Nasir (que gobernó en tres etapas en 692-740 / 1293-1340) encargó esta jofaina. Tres de los medallones tienen dibujado un blasón y los otros tres presentan una composición simétrica con seis aves: dos afrontadas, dos mirando a lados opuestos y otras dos que se alejan una de otra pero mirándose. Este tipo de medallones con composiciones de pájaros y aves acuáticas son característicos de la metalistería mameluca y la distinguen de las piezas sirias, iraquíes e iraníes de la misma época.

Los recipientes de este tipo eran bastante caros. La inscripción que circunda esta jofaina, en escritura *zuluz*, repasa los títulos de su poseedor, un alto cargo mameluco. El blasón inciso en los medallones que dividen el texto indica que el dueño de esta pieza se encargaba de la correspondencia del sultán.
holder: Galería de Arte y Museo Kelvingrove, Museos de Glasgow.
dates: Siglo VIII de la Hégira / XIV d. C.
keywords: agua; clases gobernantes; mecenazgo; caligrafía.
materials: Latón batido con incrustaciones de plata.
tags: Latón batido con incrustaciones de plata.

fr.name: Bassin.
description: Bassin en cuivre jaune, incrusté d'argent à l'origine. Sa paroi extérieure est divisée en six sections séparées par six rondeaux. L'important bandeau calligraphique proclame : “Voici l'un des objets fabriqués pour son altesse, le seigneurial, le royal, le savant, le trésor d'excellence, le juste, le conquérant, le guerrier, le défenseur, le protecteur des frontières, celui qui tire sa force de Dieu, le victorieux, le clairvoyant, l'ordonné, le maître, l'absolu, le soutien du khan, …[?], le roi le Nassiri.” Ce qui permet de penser que ce bassin a été commandé par un successeur d'al-Malik al-Nasir, sultan qui régna à trois reprises (entre 692 H /1293 J.-C. et 740 H /1340 J.-C.). Trois des rondeaux contiennent un blason. Les trois autres présentent une composition symétrique de six oiseaux : deux affrontés, deux regardant en sens contraire l'un de l'autre et deux s'éloignant l'un de l'autre en se regardant. Les compositions à oiseaux ou poules d'eau sont caractéristiques du travail du métal de l'Égypte mamelouke et distinguent celui-ci du travail syrien, iranien ou irakien.

Les récipients comme celui-ci étaient relativement chers. L’inscription autour du bassin en style *toulouth* décrit les titres de son propriétaire, un haut dignitaire mamelouk. Le blason incisé dans les rondeaux qui divisent le texte indique qu’il était en charge de la correspondance du sultan.
holder: Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum, Glasgow Museums.
En exposition temporaire à la mosquée centrale de Glasgow.
dates: VIIIe siècle de l’Hégire (XIVe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: eau ; classes dirigeantes ; mécénat ; calligraphie

en.name: Tile panel in the form of a tomb cover
description: This tomb cover consists of three large luster tiles, all of which are covered in cobalt calligraphy in relief. It is presumed that this tripartite panel constituted the upper surface of a sarcophagus marking the burial place of Imam Ja‘far’s daughter. As a descendent of an imam, her tomb would have been known as an *imamzada* (Persian: imam born). During the Ilkhanid period of rule in Greater Iran (1256–1353), Shi‘ite imamzadas preserved some of the finest Persian tilework ever made.

en.name: *David*
description:
This is the third group that Gian Lorenzo Bernini undertook for Scipione Borghese, around the same time that he was making *Apollo and Daphne*.  
It shows David, the young hero of the Old Testament (the Book of Kings), prophet of Christ, just before he slings his stone at the giant Philistine Goliath. David's attitude would be incomprehensible if we did not perceive our own space as part of the scene. The enemy Goliath is in the same space as the viewer, with Bernini removing the boundary between the sculpture and the space that surrounds it, a space that also encloses us, participants in the scene. The resultant theatrical effect is one of the recurring themes in Baroque art.  
The work reveals the influence of modern and ancient sculptural models as well as contemporary painting styles, but the artist affords the whole a new realism. The face, possibly a self-portrait, is concentrated in a moment of high drama. The tension of the imminent action is visible in every muscle of the face and body, suspended between stasis and motion, as well as in the detail of the foot jutting out over the plinth, giving a strong impression of gripping on to it.  
The sculpture was backed on to a wall so that the viewer, when entering the room, saw it from the angle intended by the artist: obliquely from the left. This effect was calculated to enhance the plastic tension of the hero and the pictorial value of the sculpture through development of the action by walking around to the front of the statue.    
The original base was lost when the work was moved around the Villa over the centuries. The plinth has been enlarged using plaster to suit a taste for greater regularity, but was removed in a recent restoration, restoring the Baroque effect rendered by the structure of the foot.

Cardinal Borghese commissioned Bernini to sculpt the David when he was 25 years old. The artist had the intuition to stop the biblical hero just one second before the shot, placing Goliath’s presence in the viewer's space; perhaps a self-portrait of Bernini.
keywords: Classical model; movement; marble; anatomy; self portrait; theatre

it.name: *David*
description:
E' il terzo gruppo che Gian Lorenzo Bernini realizza per Scipione Borghese, quasi contemporaneamente all'esecuzione di *Apollo e Dafne*.  
Rappresenta David, il giovane eroe dell'Antico Testamento (I libro dei Re), profeta di Cristo, nel momento che precede il lancio del sasso contro il gigante filisteo Golia. L'atteggiamento di David sarebbe incomprensibile se non percepissimo il nostro spazio come parte integrante della scena. Il nemico Golia difatti rimane nel campo del fruitore, abolendo così Bernini il confine tra la scultura e lo spazio che la circonda, in cui anche noi ci muoviamo partecipi alla rappresentazione. L'effetto teatrale che ne deriva è uno degli aspetti ricorrenti dell'arte barocca.  
Nell'opera si riscontrano l'influenza sia di modelli di scultura antica e moderna che di pittura a lui contemporanea, ma l'artista riesce poi a fondere tutto in un nuovo realismo. Il volto, forse un autoritratto, è concentrato in un momento di alta drammaticità, dove la tensione dovuta all'azione imminente è percepibile in ogni muscolo del viso e del corpo, sospesi tra stasi e moto, ma anche nel particolare del piede aggettante dal plinto su cui sembra poggiarsi aggrappato con forte realismo.  
La scultura era addossata ad una parete in modo da dover fruire, entrando nella sala, il punto di vista scelto dall'artista, che partiva sulla diagonale da sinistra. L'effetto era calcolato per esaltare nel crescere dell'azione - ruotando intorno alla statua sino a guadagnare il punto frontale- la tensione plastica dell'eroe e il valore pittorico della scultura.  
La base originale si è persa durante uno degli spostamenti dell'opera nel corso dei secoli all'interno della Villa. Il plinto era stato ingrandito, con una integrazione in gesso, secondo un gusto che prediligeva una maggiore regolarità, ma è stato rimosso in un recente restauro, ripristinando l'effetto barocco reso dalla costruzione del piede.

Il cardinale Borghese commissionò a Bernini la scultura del *David* all'età di 25 anni. L'artista ebbe l'intuizione di fermare l'eroe biblico nella posizione subito precedente al momento del lancio, immaginando la presenza di Golia nello spazio del visitatore. Forse è un autoritratto di Bernini.
keywords: Modello classico; marmo; movimento; anatomia; autoritratto; teatro

en.name: Mtamar Silo
description:
One of the particular things about Tétouan is that it is built on limestone soil which consists of a veritable network of cavities and underground corridors, crossing the town from east to west. Silos were built into these cavities in the 10th/16th century, the period during which Tétouan’s *medina* was rebuilt. These dungeons or caves were essentially used to house the 30,000 slaves and Christian captives who helped build the town, and were still utilised in the 11th/17th and 12th/18th centuries.  
This subterranean prison, situated close to the Sidi al-Mandri Kasbah, contained three main sections into which light filtered into the sealed manholes through iron grills. The prisoners slid down into them using a rope, and guards could watch over them through the manholes. Smaller polygonal and sinuous compartments were juxtaposed into the three main sections, and were each separated by vaults and supporting arches. A church was also fitted, where Franciscan priests conducted religious services for the Christian prisoners. Towards the end of the 12th/18th century, the Sultan Mulay Sliman gave the order for the release of all prisoners, and the silos were closed down. Since then they have remained unused.

es.name: Silo Mtamar
description:
Una de las particularidades de Tetuán es el hecho de estar edificada sobre un suelo calcáreo surcado por una verdadera red de cavidades y galerías subterráneas, que atraviesan la ciudad de este a oeste. En estas cavidades se dispusieron los silos en el siglo X/XVI, época en la que se reconstruyó la *medina* de Tetuán. Estos silos se convirtieron luego en mazmorras, o matamoros, que se reservaron fundamentalmente a los casi 30.000 esclavos y cautivos cristianos que trabajaban en la construcción de la ciudad. Mantuvieron la misma función a lo largo de los siglos XI/XVII y XII/XVIII.  
Esta prisión subterránea, situada en las proximidades de la alcazaba Sidi al-Mandri, se dividía en tres compartimentos principales en los que la luz se filtraba a través de unas trampillas cerradas con rejas de hierro. Los prisioneros se deslizaban hasta allí por medio de una soga, y a través de las trampillas podían ser vigilados por los guardianes.  
Aparte de los tres compartimentos principales había otros más pequeños yuxtapuestos, de formas poligonales y sinuosas, separados entre sí por bóvedas y arcos de sostén. Se acondicionó allí una iglesia en la que los sacerdotes de la orden franciscana celebraban los servicios religiosos para los cautivos cristianos. A finales del siglo XII/XVIII, el sultán Mulay Sliman ordenó liberar a todos los prisioneros; los silos perdieron su función y desde entonces permanecen sin usar.

fr.name: Silo Mtamar
description:
Une des particularités de Tétouan est d’être construite sur un sol calcaire constituant un véritable réseau de cavités et de galeries souterraines traversant la ville d’est en ouest. Dans ces cavités furent aménagés, au Xe/XVIe siècle, les silos; date à laquelle a été reconstruite la médina de Tétouan. Ces cachots ou matamores étaient essentiellement réservés aux quelque 30 000 esclaves et captifs chrétiens qui contribuèrent à l’édification de la ville, et continuèrent à être utilisés aux XIe/XVIIe et XIIe/XVIIIe siècles.  
Cette prison souterraine, située à proximité de la casbah Sidi al-Mandri, renfermait trois compartiments principaux où la lumière filtrait à travers des regards scellés par des grillages de fer. Les prisonniers s’y glissaient au moyen d’une corde, et par ces regards les gardes pouvaient les surveiller.  
Aux trois principaux compartiments étaient juxtaposés de plus petits, aux formes polygonales et sinueuses, séparés entre eux par des voûtes et des arcs de soutènement. Une église avait été aménagée, où des prêtres de l’ordre des Franciscains célébraient les services religieux pour les détenus chrétiens. À la fin du XIIe/XVIIIe siècle, le sultan Moulay Slimane donna l’ordre de libérer tous les prisonniers et les silos furent désaffectés. Ils sont restés depuis lors inexploités.

en.name: In the Steppe between Misrata and Zliten
names: Italian military officers on the road between Misrata and Zliten, during the Italo-Turkish war
short_description: Italy and the Ottoman Empire signed a peace treaty that officially ended the Italo-Turkish war on October 18th, 1912, passing control of the former Ottoman provinces of Tripolitania, Fezzan, and Cyrenaica to Italy. The Ottoman army left Libya, but hostilities between Italian troops and the Arabs that did not acknowledge Italian authority continued. By July 1914, Italy was able to occupy almost all the territory of Tripolitania, the coast of Cyrenaica and part of the territory of Fezzan. In 1915 a great Arab insurrection broke out and forced Italy to abandon much of the territory it had previously occupied.
holder: Italian Institute for African and Oriental Studies

en.name: Putto with a winged helmet blowing a horn
description: The small sculpture was assumedly used as a table decoration in the Augsburg Fugger Palace, the residence of the Fugger family. At the time, wealthy merchants may have felt the influence of Roman mythology and this reason chosen as their symbol the God of Commerce, Travel and Theft, Mercury, who is iconographically reflected by the winged helmet worn by the putto. The aeruginous black bronze figure has been placed in a standing, forward-stepping frontal position on a plinth. The nude body is partly covered by a fluttering cape. With his head raised and chubby cheeks, the Putto is about to sound the crumhorn and to recount the history of the Fugger family to his audience. The impression of effort and determination comes from the gesture of his left arm stretched out with a clenched fist. The front of the helmet has been decorated with the motif of a fire-spitting dragon, which might well represent a symbol of defence.

The small bronze figure of a nude Putto sounding a crumhorn and wearing a winged helmet can be regarded as an allusion to Mercury the antique God of Commerce and Travel with the helmet symbolising the world of wealthy merchants.
artist: “Weilheim School of sculptors” (with H. Krumpper, H. Degler, C. Angermair, B. Steinle, P. Dirr); an important work of the Early Baroque in Weilheim in Oberbayern because of the pathos displayed by the figures.
keywords: Figural decoration; bronze figure
