ar.name: شباك جصي.
description:
القطعة عبارة عن شباك جصِّي قسِّم إلى إحدى عشرة وحدة زخرفية تتكون من أشكال نباتية وهندسية وكتابية. تغطي الوحدة الأولى منطقة عقد الشباك، وتتكون من زهرة مستديرة تتوافق وشكل العقد زخرفت بزخارف هندسية من زجاج من الألوان الأصفر والفيروزي والأحمر الغامق. يلي هذه الوحدة وحدة مستطيلة تحتوي على النص الكتابي الوحيد الذي يشتمل عليه الشباك، وهو نص قرآني من الآية رقم 19 من سورة التوبة (رقم 9) يقرأ "في سبيل الله لا يستوون عند الله". وكتب هذا النص بخط متشابك بزجاج أبيض اللون، وملئت الفراغات المحيطة بالنص بمربعات بسيطة التركيب من زجاج أزرق فاتح. ويلي الوحدة المستطيلة ثلاثة مربعات متساوية الأحجام. المربعان الطرفيان متطابقان وتتوسط كل منهما نجمة ثمانية الأضلاع، وهما مقسمان إلى قطاعات صغيرة ومغطيان بزجاج من الألوان الأحمر الداكن والأخضر والأصفر. أما المربع الوسطي فيحتوي على معينين، وملئ بزجاج من الألوان الأصفر والأزرق. بعدها ينتقل العنصر الزخرفي إلى ثلاثة مستطيلات طولية. المستطيلان الجانبيان متطابقان، ومزخرفان بخطوط متعرجة متداخلة ومغطاة بزجاج من الألوان الأزرق والأحمر الداكن والأصفر. أما المستطيل الوسطي، فيأخذ شكل زهرية ينطلق منها نبتة متشابكة تلتف ثلاث لفات شبه مستديرة وتتوج بتاج نباتي. وينتهي الشباك بثلاثة مربعات متساوية الحجم تشبه المربعات المذكورة سابفاً.  
  
يتم تحضير الشبابيك الجصية المعشقة بالزجاج على عدة مراحل تتضمن أولاً تحضير إطار من خشب متين يكيَّف تماماً على شكل ومقاسات الشباك المراد صنعه. بعد ذلك، يسكب الجص السائل داخل الإطار الخشبي ويترك في الظل حتى يجف تماماً، ثم يرفع ويثبت على تركيبة حديدية. تطبَع الرسومات الزخرفية المراد تنفيذها بكل تفاصيلها على سطح الجص، وذلك بنقلها من ورق شفاف باستعمال إبرة وبرادة الرصاص. ثم تبدأ عملية الحفر على الجص يدوياً باستعمال أدوات حادة وبدقة متناهية حتى لا يتضرر الشباك لأن الجص هش للغاية. ويكون الحفر بدرجة ميل 45% تسمح للضوء الساقط على الشباك بالوصول إلى وسطه، خاصة وأن الشبابيك هذه تثبت في الغالب على ارتفاعات عالية. بعد الانتهاء بنجاح من عملية الحفر، يتم لصق قطع الزجاج الملون على الفتحات من الخلف، وتستخدم ألوان مميزة من الزجاج تتماشى والشكل المراد إنتاجه. وأخيراً، ينقل الشباك من المشغل إلى المكان المراد تثبيته فيه. ويستغرق العمل في إنتاج مثل هذا الشباك من ستة أشهر إلى اثني عشر شهراً.

شبّاك جصّي من المسجد الأقصى، مُقسَّم إلى 11 وحدة زخرفية، اعتمدت على الأشكال النباتية والهندسية والكتابية، تظهر كل وحدة بشكل مستقل، كما تظهر كل الوحدات كوحدة واحدة، مجتمعة بإطار خشبي، يجمع التنوُّع الكبير في شكل الزخارف، وألوانها المتعددة.
keywords: جص؛ زجاج ملون؛ زخرفة نباتية؛ زخرفة هندسية؛ المسجد الأقصى.

en.name: Stucco stained-glass window.
description:
A stucco stained-glass window divided into 21 decorative units of vegetal and geometric motifs and inscriptions. The first unit is composed of a circular “flower” that complements and forms the arch, and which is adorned with a colourful geometric decoration in yellow, turquoise and dark-red glass. Adjacent to this area is a rectangular zone which contains the only inscription on the window. This is a verse from the Qur'an \[“al-Tawba”\] (“the Repentance”, 9: 18), which reads: “In the Cause of Allah, They are not comparable in the sight of Allah.” The inscription is carved in an interlaced script of white glass. The surrounding space is filled with simple squares of light-blue glass. Adjacent to the inscription are three squares of equal size. The two side squares are identical, and in the middle of each of them there is an eight-sided star. Both are divided into small pieces of dark-red, green and yellow glass. The middle square contains two polygons of yellow and blue glass; the decorative component transfers thereafter to three long rectangles. The two side rectangles are identical and are decorated with intertwining zigzag lines of blue, yellow and dark-red glass. The middle rectangle takes the form of a flower, out of which emerges an intertwining plant that wraps around three times to resemble a circle, and which is topped by a crown formed from vegetal motifs. The window terminates with three squares that are identical in size, and which resemble those mentioned earlier.  
The manufacture of stucco windows inset with stained glass requires a number of stages. The first stage is the preparation of a solid wooden frame to contain the finished window. Liquid plaster is then poured into the frame and left to dry completely. The window is then placed on an iron mount where an imprint of the decoration is made on the surface of the plaster. This can be done by transferring the design from a sheet of tracing paper with the use of a needle and lead filings, and then using a cutting tool. The carving is done directly on to the plaster by hand with the use of precision tools. The work is extremely exacting as the plaster is fragile, making the window vulnerable to damage. The carving is done at a level of deflection of 45 per cent, allowing light to fall at the centre of the mosque hall. The glass is slotted into the empty spaces from the back. Finally, the window is transferred from the workshop to the site where it is mounted. To produce a window such as this would take between nine and 12 months.

This stucco window from al-Aqsa Mosque is divided into 11 decorative elements derived from vegetal, geometric and epigraphic forms. The independent elements appear as a collective unit within a wooden frame, which gathers a multiplicity of decorative forms in a number of colours.
holder: Islamic Museum, al-Aqsa Mosque / al-Haram al-Sharif.
keywords: Stucco; stained-glass; vegetal decoration; geometric decoration; mosque interior decoration

es.name: Vidriera de estuco.
description:
Ventana de estuco con vidriera dividida en 21 unidades decorativas con motivos vegetales y geométricos e inscripciones. La primera unidad presenta una “flor” circular dentro de un arco, adornado con motivos geométricos de color amarillo, turquesa y rojo oscuro. Justo debajo hay una sección rectangular que contiene la única inscripción de la ventana, una aleya de la sura “Al-Tawba” ('El arrepentimiento', 9:19). Dice así: “Por la causa de Allah. No son comparables a los ojos de Allah”. La inscripción está formada por letras entrelazadas de vidrio blanco y el espacio que tiene alrededor está decorado con pequeños cuadrados azul claro. Bajo la inscripción hay tres cuadrados de igual tamaño. Los dos laterales son idénticos y tienen en el centro una estrella de ocho puntas. Ambos están divididos en pequeñas piezas de vidrio rojo oscuro, verde y amarillo. El cuadrado central presenta dos polígonos de vidrio amarillo y azul. La composición ornamental continúa con tres rectángulos largos. Los dos laterales son idénticos y están adornados con líneas en zigzag entrelazadas de vidrio azul, amarillo y rojo oscuro. El rectángulo central adopta la forma de una flor de la que sale una planta entrelazada que se enrosca tres veces, coronada con motivos vegetales. La composición de la ventana se cierra con tres cuadrados de tamaño idéntico, similares a los anteriores.  
La producción de vidrieras con estructura de estuco consta de varias etapas. Primero se fabrica un armazón de madera resistente que soportará la ventana terminada. En segundo lugar, se vierte escayola líquida sobre el marco y se deja secar totalmente. Después, se coloca la ventana sobre un soporte de hierro y se traza la decoración en la escayola; para ello, normalmente se copia el diseño con una hoja de papel de calco, aguja e hilos de plomo y, después, se recorta. A continuación, se talla a mano directamente sobre la escayola, utilizando herramientas de precisión, ya que se trata de un material frágil. La talla se realiza con una inclinación del 45%, lo que permite que la luz entre dirigida al centro de la mezquita. Más tarde, el cristal se inserta en los huecos desde la parte de atrás. Por último, la ventana se traslada desde el taller al lugar donde estará ubicada. Este proceso puede durar entre nueve y doce meses.

Ventana de estuco de la Mezquita al-Aqsa, dividida en once elementos decorativos derivados de formas vegetales, geométricas y epigráficas. Los elementos independientes aparecen como una unidad dentro del marco de madera, que conjunta una multiplicidad de formas decorativas de variado colorido.
dates: Siglo XII de la Hégira / XVIII d. C.
keywords: Estuco; decoración vegetal; decoración geométrica; ventana.
materials: Madera, estuco y vidrio de colores.
tags: Madera, estuco y vidrio de colores.
partner: Museo islámico en la mezquita de Al-Aqsa

fr.name: Fenêtre en stuc à verres de couleur.
description:
Fenêtre en stuc à verres de couleur divisée en 21 éléments décoratifs composés de motifs végétaux et géométriques et d'une inscription. La première partie comprend une rosace insérée dans l'arc en plein cintre. Elle présente un riche décor de morceaux de verre de couleur turquoise, jaune et rouge foncé. Au-dessous figure une importante zone rectangulaire horizontale qui contient la seule inscription de l'ensemble consistant en un verset du Coran tiré de la sourate “al-Tauba” (La repentance, IX, 18) : “Pour la cause d'Allah, Ils ne sont pas comparables à la vue d'Allah.” Le texte est en verre transparent. L'espace qui l'entoure est meublé de carrés en verre bleu clair. Cette inscription repose sur un rectangle composé de trois carrés de dimensions identiques. Les deux parties latérales sont également identiques et comportent en leur centre une étoile à huit branches en verre rouge foncé, vert et jaune. Le carré central contient deux polygones en verre jaune et bleu. En partie inférieure, le décor se répartit en trois rectangles verticaux. Les rectangles latéraux identiques sont décorés de lignes en zigzag enlacées en verre bleu, jaune et rouge foncé. Le rectangle central est meublé d'une composition végétale de trois cercles surmontés d'un couronnement à motif floral. L'ensemble s'achève en partie inférieure par trois carrés de dimensions identiques et de décor semblable à celui des précédents.  
La fabrication des fenêtres en stuc à inserts de verre de couleur suit un certain nombre d'étapes. La première est la préparation d'un solide cadre de bois qui contiendra l'objet fini. Un plâtre liquide est versé dans ce cadre et laissé à sécher. La fenêtre est alors placée sur une monture métallique et une empreinte des motifs décoratifs est pratiquée à la surface du plâtre par transfert du dessin à partir d'une feuille de papier transparent et par le recours à une aiguille et un remplissage de plomb, puis un outil à découper. Le travail demande une grande précision car le plâtre reste fragile. La découpe est effectuée selon un angle de 45° pour que la lumière traversant la fenêtre atteigne le milieu de la salle de la mosquée. Le verre est glissé dans les espaces évidés par l'arrière, puis la fenêtre est transférée de l'atelier vers le site où elle doit être mise en place. Produire une fenêtre de ce type pouvait prendre de 9 à 12 mois.

Fenêtre en stuc de la mosquée al-Aqsa divisée en 21 éléments décoratifs dérivés de formes végétales, géométriques et épigraphiques. Les éléments indépendants forment un tout à l’intérieur d’un cadre en bois, qui rassemble une multiplicité de formes décoratives dans de nombreuses couleurs.
holder: Musée islamique, mosquée al-Aqsa / Haram al-Charif.
dates: XIIe siècle de l’Hégire (XVIIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: Stuc ; vitraux ; décoration végétale ; décoration géométrique
materials: Bois, plâtre (stuc) et verres de couleur ; moulage, sculpture et assemblage.
tags: Bois, plâtre (stuc) et verres de couleur

cs.name: *Uctívání Pallas Athény*
description:
Sochu bohyně moudrosti Pallas Athény na oltáři věnčí jedna skupina puttů  girlandou, zatímco jejich druhové sypou kadidlo do obětní nádoby se zápalnou obětí. Kresba vychází z několikaletého pobytu Paula Trogera v Itálii, kdy malíř mj. spolu s Martinem van Meytens „*studovali s tak neustálou pilnosti antické památky v okolí Říma, že se velmi často celé dny spokojili pouze s chlebem a vodou, aby mohli ve svém studiu nerušenì pokračovat*“. Jako bezprostřední předlohu pro ústřední motiv si malíř zvolil sochu Pallas Athény, která byla součástí proslulé sbírky antik markýze Vincenza Giustinianiho (dnes Řím, Musei Vaticani). Podoba této sochy byla známa i z grafického přepisu z r. 1631 a  
z obrazových publikací o antických sochařských památkách. Podobné téma jako na brněnské kresbě zpracoval Paul Troger také v leptu, jehož vznik v roce 1724 spadá do doby malířova římského pobytu. Trogerův lept i brněnská kresba připomínají ryteckou techniku benátských peintre-graveur, využívajících pro modelaci a postižení světelných přechodů jemnou síť šrafur, zejména významného představitele malířství settecenta Giovanni Battisty Tiepola (1696–1770).  
Téma oslavy bohyně moudrosti souvisí s dobovým rostoucím důrazem na vzdělanost. Trogerova nedokončená  kresba měla patrně sloužit jako předloha pro Moudrost oslavující grafický list. Hlavní motiv je detailně propracován, zatímco doprovodné figury puttů a krajinné pozadí zůstaly jen načrtnuty tužkou. Průběžné vlnovkovité šrafury svědčí o rychlé a expresivní kresbě malíře, který jako vlivný profesor vídeňské akademie patří mezi hlavní osobnosti středoevropské malby 18. století.

Kresba znázorňující sochu bohyně moudrosti Pallas Athény vychází  
z několikaletého pobytu Paula Trogera v Itálii, kde malíř studoval antické památky. Svým charakterem připomíná ryteckou techniku benátských peintre-graveur. Téma oslavy bohyně moudrosti souvisí s dobovým rostoucím důrazem na vzdělanost.
keywords: antika; settecento
materials: Kresba perem a hnědým inkoustem, papír
tags: Kresba perem a hnědým inkoustem, papír

en.name: *The Worship of Pallas Athene*
description: The scene shows a statue of Pallas Athene, goddess of wisdom, on an altar. A group of *putti* are garlanding the statue, while their companions pour incense into an offering vessel. The drawing was inspired by Paul Troger's time in Italy, a period of several years. Together with Martin van Meytens among others, he “studied ancient monuments in the vicinity of Rome with such unceasing diligence that very often we only made do, for days, with bread and water in order to continue with our study without disturbance”. The artist modelled the central motif on a statue of Pallas Athene from the famous collection of ancient art assembled by Marquis Vincenzo Giustiniani (now in the Vatican Museum, Rome). The statue was also known from a print of 1631 and from pictorial publications on ancient sculpture. Paul Troger employed a subject similar to the Brno drawing in an etching from 1724, the origin of which is provably associated with the artist's stay in Rome. Troger's etching and the Brno drawing resemble the engraving technique of Venetian *peintre-graveur*, using a fine grid for the modelling and to capture transitions in light. Typical examples may be found in the work of Giovanni Battista Tiepolo (1696–1770), a major exponent of Italian *Settecento* painting. The subject of adoration of the goddess of wisdom reflects the growing emphasis placed on education at the time. Troger's unfinished drawing probably served as a template for a print celebrating Wisdom. The principal motif is worked up in detail, while the accompanying figures of *putti* and the landscape in the background are sketched in pencil. Continuous wavy lines give evidence of a swift and expressive drawing manner. The artist was an influential professor of the Vienna Academy and was a leading Central European painter of the 18th century.

The drawing of a statue of Pallas Athene was inspired by Paul Troger's long stay in Italy. Its execution resembles Venetian *peintre-graveur*. The unfinished drawing was probably to serve as a template for a print celebrating Wisdom.
keywords: Antiquity; *Settecento*; drawing; mitology; engraving; education
materials: Pen and brown ink on paper
tags: Pen and brown ink on paper

en.name: Variation of the Basmala
description: This work is made of patterned teal silk with mounted calligraphy on paper. The Arabic calligraphy in black ink forms a central abstract pattern, its shape reminiscent of a tulip. The title of the work appears in black ink on the left, above two red seals. A third red seal appears on the top right.
materials: Ink and red seal colour on rice paper, mounted on silk
tags: Ink and red seal colour on rice paper, mounted on silk
partner: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums

en.name: Chapel of Nossa Senhora da Visitação
description: The centre of a regional pilgrimage, the chapel was initially situated on the outskirts of the town, but nowadays it is completely integrated into the urban grid.There is nothing of the Late Gothic visible in the exterior, other than a fine and distinctly Baroque portal, dating from about 1515.The structure inside has magnificent vaulting mainly in the chancel, in a very advanced style with curved ribs, typical of those that were used from about the third decade of the 16th century onwards.

en.name: General View of the Interior and three lateral chapels
description: General view of the single-nave interior with three of the four lateral “Lady” chapels: Chapel of Our Lady of Glory (the *Apocalypse* in low relief in the tympanum), Chapel of Our Lady of Conception and the Chapel of Our Lady of Assistance, all of which have gilt-wood retables.
artist: Architects: Mateus do Couto (“uncle”; active 1660), Carlos Baptista Garvo stone carvers: António Pereira, Vicente Soares, Manuel Rodrigues; woodcarvers: António Martins Calheiros, António Luís, Claude Laprade, Manuel Álvares [dates unknown]
partner: Institute for the Administration of Architectural and Archaeological Heritage -  IGESPAR

pt.name: Vista geral do interior e três capelas laterais
description: Vista geral do interior de nave única e três das quatro capelas laterais dedicadas a Nossa Senhora: Capela de Nossa Senhora da Glória (contendo no tímpano um baixo relevo alusivo ao Apocalipse), Capela de Nossa Senhora da Conceição e Capela de Nossa Senhora do Socorro, todas elas em talha dourada.
artist: Arquitecto: Mateus do Couto (tio, activo 1660); Carlos Baptista Garvo; canteiros: António Pereira, Vicente Soares e Manuel Rodrigues; entalhadores: António Martins Calheiros e António Luís; Manuel Álvares, Claude Laprade. Datas desconhecidas.

en.name: Photograph: *Arabic School, Learning the Koran, Egypt*
description:
Stereoscopic photography that creates the illusion of depth of field from two apparently identical images mounted on a rigid board by using a specific viewfinder, or stereoscope.  
The arrival of Islam to Africa caused the birth of schools where the Qu'ran was taught in Arabic. Probably Islamic education was the first education system introduced in African populations. Islam establishes education as a key priority for children.  
Universities, *madrasas* (organised institutions with different levels for studying Islamic religion), and Qur'anic schools (first education that children receive) are used by Islam as educational institutions and have played an important role in spreading Islamic religious, social, moral and cultural values between African populations.  
In the *madrasas* and Qur'anic schools, the Qur'an is learned and memorised by reading and writing at a wooden table. The memorization of the Qur'an is done by copying the teacher a text written on paper, and later recited aloud until memorised. Students were not allowed to pass to another passage until the current passage had been memorized.
keywords: Photography; education; Egypt; scenes of life

en.name: *Bust of Cardinal Domenico Ginnasi*
description:
In 1911 the bust was found in the Carmelite Convent at the Church of Santa Maria della Vittoria, relocated from the Church of SS. Pietro e Marcellino, the seat of the Teresian Nuns. The nuns moved there in 1757, from the convent founded after the death of Domenico Ginnasi in Palazzo Ginnasi in 1639, and they took the bust with them, having always identified it as a portrait of the cardinal.  
The work was first attributed to both Bernini and Algardi, before being linked to Giuliano Finelli following comparison with the bust the sculptor made for the cardinal for his funeral monument at S. Lucia dei Ginnasi (the decoration is based on a design by Lanfranco, whose daughter married Finelli).  
The sculptor worked with Bernini on several occasions, notably on *Apollo and Daphne* in the Galleria Borghese and the baldachin (large sculpted bronze canopy over the altar) of Saint Peter's. He worked alone from 1629 and joined Rome's artistic circle thanks to the numerous contacts that he was able to make, notably Pietro da Cortona, who in turn introduced him to the Sacchetti family, well known patrons.  
His style is characterised by attention to detail, intense skill and psychological depth, but always retaining spontaneity and immediacy, a peculiarity of Bernini's so-called “talking portrait”. The partially unbuttoned *mozzetta* (a short elbow length cape worn by Catholic clergy), the kindly and informal face and the realistic lines are clear evidence of this style.  
In relation to this, a *Bust of Cardinal Scipione Borghese* made by Finelli and currently in the Metropolitan Museum of New York, was sculpted at the same time as the Bernini version (1632). In 1634 Finelli moved to Naples, where he developed a portrait style closer to Parthenopean and Spanish taste, preferring distant, official, commemorative portraits. However in the work undertaken at this time for Roman clients, he never completely abandoned his refined virtuosity and keen psychological study, as can be seen in the bust of Cardinal Ginnasi, sculpted in 1639.

A pupil of Bernini, Finelli focused his attention on the particular rather than the whole. This tendency prevented Finelli from being a great statuary artist, although it enabled him to evolve a striking flair for portraiture.
place: Carmelite Convent in Santa Maria della Vittoria
keywords: Bust; marble; portrait; Bernini; Algardi; patronage; talking portrait

it.name: *Busto del Cardinale Domenico Ginnasi*
description:
Il busto fu rintracciato nel 1911 nel convento dei carmelitani presso la chiesa di S. Maria della Vittoria, dove si trovava a seguito dello spostamento dalla chiesa dei SS. Pietro e Marcellino, sede delle monache Teresiane. Queste si erano trasferite lì nel 1757, provenienti dal monastero fondato dopo la morte di Domenico Ginnasi in Palazzo Ginnasi nel 1639, e si erano portate dietro il busto, che avevano sempre identificato come ritratto del cardinale.  
L'opera che era stata precedentemente attribuita sia a Bernini che all'Algardi, è stata ascritta a Giuliano Finelli grazie anche al confronto con il busto che lo scultore aveva realizzato del cardinale per il suo monumento funerario a S. Lucia dei Ginnasi (la decorazione è su disegno di Lanfranco, di cui Finelli sposò la figlia).  
Lo scultore collaborò in diverse occasioni con Bernini; si ricordano in particolare l'esecuzione dell'*Apollo e Dafne* della Galleria Borghese e il *Baldacchino* di S. Pietro. Dal 1629 gestì la propria attività in modo autonomo e ben si inserì nel circuito artistico romano, grazie alle molte conoscenze che riuscì a realizzare (si ricorda tra gli altri,  Pietro da Cortona che a sua volta lo introdusse alla famiglia Sacchetti, noti committenti).  
Caratterizzano il suo stile l'attenzione al particolare, l'intenso virtuosismo e la profondità psicologica, pur mantenendo viva la spontaneità e l'immediatezza, peculiarità del cosiddetto “ritratto parlante” berniniano. La mozzetta parzialmente sbottonata, il viso bonario e colloquiale, i lineamenti realistici, ne sono una prova evidente.  
A tal proposito si cita un *busto del Cardinale Scipione Borghese* realizzato da Finelli, oggi al  Metropolitan Museum di New York, scolpito all'incirca negli stessi anni delle versioni di Bernini (1632). Nel 1634 Finelli si trasferì a Napoli, dove definì una ritrattistica più vicina al gusto partenopeo e spagnolo, prediligendo il “distante” ritratto ufficiale e celebrativo. Nelle opere di quegli stessi anni, destinate invece alla committenza romana, non abbandonò mai del tutto i raffinati virtuosismi e l'acuta indagine psicologica, come è possibile notare appunto nel busto del cardinal Ginnasi, realizzato nel 1639.

Allievo di Bernini, Finelli focalizzò la sua attenzione più sul particolare che non sull'effetto totale dell'opera. Questo impedì a Finelli di diventare un grande artista della statuaria, sebbene ciò gli ha permesso di evolvere verso un sorprendente gusto per la ritrattistica.
place: Convento dei Carmelitani in Santa Maria della Vittoria
keywords: Busto; marmo; ritratto; Algardi; Bernini; mecenatismo; ritratto parlante

ar.name: لوحة لامرأة
description:
تصور اللوحة امرأة شابة من الطبقة النبيلة وهي ترتدي ألبسة أنيقة وتتشح بمعالم الغنى بمجموعة من المجوهرات. وبينما يبدو من النظرة الأولى يبدو العمل جميلا وناجحا فإن العديد من الأخطاء والتناقضات تصبح ظاهرة فيه عن التدقيق عن كثب.  
بواسطة الاختيار الماهر للألوان فإن الإظهار المدقق للتفاصيل والتركيب الزخرفي الفعال يمكن أن نلاحظ عن قرب أكثر أن المرأة موضوعة في نوع من الخيام والذي عمقه يظهر بشكل ضعيف بواسطة حجاب. وشكل الفناة نفسه مجسد بدون عمق. والوجه الظاهر بنسبة ثلاثة أرباعه مستدير لليسار والجسم يرى من الأمام بينما القدمين هما من حيث الشكل مفتولتان للأمام. والصورة مشكَّلة بعناصرها المفردة بشكل غير طبيعي وهذا يبدو دون معرفة التشريح او المنظور. وعن طريق هذه التنافرات يظهر العمل نفسه كقطعة متأثرة بالفن الغربي الذي حاول أن يجربه فنان شرقي(أي تجريب الفن الغربي) بدون أن يعرفه بالعمق. وكل من التقنية(الزيت على كنفا) والموضوع ( لوحة شخصية) تشير إلى أن التقاليد هذه غريبة عن الثقافة المحلية.
dates: القرن الثاني عشر – الثالث عشر هجري / القرن الثامن عشر – التاسع عشر ميلادي
partner: متحف الحضارات | متحف الفن الشرقي جوزيبي توتشي

en.name: Painting with female figure
description: The painting depicts a young noblewoman, elegantly dressed and richly embellished with a variety of jewels. While at first glance the work is pleasant and successful, many inconsistencies are apparent upon closer inspection. With a skilful choice of colours, a refined rendering of details and an effective decorative composition, we can more closely observe that the woman is placed in a type of pavilion, whose depth is only weakly indicated by a veil. The figure of the girl herself is rendered without depth. The three-quarter face is turned to the left, the body is seen from the front, while the feet are in profile, turned to the right. The image is constructed with its singular elements in an unnatural way, seemingly without any knowledge of anatomy or perspective. Through these dissonances the work reveals itself to be an object influenced by Western art, which the artist tried to orient himself (i.e., to Western art) without knowing it in depth. Both the technique (oil on canvas) and the subject (a portrait) refer to traditions that are foreign to the local culture.
holder: Museum of Civilizations / Eastern Art Museum
partner: Museum of Civilisations | Museum of Oriental Art (EIAC)

it.name: Dipinto con figura femminile
description: Il quadro raffigura una giovane nobile, elegantemente vestita e riccamente abbellita con gioielli di vario tipo. Mentre l’opera risulta nell’insieme piacevole e riuscita, rivela ad un secondo sguardo, più ravvicinato ed attento, numerose incongruenze. Accanto ad una sapiente scelta cromatica dei colori e una raffinata resa dei dettagli con un buon senso della composizione decorativa, osserviamo difatti che la donna è collocata in una specie di padiglione, la cui tridimensionalità è solo debolmente indicata da un velario. La figura della fanciulla stessa è resa senza profondità. Il viso di tre quarti è volto verso sinistra, il corpo è visto frontalmente, mentre i piedi sono di profilo, girati verso destra. L’immagine è costruita dai singoli elementi assemblati in modo disorganico (senza una versa conoscenza dell’anatomia né della prospettiva). Sono proprio queste dissonanze che tradiscono nell’opera una realizzazione condizionata da un predominante influsso dell’arte occidentale, a cui l’artista ha cercato di orientarsi senza conoscerla a fondo. Sia la tecnica (olio su tela) sia il soggetto (un ritratto) rimandano difatti a tradizioni estranee alla cultura locale.
holder: Museo delle Civiltà/Museo d’arte orientale „Giuseppe Tucci“
partner: Museo delle Civiltà | Museo d’arte orientale “Giuseppe Tucci”

en.name: Mosque of Nabi al-‘Is
description:
The village of Sa‘ir stretches today over a vast area; to reach its Mamluk mosque, therefore, one has to go through the modern parts of the village, toward the centre, where the Mosque of Nabi al-‘Is (Esau), the son of Isaac, son of Jacob, son of Ibraham, lies.  
The historical sources refer to a mosque that was built in the Mamluk period to commemorate the prophet, who holds an important place in the local Hebron heritage. The first two generations of Abraham’s descendants were buried in Hebron, while the grandson was buried here in Sa‘ir. The exact date of construction of this *maqam* is not known, but it is almost certain that it is the first mosque to be built here and probably dates back to the early Islamic period.  
A large, modern mosque was recently built on top of the Mamluk one to accommodate all the worshippers of the village.  
Nothing is left of the Mamluk building except for the southern and western façades, but these remains are negligible when the impressive architecture of the period is considered. Rather, these two parts of the façade were built in the local traditional style: the masonry was crudely cut, no coloured stones were used, and no decorations or inscriptions were employed. The cenotaph and the tomb chamber were left untouched.  
The shrine is reached from the west via a small door on the second floor of the mosque. There is a rectangular room (approximately 20 m. × 7 m.) just before it, which consists of a portico that has three cross vaults to the north of the tomb chamber. A simple and small *mihrab* is found inside it, which is likely to be the original one. The western side of the room is semi-closed and provides a retreat for *sufi*s.  
In this hall, prayers are held and Qur’anic verses read whilst looking into the cenotaph through a window. The cenotaph chamber can also be seen from the mosque that lies to the east. At the centre of the chamber – covered by a 10 m. long flattened barrel-vault – the cenotaph is also covered in green cloth.

es.name: Mezquita Nabi al-‘Is
description:
El pueblo de Sa‘ir se levanta sobre una amplia superficie; para llegar a su mezquita hay que atravesar los barrios modernos del pueblo en dirección al centro, donde se encuentra la mezquita de Nabi al-‘Is (Esaú), hermano de Jacob e hijo de Isaac, hijo este de Abraham.  
Las fuentes históricas mencionan una mezquita construida en época mameluca para conmemorar al profeta, cuya figura ocupa un lugar importante en la tradición local de Hebrón. Las dos primeras generaciones de descendientes de Abraham fueron enterradas en Hebrón, pero el otro nieto, Esaú (al-‘Is) fue sepultado en esta ciudad. No se sabe cuándo se construyó el *maqam*, aunque es prácticamente seguro que se trata de la primera mezquita levantada en Sa‘ir, probablemente en la época temprana del Islam.  
Recientemente se ha construido una gran mezquita moderna, para dar cabida a todos los fieles del pueblo, en el emplazamiento de la mezquita mameluca, de la cual solo se han conservado las dos fachadas sur y oeste. Pero estos restos carecen de interés al compararlos con la impresionante arquitectura de la época; entre las piedras, bastamente talladas, no hay ninguna de color ni rastro de decoraciones o inscripciones. El cenotafio y la cámara funeraria son de origen.  
Al mausoleo se accede por una pequeña puerta abierta en el lado oeste de la primera planta de la mezquita. Se entra primero en una sala rectangular (de aproximadamente 20 × 7 m), formada por un pórtico con tres bóvedas por arista al norte de la cámara funeraria. En el interior de esta estancia hay un modesto *mihrab*, probablemente el original. La zona oeste de esta sala está parcialmente cerrada y proporciona a los sufíes la posibilidad de aislarse.  
En esta sala se puede rezar y leer los versículos del Corán, mientras se observa el cenotafio a través de una ventana. También puede verse el mausoleo desde la mezquita que se eleva al este. Al centro de la cámara funeraria —rematada por una bóveda de cañón algo rebajada y de una longitud de casi 10 m— se encuentra el cenotafio, también cubierto con una tela de color verde.

fr.name: Mosquée Nabi al-‘Is
description:
Le village de Sa‘ir s’étend aujourd’hui sur une vaste superficie; c’est pourquoi, pour arriver à la mosquée, il faut traverser les quartiers modernes de la bourgade pour atteindre le centre où l’on trouvera la mosquée de Nabi al-‘Is (Esaü), le frère de Jacob fils d’Isaac, Isaac étant lui-même le fils d’Abraham.  
Les sources historiques citent une mosquée édifiée à l’époque mamelouke pour commémorer le prophète, qui tient une place majeure dans la tradition locale d’Hébron. Les deux premières générations des descendants d’Abraham ont été enterrées à Hébron, tandis que l’autre petit-fils, Esaü (al- ‘Is) fut enterré ici même. Nous ne connaissons pas exactement la date de construction du *maqam*, mais il est presque certain qu’il s’agit de la première mosquée construite à Sa‘ir ; elle remonterait probablement au début de la période islamique.  
Afin de pouvoir accueillir tous les fidèles du village, une grande mosquée moderne a été construite récemment à l’emplacement de la mosquée mamelouke, dont ne subsistent que les deux façades méridionale et occidentale, mais ces vestiges sont sans intérêt au regard de l’impressionnante architecture de l’époque: l’appareil de pierres grossièrement taillées ne présente pas la moindre pierre de couleur et se trouve dépourvu de toute décoration ou inscription. Le cénotaphe et la chambre funéraire sont d’origine.  
On accède au mausolée par une petite porte percée dans le côté occidental au premier étage de la mosquée. On pénètre d’abord dans une pièce rectangulaire (environ 20 m de long sur 7 m de large), qui consiste en un portique présentant trois voûtes d’arêtes au nord de la chambre funéraire. Un modeste *mihrab*, probablement celui d’origine, se trouve à l’intérieur. Le côté occidental de la salle est partiellement fermé et permet aux soufis de s’isoler.  
C’est dans cet espace qu’on accomplit les prières, qu’on lit des versets du Coran, tout en portant le regard sur le cénotaphe à travers une fenêtre. Le mausolée peut également être vu depuis la mosquée qui s’élève à l’est.Au centre de la chambre funéraire – couverte d’une voûte en plein cintre légèrement surbaissée et longue d’une dizaine de mètres – se trouve le cénotaphe, lui aussi drapé d’un tissu de couleur verte.

en.name: Ewer (*Aftaba*)
description: A ewer, adorned with vegetal motifs and geometric designs, composed of a base, body, neck, mouth, lid, handle and spout. The base is circular, with a lobed contour and ornamented with arrowheads using the chasing technique. The body is spherical and lobed. Each lobe is ornamented with a meandering vegetal branch, while the field is adorned with rosettes of four petals in varying sizes. The neck is short, circular and lobed, beginning with a plain metallic band, followed by a frieze of arrowheads. The circular mouth is covered with a hemispherical helmet-shaped lid, topped by a small spherical knob entirely undecorated. The spout is cylindrical, beveled, and tapering towards the tip, narrowing upwards, with a central protrusion. It is adorned with longitudinal framed motifs of arrowheads, beginning with a row of broken arches. The handle is curved, extending from the middle of the body and ending in a lotus flower, attached to the lid by hinges fixed with circular pins.

en.name: Military Infirmary
description: This hospital (or *hastahane* in Ottoman Turkish), commissioned by Sultan 'Abd al-'Aziz (Abdülaziz) (1861-76) in 1865, was often referred to as the military infirmary. The building included two wings, and the northern wing housed a drugstore (*ajzah*). The courthouse which later inhabited the building was moved to a different location when it became the Lebanese University's Institute of Fine Arts.
history: In 1865, this military hospital was commissioned by the Ottoman sultan 'Abd al-'Aziz (Abdülaziz).The hospital was later converted to a courthouse by the French, who took control of the city in 1918 following the collapse of the Ottoman Empire. Today, the building houses the Lebanese University's Institute of Fine Arts.

de.name: Rathaus der Stadt Augsburg
description:
Eine Besonderheit des Augsburger Rathauses bildet seine bis dato nur bei Kirchen gebräuchliche Doppelturmfassade. Zum bedeutungsvollen Fassadenschmuck zählen außerdem das Säulenportal sowie der Schweifgiebel, der mit der römischen Zirbelnuss des Stadtwappens und dem Doppeladler des Kaiserwappens die einstige Reichsunmittelbarkeit der Stadt signalisiert.  
Die Dreiteilung der Fassade bildet die venezianischen Palästen folgende Raumdisposition ab: Außen befinden sich die Verwaltungs- und Fürstenzimmer, wobei die mit Zwiebelhauben bekrönten Türme die Treppenhäuser überhöhen, und mittig die repräsentativen Säle. Durch die Hanglage weist der Bau vorne sieben und hinten neun Einzelgeschosse auf.  
Im Mittelteil liegen drei Säle übereinander, die ihrer Bedeutung gemäß höhenmäßig gestaffelt sind: Das Erdgeschoss nimmt der Untere Fletz ein, eine Halle mit Marmorpfeilern und Gewölbedecke. Es folgt im ersten Hauptgeschoss der Obere Fletz, eine einst niedrige Säulenhalle mit Kassettendecke, deren Anräume die Amts- und Sitzungszimmer der Ratsgremien beherbergten. Im zweiten Hauptgeschoss befindet sich schließlich der über drei Fenstergeschosse reichende Goldene Saal, der als Festsaal mit seinen sechs Prunkportalen, den Wandmalereien und der prachtvollen Kassettendecke den raumkünstlerischen Höhepunkt bildet. Daran grenzen in den Ecken vier sogenannte Fürstenzimmer an.  
Wie das über Decke und Wände verteilte allegorische Bildprogramm verrät, war der Goldene Saal als Tagungsort für Reichstage konzipiert, von denen aber nie einer darin stattfand. Appellativ zeigt daher das Mittelbild der Decke den Triumphzug der Weisheit; lateinische Inschriften verkünden das Motto: “Durch mich herrschen die Herrscher”. Zwei kreisförmige szenische Rundbilder und acht ovale mit weiblichen Personifikationen flankieren das Mittelbild. In dem einen kreisrunden Gemälde ist das Rathaus im Bau und der Baumeister Elias Holl mit dessen Grundriss zu sehen, wozu das Spruchband sinngemäß meint: “Städte werden gegründet”. Die dazu nötigen Grundlagen: Bildung, Fruchtbarkeit, Fleiß und Frömmigkeit, beschwören die umgebenden vier Ovalbilder. Im anderen kreisrunden Gemälde ist die Wehrhaftigkeit Augsburgs thematisiert, auf einem Spruchband steht sinngemäß zu lesen: “Feinde werden abgewehrt”. Auch dieses ist von vier ovalen Bildern umgeben, die allegorisch Heilkunst, Redlichkeit, Gerechtigkeit und Wohlstand verbildlichen. Fresken an den Wänden stellen römisch antike und deutsche Kaiser dar.

Das 1615 begonnene doppeltürmige Rathaus der ehem. Freien Reichsstadt Augsburg ist eine bautechnische Pionierleistung, da es seinerzeit als das einzige Gebäude der Welt mit mehr als sechs Stockwerken galt. Seine Baugestalt orientiert sich an venezianischen Palästen sowie an den edlen Formen der italienischen Renaissance-Architektur. Ausdruck des Selbstverständnisses der Stadt sind außen die römische Zirbelnuss und der kaiserliche Doppeladler, die den Stolz auf die lange Geschichte und die Reichsunmittelbarkeit symbolisieren, sowie innen der überaus prunkvolle Goldene Saal mit seiner prächtigen Kassettendecke.
artist: Stadtpfleger Hieronymus Imhof und Hans Jakob Rembold
history: 1614 wurde angedacht, das baufällige mittelalterliche Rathaus durch einen repräsentativen Neubau zu ersetzen. Am 25. August 1615 erfolgte hierzu die Grundsteinlegung durch den Stadtbaumeister Elias Holl. Infolge einer Planänderung wurden 1618 die beiden Türme hinzugefügt. 1620 stand der Bau bereits in Benutzung, und sechs Jahre später war die Ausgestaltung des Inneren abgeschlossen. 1944 zerstörte ein Luftangriff das Gebäude bis auf die Außenmauern. Nach anfänglich vereinfachtem Wiederaufbau rekonstruierte man 1980-1984 im Zuge einer Sanierung den Goldenen Saal, das Prunkstück des Rathauses, sowie zwei der ehemals vier Fürstenzimmer.
keywords: Rathaus; Reichsunmittelbarkeit; Imperiale Ikonographie; Palastbau; Tugendallegorien

en.name: The Town Hall of Augsburg
description:
A special feature of the Augsburg Town Hall is the double-tower façade, an element that previously had been exclusively incorporated in churches. Other meaningful front decorations include the columned portal and the scrolled gable, which is equipped with two icons that signify the city’s imperial immediacy: the Roman cembra nut of the municipal coat-of-arms resting above and the double eagle of the Emperor's coat-of-arms in the centre.  
The spatial layout follows the models of Venetian palaces and is defined by the threefold division of the façade: The representative halls form the centre, beside them are administration and *Fürstenzimmer* spaces, in which the onion dome crowned towers surmount the staircases. Due to its hillside location, the building features seven single storeys facing forward and nine storeys in the rear.  
The middle section houses three halls that are staggered vertically according to their meaning: The ground floor is occupied by a vestibule, the so-called “Unterer Fletz”, a hall with marble pillars and a vaulted ceiling. Located in the first main storey is a secondary vestibule, also known as the “Oberer Fletz”, a once low coffered ceilinged hall with columns, whose adjacent rooms contained offices and assembly halls for the council body. Finally, on the second main storey is located the Golden Hall, the highlight of the building's interior design. This ceremonial hall features six portals, wall frescos, splendid coffered ceilings, and extends one row of windows and two clerestories high. Around the corners of the hall are four adjoined *Fürstenzimmer*.  
The allegoric iconography covering the walls and ceiling portray the Golden Hall’s concept as a conference site for the Diets of Augsburg, though such meetings never actually took place there. The ceiling centrepiece appellatively shows the triumphal procession of Sapientia (Wisdom); Latin inscriptions proclaim her motto: “By me rulers reign”. The centrepiece is flanked by two circular scenic tondos and eight oval-shaped paintings featuring female personifications. One of the circular paintings shows the Town Hall under construction and the architect holding the layout plan, to which the banner correspondingly says: “Cities are founded”. The required basic principles for the statement: education, productivity, diligence and piety are invoked by the four surrounding oval paintings. The other circular painting depicts Augsburg’s strength for defence, a banner says: “Foes will be fended off”. This, too, is surrounded by oval paintings, that allegorically visualise medicine, justice and prosperity. Wall frescos depict ancient Roman and German emperors.

With development beginning in 1615, the double-towered town hall of the former free imperial city of Augsburg was a constructional pioneering achievement, because at that time it supposedly was the only building in the world with more than six storeys. Its form follows the models of Venetian palaces and the exquisite shapes of Italian Renaissance architecture. Expression of the municipal identity are the Roman cembra nut and the imperial double eagle residing exteriorly, as well as the magnificent Golden Hall with its splendid coffered ceiling interiorly. They symbolise the pride of the long history and immediacy of the city.
artist: Mayors Hieronymus Imhof and Hans Jakob Rembold
history: In 1614, the dilapidated medieval town hall’s prestigious new construction was under consideration. The laying of the first stone was carried out by municipal architect Elias Holl on 25 August 1615. Due to a change of plans, two towers were added in 1618. Unfinished, the building was already in use in 1620, and the interior decoration was finalised six years later. In 1944, an air raid destroyed the building almost entirely, leaving only its external walls. After an initial simplified rebuilding, the showpiece of the town hall, the Golden Hall, and two of the original four *Fürstenzimmer* (literally “princely rooms”, similar to state rooms; spaces which served to receive German “Fürst”, or leaders of a feudal state) were reconstructed during a renovation between 1980 and 1984.
partner: University of Munich, Institute of Art History

en.name: Islamic Beja
description:
Having enjoyed a brilliant past in Roman and mediaeval times, Beja frequently played an important role in the political evolution of Gharb al-Andalus. On several occasions, the city was the centre of important rebellions against the political hegemony of the large urban centres, such as Cordoba and Seville.  
According to al-Maqqari, the territory of Beja not only possessed a large number of silver mines, but also had the “glory of being the birthplace of al-Mutamid Ibn Abad”. Another author al-Razi, in the *General Chronicle of Spain* in 1344, stated: “Beja is one of the oldest cities in Spain and was built at the time of Julius Caesar, who was the first of the Caesars. And Julius was the first to begin to mark out and divide the land into plots. Beja is a very good and arable land, excellent for the rearing of cattle. And it is a very good land for hives, for there are very good flowers, most excellent for bees. And the water of Beja is naturally good for the tanning of leather. And the city has many good wide streets”.  
Beja’s *Mozarab* community is said to have enjoyed a certain amount of power. This is suggested by the persistence of ancient forms of Christian worship and the work that was undertaken at the Igreja de Santo Amaro, rebuilt or modified in the 4th/10th-5th/11th century.  
From the 5th/11th century onwards, with the increasing importance of Évora and mainly with the territory’s political division into the *Taifa* kingdoms, Beja entered upon a period of sharp decline, so that it is not surprising that the heavily fortified city of Mértola should sporadically have become the regional capital.  
Today, the successive building programmes undertaken in the historical centre have hidden most of the remains of the Islamic City. The most important of these works were certainly those that took place in the 19th century, when extensive areas of the mediaeval city were demolished. The late Islamic horseshoe arch of the castle keep, some epigraphs at the Regional Museum and the odd ceramic piece are the only visible remains of what was once one of the most important cities in Gharb al-Andalus.

es.name: Beja islámica
description:
Ciudad de brillante pasado en las épocas romana y altomedieval, Beja desempeñó un papel de relieve en la evolución política de Garb al-Andalus en diversas ocasiones. La ciudad fue, varias veces, sede de importantes rebeliones que trataron de contrarrestar la hegemonía política de grandes urbes como Córdoba o Sevilla.  
Según al-Maqqari, Beja, además de poseer en su territorio muchas minas de plata, tenía “la gloria de ser la tierra natal de al-Mu‘tamid Ibn Abad”. Otro autor, al-Razi, como transcribe la *Crónica General de España* de 1344, afirmaba: “Beja es una de las antiguas ciudades que hay en España y fue hecha en tiempos de Julio César, que fue el primero de los césares. Y Julio fue el primero que comenzó a cuadrar y partir la tierra. Beja es muy buena tierra y de buena simiente y de muy buena crianza. Es muy buena tierra de colmenas, que hay ahí flores muy buenas y muy provechosas para las abejas. Y el agua de Beja es en su naturaleza buena para el curtido de cueros. Y hay en ella muchas y buenas calles y muy anchas”. La comunidad *mozárabe* de Beja, según se supone, tuvo que conservar cierto poder. Apuntan en ese sentido la persistencia de cultos cristianos antiguos y las obras de que fueron objeto sitios como la iglesia de Santo Amaro, reconstruida o modificada en los siglos IV/X-V/XI.  
A partir del siglo V/XI, con la creciente importancia de Évora y, principalmente, con la fragmentación política de los reinos de *taifa*, la decadencia de Beja se acentuó, por lo que no es de extrañar que la bien fortificada Mértola pasase a ser, temporalmente, capital de la región.  
La memoria de la ciudad islámica está oculta hoy tras las sucesivas intervenciones urbanas obradas en el centro histórico. Las más importantes fueron, sin duda, las habidas en el siglo XIX, época en que se demolieron extensas zonas de la ciudad medieval. El tardío arco de herradura de la torre del homenaje del castillo, unos epigramas del Museo Regional y alguna que otra pieza de cerámica son los vestigios visibles de la que fue una de las ciudades más importantes de Garb al-Andalus.

en.name: Vase
description: Made of blown cobalt blue glass, this vase is painted with polychrome enamel and gilt decoration consisting of horizontal registers of vegetal motifs, calligraphy, and birds. The inscriptions encircling the neck and the body carry the attributes of an unnamed sultan, a form of eulogy commonly found on Syrian objects from the AH 7th / AD 13th century onwards. The precision and detail of the vase’s decoration suggest that it was made in a glass workshop in either Egypt or Syria during the Mamluk period.

en.name: Church of Santa Maria de Marvila
description:
The Church of Santa Maria de Marvila was one of the first to be built in Santarém after the Conquest of 1147, but it was completely rebuilt in Manueline times. Only the east end and a fine portal remain from this period, as further work was carried out on the main vessel of the church, no doubt due to the earthquake of 1531.  
The exuberant naturalistic portal includes architectural elements reminiscent of the Monastery of Batalha. The interior boasts a *triumphal arch* in the chancel and late Gothic vaulting in the main and collateral chapels.  
The fine early Renaissance longitudinal nave arcades are worthy of note, as are the 17th-century tiles, among the best of Lisbon production of the time.

ar.name: زبدية حليب
description: إن شعب المهرة ليسوا شعبا بدويا عادي فقد كانوا يطعمون إبلهم السردين المجفف وكانوا لا يتحدثون العربية. وهم لم يستخدموا الخيام السوداء لكنهم سعوا للحماية وتأمين المأوى تحت الأشجار أو كانوا يعيشون فوق الصخور. و إن ثقافتهم المادية متفرقة. وفي عام 1901 فإن الباحث في الأعراق من فينا فيلهم هاين قضى طفولته وهو يحلم بالسفر مع زوجته ماريا و قد قام بذلك. و قد سافرا من عدن إلى ميناء المكلا في شرق البلاد و لكنهم غادروا فورا بسبب خوفهم على سلامتهم وقد تابعا وصولا إلى قيشن وهي الموقع الرئيسي لبدو المهرة لدراسة لغتهم والتي كان من الصعب معرفتها في ذلك الوقت. وطمعا في فدية فقد وضعهما سلطان المهرة تحت حراسة في بيت و بالرغم من الأوضاع السيئة جدا فإن الزوجين هاين سجلا الأغاني و الخرافات والقصص بلغة شعب المهرة ووثقا ثقافتهم المادية لأول مرة.

en.name: Milking bowl
description: The Mahra are not typical Bedouin people. They feed their camels with dried sardines and they do not speak Arabic. They do not use black tents but seek protection and shelter beneath bushes or overhanging rocks. Their material culture is sparse. In 1901, the Viennese ethnologist Wilhelm Hein fulfilled his childhood dream and travelled on behalf of the Academy of Sciences to Yemen with his wife Marie. They journeyed from Aden to the harbour town of Muqalla in the east of the country, however, they had to  immediately leave because they feared for their safety. They continued to Qishn, the main site of the Mahra Bedouins, to study their language which was hardly known at the time. Hoping for ransom money, the sultan of the Mahra placed both of them under house arrest. Despite extremely adverse conditions, the Heins recorded songs, fables and stories in the language of the Mahra, and documented their material culture for the first time.

en.name: Three fragments of woven fabric decorated with female figures carrying rose water bottles
description: These silk weavings once framed a large blanket with an embroidered middle section and have been remounted to the original fabric sheet. Depicted on the background, which used to be gold, are young women in elegantly curved stance holding rosewater bottles in their arms. Curved blossoming plants emerging from a rise in the ground are visible in the spaces between the figures. The décor is arranged in offset horizontal rows: the direction of the women’s gaze switches in each row and the colouring of the garments is repeated after every fourth row. Miniature paintings were often used as templates for silk weaves during this era. An especially delightful detail is the circlet-shaped feathered headdress with a long scarf that falls behind the back and is elegantly ruffled. This type of headdress was common until c. 1620 and is defining for the time in which this silk weaving was created.
holder: GRASSI Museum of Applied Art, Leipzig

ar.name: بلاطة
description: المعروضة هي صور المسجد الحرام بأشكال مختلفة.ومن بين الصور الأكثر شيوعا هناك الصورة ثنائية الأبعاد في شهادات/وثائق الحج والأقمشة والمخطوطات والبلاطات. وكل وحدة في هذه الرسوم يكتب عليها كتابة عربية وتشير للأماكن الرئيسية المبينة في الشكل. وهذه البلاطة من إزنيق (نيقية) تعرض مخطط للمسجد الحرام في مكة ذو السبع مآذن ويوجد نقوش كتابية تعريفية بالخط النسخي.

en.name: Tile
description: Depictions of al-Masjid al-Haram come in a variety of forms. Among the popular depiction is a two-dimensional image found on *hajj* certificates, textiles, manuscripts and tiles. Each unit in these drawings is usually labelled in Arabic script, highlighting the key places shown in the illustration. This Iznik tile depicts the plan of al-Masjid al-Haram in Makkah with seven minarets and identifying inscriptions in *naskhi*.

ar.name: سجادة.
description: جزء من سجادة مؤلف من أجزاء أصغر مخاطة معاً، تمثل زخارفها تصميماً نادراً يعرف أحياناً بنموذج "الرصيعة النجمية رباعية الفصوص" حيث يتم فيها ربط زوايا نماذج كبيرة متصالبة الشكل بعقد مع نماذج أصغر مستطيلة الشكل مما يخلق فراغات يتم وضع معينات أفقية أو عمودية فيها. ويعتقد أن هذا النموذج سابق للنموذج المعروف باسم "نجمة أوشاق" حيث يمكن مشاهدة رصائع مماثلة على سجاد مزين بالمنمنمات من القرن الخامس عشر بإيران. تدل التفاصيل الأخرى، كالعقد الرابطة، والنماذج في الزوايا، والبنية الشبكية بين الرصائع، على تأريخ أبكر، وهي تخلق إحساساً بتركيب مستمر. وهناك حوالي 20 سجادة حالياً تحمل هذا النموذج، لكن هذه السجادة هي النموذج الأكثر حفظاً.
قطعة من سجادة كبيرة، نُسجت من قطع قماش صغيرة. صُنعت على الطراز القديم الذي يطلق عليه " نجمة أوشاك"، وقد وُجدت زخارف مشابهة، على لوحات تعود إلى القرن التاسع الهجري/ الخامس عشر الميلادي، في إيران.
dates: أواخر القرن التاسع/ الخامس عشر حتى القرن الحادي عشر/ السابع عشر.
keywords: زخرفة زهرية.

en.name: Carpet.
description: A fragment of a carpet, sewn together from several smaller fragments. It features a relatively rare design sometimes referred to as the 'four-lobed star-medallion' pattern, in which the corners of large cross-shaped motifs are linked by knots to smaller rectangular motifs, creating spaces in which horizontal or vertical lozenges are placed. This pattern is thought to pre-date the well-known 'star Uşak' pattern, as similar medallions can be seen on carpets depicted in miniature paintings from 15th-century Iran. Other details suggesting an early date include the knots joining the motifs at their corners and the latticework structure running between the medallions, creating a sense of a continuous composition. There are about twenty carpets surviving with this pattern, but the present example is the best preserved.

A fragment of a larger carpet, itself sewn together from smaller fragments. The design is an early and relatively rare variation on the famous ‘star Uşak’ pattern. Similar patterns are seen on carpets in AH 9th- / AD 15th-century paintings from Iran.
dates: Late hegira 9th/ AD 15th to AH 11th / AD 17th century.
keywords: geometric decoration; floral decoration; star; miniature; painting

es.name: Alfombra
description: Fragmento de alfombra formado a su vez por varios fragmentos menores cosidos entre sí. Presenta un diseño relativamente raro, a veces denominado “medallón estrellado de cuatro lóbulos”, en el que los picos de grandes motivos en forma de cruz están enlazados por nudos a motivos rectangulares de menor tamaño, dando lugar a espacios en cuyo centro se han tejido formas romboidales. Se cree que este diseño precede en el tiempo a la conocida “estrella de Uşak”, pues en alfombras representadas en miniaturas iraníes del siglo XV se puede ver este tipo de medallones. Otros detalles que hacen pensar en una datación temprana son los nudos que unen los picos de los motivos y la estructura de celosía entre los medallones, que crea la impresión de una composición continua. Se conservan unas 20 alfombras con este diseño, pero esta es la mejor conservada.

Fragmento de alfombra formado a su vez por varios fragmentos menores cosidos entre sí. Su diseño es una variación más antigua y relativamente poco común de la famosa “estrella de Uşak”. Alfombras con diseños similares a este aparecen representadas en pinturas iraníes del siglo IX / XV.
dates: Entre finales del siglo IX y el siglo XI de la Hégira / siglos XV-XVII d. C.
keywords: decoración geométrica; decoración floral

fr.name: Tapis.
description: Fragment de tapis, composé de plusieurs fragments plus petits cousus ensemble. Il présente un motif relativement rare parfois appelé “médaillon étoilé à quatre lobes”, dans lequel les coins de grands motifs cruciformes sont reliés par des nœuds à des motifs rectangulaires plus petits en une composition qui génère des vides meublés par des losanges verticaux ou horizontaux. Ce motif serait antérieur à la célèbre “étoile d'Ouchak”, car des médaillons similaires s'observent sur des tapis reproduits dans des miniatures peintes persanes du XVe siècle. D'autres détails, comme les nœuds qui partent des coins des motifs et le réseau de treillis entre les médaillons qui crée une impression de composition continue, suggèrent une date ancienne. Si une vingtaine de tapis de ce modèle existent encore, celui-ci est le mieux conservé.

Fragment d'un grand tapis lui-même composé de fragments plus petits cousus ensemble. Le motif en est une variation précoce et relativement rare de la fameuse “étoile d'Ouchak”. On peut voir des motifs similaires sur des tapis reproduits dans des miniatures iraniennes du IXe s. H / XVe s. J.-C.
dates: fin IXe-XVe siècles de l’Hégire (XVe-XVIIe siècles J.-C.).
keywords: Décoration géométrique ; décoration florale

en.name: *Les amis de l’art* society, by the Greek cartonist Kem
short_description: The cartoon shows the art collectors of Alexandria: on the left is Antonis Benakis holding a paintbrush; K. Synadinos washes the floor, Chr. Nomikos hangs a ceramic dish on the wall and Baron de Menasque paints the ceiling standing on a ladder.
keywords: collecting; Greeks; Egypt; cartoon; caricature

en.name: Ceremonial Façade (main façade)
description: Perhaps one of the best palace façades of the Portuguese Baroque, it combines traditional Portuguese features with Classical precision. The triangular pediment, adorned at the tympanum with garlands, averts the solemnity of a façade which is the keynote of the garden views.
place: Exterior view from the Pênsil Garden
artist: Jean Baptiste Robillion (active 1758–1782), Mateus Vicente de Oliveira (1706–1786)
partner: Institute for the Administration of Architectural and Archaeological Heritage -  IGESPAR

pt.name: Fachada de cerimónia (fachada principal)
description: Talvez uma das melhores fachadas palacianas barrocas portuguesas. Possui os traços da tradição portuguesa, sem requebros de maior, aparentando um rigor classicista. O grande frontão triangular, ornado no tímpano com grinaldas, repõe a solenidade de uma fachada pensada como protagonista do eixo principal do jardim.
artist: Jean Baptiste Robillion (activo 1758–1782), Mateus Vicente de Oliveira (1706–1786)

ar.name: صحفة.
description:
صحفة مع غطاء واقٍ تعود إلى عائلة توندي في سينا، إيطاليا. مركزها مُحاط بأنساق من أزهار الفاشِرا المتألقة (تلك التي بتلاتها زرقاء وكؤيساتها مصبوغة بلون ذي بريق معدني )، متناوبة مع أنساق من أوراق شبيهة بـ' البقدونس' (وهي تلك المماثلة لأوراق البرسيم المسنَّنة)، وجميع هذه الأنساق مضفورة بوريقات السَّرخس المتطاولة، ذات البريق المعدني. هذا الطراز من الصحفات ينتمي إلى نسق مميَّز كان مرغوباً جداً في أسبانيا ومناطق أخرى من أوروبا، حيث يتمُّ تصديره بكميات كبيرة. وهذا ما يفسِّر وجود اسم العائلة الإيطالية على الغطاء، لأن هذا النوع من الأواني ذات البريق المعدني كانت شائعة في إيطاليا إلى حدٍ بعيد.  
كانت مانيسيز كانت إحدى المدن الرئيسية لتصنيع الفخار في فلينسيا، وقد لعبت دوراً ريادياً في صناعة الأواني ذات البريق المعدني من أجل تصديرها إلى أوروبا، وبالدرجة الأولى إلى فرنسا وإيطاليا. كانت منتجات مانيسيز الفخارية تعدُّ للتصدير عبر ميناء غروا في فلينسيا، حيث العديد من خزَّافي مانيسيز كانت لهم مستودعات ومتاجر هناك. وهؤلاء الخزَّافون كانوا خليطاً من المسيحيين والمغاربة ( المسلمين )، لكنَّ هؤلاء الأخيرين لم يكن مسموحاً لهم مزاولة حرفتهم خارج المدينة، وهذا دليل على الأهمية المميَّزة لمهاراتهم في اقتصاد مانيسيز. بحلول عام 956 / منتصف القرن السادس عشر، أضحت مانيسيز المحتكِر الرئيسي لمنتجات الأواني ذات البريق المعدني في فلينسيا.

إن التسمية القديمة لهذا النمط من خزف البريق المعدني، ذي الطراز المُدجَّن، هي "اسبانية مغربية"، عبارة تشي بأن الخزّافين الذين كانوا يصنعونه ظلّوا خليطاً من المسيحيين والمغاربة (المسلمين)، حيث كان الأخيرون ملزمين بحصر ممارستهم لمهارتهم المتمتعة بقدرٍ كبير من الإطراء، خارج بلدة مانيسس الفالنسية.
dynasty: المدجَّنون في أسبانيا، سلالة بنو نصر
keywords: تجارة.
materials: فخَّار مزجَّج مصبوغ بلون ذي بريق معدني.
tags: فخَّار مزجَّج مصبوغ بلون ذي بريق معدني.

en.name: Dish.
description:
A dish with the shield belonging to the Tondi family of Siena, Italy, in the centre surrounded by radiating chains of 'bryony' flowers (those with blue petals and lustre-painted centres) alternating with chains of blue 'parsley'-shaped leafs (those that are made up of ragged trefoil shapes), and both interwoven with lustre-coloured spindly 'fern' leaves. This style of dish belongs to a distinctive range that was much sought after in Spain and in other parts of Europe where it was exported in large quantities. This explains the presence of the Italian family's shield, for this type of lustre-ware was extremely popular in Italy.  
  
Manises was one of the main pottery-making towns in Valencia, and played a leading role in the manufacture of lustre-wares for export to Europe, principally to France and Italy. Manises's pottery left for export from the Valencian port of Grao where many Manises potters owned pottery warehouses and shops. These potters were a mixture of Christians and Moors (Muslims), the latter of which were not permitted to take their skills to work outside the town, testifying to the value of their special skills to the economy of Manises. By the mid-16th century (AH 956), Manises had a major monopoly on the production of lustre-wares in Valencia.

The old name for this type of Mudéjar-style Spanish lustre ceramics is ‘Hispano-Moresque’, a term indicating that the potters who made it were a mixture of Christians and Moors (Muslims), the latter of which were restricted to practising their much-praised skill outside the town of Manises in Valencia.
keywords: Commerce; Hispano-Moresque; coat of arms; floral decoration

es.name: Plato.
description:
Plato con escudo de la familia Tondi de Siena (Italia). Del escudo central salen cadenetas de flores de brionia (con pétalos azules y centros en reflejo metálico) que se alternan con cadenetas de hojas azules similares a las del perejil (con forma de trébol irregular); ambos grupos se intercalan con estilizadas hojas de helecho de colores brillantes. Esta clase de plato pertenecía a una serie característica, muy solicitada en España y el resto de Europa, adonde se exportaba en grandes cantidades. Este tipo de reflejo metálico fue muy popular en Italia, lo que explica la presencia del escudo de una familia italiana.  
Manises fue una de las principales poblaciones productoras de alfarería en Valencia y desempeñó un papel relevante en la fabricación de objetos de cerámica de reflejo metálico que se exportaban a Europa, principalmente a Francia e Italia. La alfarería de Manises se transportaba desde el puerto valenciano de Grao, donde muchos alfareros tenían sus almacenes y tiendas. Entre estos alfareros había cristianos y “moros”; estos últimos no estaban autorizados a ejercer su oficio fuera de la ciudad, lo que da idea del valor que tenía su actividad para la economía de Manises. A mediados del siglo XVI (956), Manises tenía el mayor monopolio de producción de objetos cerámicos de reflejo metálico en Valencia.

Estas cerámicas españolas de reflejo metálico, de estilo mudéjar, eran conocidas como “hispano-moriscas” por haber sido realizadas por artesanos cristianos y “moros”. Estos últimos no estaban autorizados a ejercer su apreciado oficio fuera de la ciudad de Manises (Valencia).
keywords: comercio

fr.name: Plat.
description:
Plat décoré en son centre de l'emblème de la famille siennoise des Tondi entouré de chaînes rayonnantes de fleurs de “bryone” (à pétales bleus et cœurs peints au lustre) alternant avec des feuilles de “persil” (faites de petits éléments trilobés), toutes deux entrelacées de feuilles de “fougère” fuselées colorées au lustre. Le style particulier de ce plat était alors très apprécié en Espagne et dans d'autres pays d'Europe où il était exporté en grandes quantités. Ce type de décor lustré était extrêmement populaire en Italie, ce qui explique la présence des armes de cette famille de Sienne.  
Manisès, l'un des principaux centres potiers de la région de Valence, a joué un rôle moteur dans la fabrication de pièces lustrées à destination de l'Europe, principalement la France et l'Italie. Les potiers de Manisès expédiaient par le port de Grao, où beaucoup d'entre eux possédaient des entrepôts et des boutiques. Ces artisans étaient aussi bien des musulmans que des catholiques, les premiers n'ayant pas l'autorisation de quitter la ville, ce qui témoigne du prix qui était attaché à leur talent. Vers le milieu du Xe siècle H (XVIe siècle J.-C.), Manisès possédait un quasi-monopole de la production d'articles à décor lustré dans la région de Valence.

L’ancien nom de ce type de céramiques lustrées espagnoles de style mudéjar est “hispano-mauresque”, un terme indiquant que les potiers qui les fabriquaient étaient aussi bien chrétiens que maures (musulmans). Ces derniers n’avaient pas le droit de pratiquer leurs talents très prisés en dehors de la ville de Manisès près de Valence.
keywords: commerce

ar.name: عناصر شماسية.
description:
أربعة عناصر من تصوينة (شماسية) مفرّغة لها شكل صليب يخترقه في المركز ثقب دائري. طُليت العناصر بالمينا باللون الأخضر، الذي زال عن بعض الأجزاء.  
يذكر ل. جولفان أنّ الأجزاء التي تشكل هذا النوع من الحواجز الخزفيّة تُجمع بشكل عام إلى بعضها البعض بواسطة أوتاد معدنيّة، وعلى عكس التصوينات الجصّية، فإن التصوينات من هذه الفئة لاتحتوي على قطع من الزجاج الملوّن.

تتخذ هذه العناصر الأربعة المنتمية لشماسية شكل صليب اخترق بثقب دائري في وسطه. طليت العناصر بلون أخضر، إلا أن الطلاء انقرض من بعض الأماكن؛ وقد كانت هذه العناصر تجمع بشكل عام فيما بينها بواسطة أوتاد معدنية.
keywords: تصوينة؛ شماسية؛ خزف؛ قلعة بني حمّاد؛ مينا.

en.name: Elements of a shutter.
description:
Four elements of a shutter, each in the shape of a cross and pierced by a circular hole at its centre. They are covered in green enamel, some of which has disappeared from certain parts.  
Golvin (se Bibliography) mentions that the elements that compose this type of ceramic partitioning are usually assembled together with metal studs, and that, in contrast to plaster ones, those of this type do not include any fragments of coloured glass.

These four parts of a screen wall are cross-shaped with a circular hole in their centre. They are covered with a green enamel that has disappeared in places. These parts were usually joined together using metal dowels.
keywords: Ceramic; cloister; enamel; Qal’at Bani Hammad; Cross-shaped shutter; circular hole; ceramic partitioning
partner: National Museum of Antiquities and Islamic Art

es.name: Elementos de celosía.
description:
Cuatro elementos de una celosía, cruciformes y con un agujero en el centro. Están vidriados en color verde; el esmalte ha desaparecido en ciertas partes.  
L. Golvin indica que los componentes de este tipo de tabiques de cerámica solían estar unidos por clavijas metálicas y que, a diferencia de los de yeso, las celosías de esta clase no tenían vidrios coloreados.

Cuatro elementos de una celosía de cerámica, cruciformes y con un agujero en el centro. Están vidriados en color verde, aunque el esmalte ha desaparecido en ciertas partes. Estos elementos solían estar unidos entre sí con clavijas metálicas.
keywords: cerámica; celosía; esmalte; Qala'a de los Banu Hammad
partner: Museo Nacional de Antigüedades y de Arte Islámico

fr.name: Eléments de claustra.
description:
Quatre éléments de claustra en forme d'une croix percée d'un trou circulaire en son centre. Ils sont émaillés de couleur verte, l'émail a disparu sur certaines parties.  
  
L. Golvin mentionne que les éléments composant ce genre de cloisonnements de céramique sont généralement assemblés entre eux par des goujons de métal, et que, contrairement aux claustras en plâtre, les claustras de cette catégorie ne portent pas de fragments de verres colorés.

Ces quatre éléments de claustra ont la forme d'une croix percée d'un trou circulaire en son centre. Ils sont émaillés de couleur verte, même si l'émail a disparu par endroits. Ces éléments étaient généralement assemblés entre eux par des gougeons de métal.
keywords: céramique ; claustra ; émail ; Qalaa des Beni Hammad
partner: Le Musée national des antiquités et d’art musulman

en.name: Conical cup
description:
Stoneware, celadons, and porcelain from China fascinated the Arab, Iranian, and Turkish worlds. The chronicles of the reigns of the Abbasid caliphs bear witness to this, as do the collections of the Ottoman sultans.  
In the absence of kaolin, and to replace porcelain, ceramists opt for a new clay mixture, obtained from pulverised quartz pebbles, white clay, and frit (pulverised mixture of quartz pebbles and soda from vegetable ash). These are the available materials. The mixture is soft; this piece mimics the translucency of porcelain. This technique was not known in the West until the 18th century, evidence of the technical progress made by Eastern ceramists.
holder: Museum of the Arab World Institute
materials: Siliceous material (pulverised quartz pebbles, white sintered clay); champlevé design, colourless transparent glaze
tags: Siliceous material (pulverised quartz pebbles, white sintered clay)
partner: Museum of the Arab World Institute

fr.name: Gobelet tronconique
description:
Grès, céladons et porcelaines de Chine ont fasciné les mondes arabes, iranien et turc. Les chroniques des règnes des califes abbassides en témoignent tout comme les collections des sultans ottomans.  
En l'absence de kaolin, et pour remplacer la porcelaine, les céramistes optent pour une nouvelle composition de la pâte, obtenue à partir de galets de quartz pulvérisés, d'argile blanche et de fritte (mélange pulvérisé de galets de quartz et de soude provenant de cendres végétales). Ce sont les matériaux dont ils disposaient. La pâte est tendre ; le gobelet imite la translucidité de la porcelaine. Cette technique ne sera obtenue en Occident qu'au XVIIIe siècle J.-C., témoignant ainsi des progrès techniques réalisés par les céramistes orientaux.
holder: Musée de l'Institut du monde arabe
dates: Ve siècle de l'Hégire / XIe siècle J.-C.
materials: Pâte siliceuse (galets de quartz pulvérisés, argile blanche et fritte), décor champlevé, glaçure transparente incolore
tags: Pâte siliceuse (galets de quartz pulvérisés, argile blanche et fritte), décor champlevé, glaçure transparente incolore

ar.name: زي أسمال لدرويش
description: في ذات يوم أراد شخص أن يعيش حياة صوفية و تخلى عن العالم وارتدى ثوبا من الصوف الخشن وعرف بالصوفي وهو مشتق من كلمة صوف العربية وهذا الناسك ارتدى لباس درويش (خرقة/ سمل) وقد تم قبوله في الأخوية. والملابس الرثة للصوفيين تعبّر عن الفقر وكانت تخاط من قطع عديدة (رقع). وهي أيضا بشكل ما تذّكر بالزي الملون للمهرج ذو الشرائط الملونة المعينة الشكل كما لو أن مرتديها يهيم على وجهه  في الملكوت في شكل كوميدي متقمصا دور نصف مهرج ونصف شيطان من أجل اكتشاف البنى والآليات في المجتمع و لفت الانتباه بشكل ساخر والازدراء ومن الناحية الروحية فإن الفكاهة يمكن أن تفهم كمحاولات فعالة في كشف الحالات المعقدة والمتناقضة التي تمتلئ بها الحياة الحقيقية.وفي هذه الأيام يرتدي الصوفيون ملابس عادية مألوفة.

en.name: Rag costume of a Dervish
description: Once upon a time, an individual who wanted to lead the life of a mystic and had renounced the world, donned a robe of rough wool and was identified as a Sufi, derived from the Arabic word for wool, *ṣūf*. The novice was dressed in the clothing of a dervish, the *hirqa* once admitted into a brotherhood. The tattered clothing of the Sufis expresses poverty and was stitched together from numerous patches. It is somehow also reminiscent of the colourful costume of a harlequin, with vivid lozenge-shaped stripes. It seems as if the rambling fool of God in the Commedia dell'arte slipped into the role of the half-clownish, half-demonic prankster, in order to expose the structures and mechanisms of society, attracting ridicule and disdain upon himself. Spirituality and humour can be understood as effective attempts to reveal the complex and paradox situations of which real life is so full. Nowadays a Sufi wears normal daily clothing.

en.name: The Solovetsky Monastery
description: Savvaty, a monk from the Kirilov Monastery, founded a small commune on the island of Solovki near the White Sea in 1392. He left the inhospitable island in 1435 and died later the same year. The next year, the monk Zosimas moved to Solovki and built the first monastic cell, which eventually became a splendid and wealthy monastery thanks to a lucrative salt trade and plentiful gifts. Zosimas remained the abbot until his death in 1478.  The monastery, with its numerous towers and thick, fortified walls, is depicted in the lower half of this icon, and Saints Zosimas and Savvaty are depicted above the monastery, flanked by two angels. This icon’s large scale and thematic content suggest that the image was produced at the Solovetsky Monastery.
keywords: Saints; Religious iconography

en.name: Dragon carpet
description: The so-called dragon carpets are the oldest preserved group that can be localised to the South Caucasus production area. The Chinese symbol of power, the dragon, which became popular in Iran during the Ilkhanid dynasty (13th/14th century), was carried through by the art of the Timurids and Safavids into remote regions. In knotted executions, the dragons became noticeably more geometric. In total, three pairs of geometrised yellow dragons are to be seen in the carpet, yet, since they are difficult to distinguish, the exemplar is dated to the late 17th, or the early 18th century respectively. One can clearly recognise the head and tail in the MAK Collection’s dragon carpet; the originally lambent flames on the legs, however, were stylised into geometrised, tendril-like forms. Today, the carpet’s place of origin is presumed to be the Karabakh region, where Shah Abbas I (r. 1587–1629) had established manufactories.
holder: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art
keywords: Safawid; textile; carpet; wool; geometric design; dragon
materials: Wool warp and weft; knotted; asymmetrical knot
partner: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art

en.name: House
short_description: The architecture of Krushevo was influenced by houses in Moscopole, as well as by the mountain dwellings in Epirus and Thessaly. Native architects, Vlachs originating from Moscopole and Miyaks from the Reka Area, created their distinctive and highly autonomous dwelling architecture which combined the traditional mode of building with architectural solutions arising from the steep terrain. This house is a three-storied structure of symmetrical type. The ground floor is made of stone and mortar. Upper stories were built of wooden framing and adobe, covered with plaster. The dynamic rhythm of the front façade has been achieved by the repetitive layout of windows and balconies above the front door at the second and third storey. The decoration is enhanced by the intricate wooden and iron balcony balusters on the second and third storey.
history: Krushevo houses had to be adjusted to the naturally steep terrain on which they sit. The dwelling architecture of this town thus shows notable vertical development, which has given rise to creative architectural solutions for the purpose of maximum use of space.
keywords: painted façade decoration; symmetrical type

en.name: Indigo-died parchment page from a Holy Qur’an manuscript
description: This horizontal Qur’an page of indigo-died parchment was executed in golden *kufic* script without any auxiliary vowel markers or diacritics. It is assumed to have formed part of a manuscript made in North Africa, possibly Kairouan, during the AH 4th century / AD 10th century. The page gives verses 135-137 from chapter 4 "*Al-Nisa’* (The Women)".
