es.name: Plato con pequeño toro.
description:
Plato de paredes curvas y pie circular, pintado en reflejo metálico rojo intenso sobre fondo blanco crema. La decoración presenta en el centro la silueta de un novillo en reflejo metálico con detalles en reserva; de ella parten cuatro largos tallos simétricos con flores estilizadas que podrían derivar de una transformación de ramas de parra como las representadas en piezas de la misma serie.  
Cada una de las cuatro secciones en que aparece dividida la superficie está decoradas con un frondoso arbusto inclinado, con hojas en forma de pluma que anuncian un motivo que llegará a ser muy común en objetos más tardíos (siglo XVIII). De cada arbusto nacen dos pares de una especie de fruto triangular con dibujo interior en forma de escamas obtenido dejando partes en reserva.
Plato decorado con motivos que serán típicos de los productos más tardíos realizados en los talleres valencianos.
holder: Museo de Civilizaciones | Museo de Arte Oriental “Giuseppe Tucci”
dates: Finales del siglo XVII d. C.
keywords: plato; reflejo metálico; arte mudéjar
partner: Museo de Civilizaciones | Museo de Arte Oriental

fr.name: Plat avec taurillon.
description:
Plat à marli bombé sur pied annulaire peint au lustre rouge intense sur fond crème. Le décor présente, au centre, la silhouette d'un taurillon peint en lustre, avec des détails en réserve ; de cette silhouette partent, symétriquement, quatre longues tiges avec inflorescences stylisées, dérivant très probablement d'une ultérieure transformation de rinceaux du type représenté sur certaines pièces appartenant à la même classe d'objets.  
Les quatre compartiments entre lesquels se divise la surface sont décorés chacun avec un rameau à feuilles en forme de plumes, disposé obliquement, qui annonce un motif très courant dans des productions plus tardives (XIIe siècle H / XVIIIe siècle J.-C.).  
Chaque rameau donne naissance à deux paires d'une sorte de fruit triangulaire, à l'intérieur duquel sont dessinées des écailles, et obtenu à partir d'éléments en réserve.
Le décor de ce plat annonce des motifs qui deviendront typiques des produits réalisés plus tard dans la région de Valence (Espagne).

it.name: Piatto con piccolo toro.
description:
Piatto a parete ricurva su piede ad anello dipinto a lustro rosso intenso su fondo bianco-crema. La decorazione presenta al centro la silhouette di un torello dipinto a lustro con particolari risparmiati, dalla quale partono, simmetricamente, quattro lunghi steli con infiorescenze stilizzate, derivanti molto probabilmente da una ulteriore trasformazione di tralci vegetali del tipo rappresentato in esemplari della stessa classe di oggetti.  
I quattro settori, in cui risulta divisa la superficie, sono decorati ciascuno con un grosso cespuglio a foglie piumate, disposto obliquamente, che preannuncia un motivo assai comune in prodotti più tardi (XII/XVIII secolo).
Il piatto mostra una decorazione che preannuncia motivi che diverranno tipici dei prodotti più tardi realizzati in ambito valenzano.

en.name: Nossa Senhora da Conceição (Parish Church)
names: Nossa Senhora da Conceição (Redinha Parish Church)
description:
This settlement grew up around a fort built by the Knights Templar, that was handed over to the Order of Christ in the 14th century. The first charter was granted to Gualdim Pais, Master of the Order, in 1159, who re-built the small castle and the Romanesque bridge that still exists here.  
The Romanesque Parish Church was considerably altered during the Manueline period. The general structure dates from the 16th century, as do the simple outer doorways with foliate decoration that is typical of this period.

en.name: *Madonna with Child and Saints* (Anthony of Padua, Martin, Roch and Sebastian)
description:
Painted in 1655, the «small picture with the Blessed Virgin, St. Martin, St. Sebastian, St. Roch and St. Anthony of Padua for the municipality of Trasasso», is still in its original location.  
Made for a peripheral area, the painting is an example of the style of a young woman artist at the beginning of her carrier, when she was still strictly dependent on her father and teacher, the painter Giovanni Andrea Sirani. The painting of the *Madonna and Child and Saints* painted by Giovanni Andrea in the same years for the church of Santi Luigi e Alessio(today, in Rome, church of San Petronio dei Bolognesi) was clearly a model for his daughter and pupil. Elisabetta, however, goes back to the roots of Bolognese classicism, imitating the more vibrant and rich results of Annibale Carracci in his celebrated *Madonna with Saint Louis* (Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale).  
The divine is interpreted in a more human way through the intimate and confidential dialogue between the Virgin in glory with the Child and the saints, nearly tangible, standing on the step in the foreground. Tenderness is glimpsed under the polished and soft surfaces, a sort of prelude of the artist’s future stylistic inclinations: Elisabetta starts to experiment with her own language with a prestigious and difficult genre: the altarpiece.

The painting, made for a peripheral area, is the first public commission of by a famous woman painter at a very young age, she was only seventeen years old. It shows her extremely precocious talent and underlines the still strong link with Bolognese Classicism through the influence of Annibale Carracci and Guido Reni, the master of Giovanni Andrea Sirani, father and master of Elisabetta.
keywords: Altarpiece; Religious/liturgical painting; Elisabetta Sirani; women; Giovanni Andrea Sirani; Guido Reni; Christian themes

it.name: *Madonna col Bambino e santi Antonio da Padova, Martino, Rocco e Sebastiano*
description:
Eseguita nel 1655, la «tavolina con la B.V., S. Martino, S. Bastiano, S. Rocco e S. Antonio da Padova, per il Comune di Trasasso», come ricorda la *Nota delle pitture* (*Nota*, in Carlo Cesare Malvasia, *Felsina pittrice*, Bologna 1678, (ed. cons. 1841), p. 393), si trova ancora nell'ubicazione d'origine.  
Destinata ad una sede periferica, documenta l'attività della giovane artista ai suoi esordi, ancora profondamente legata alla lezione di Giovanni Andrea Sirani. La coeva pala con la *Madonna col Bambino e santi* dipinta dal padre/maestro per la chiesa dei Santi Ludovico e Alessio (oggi a Roma, chiesa dei Santi Giovanni e Petronio dei Bolognesi) si rivela, infatti, un chiaro modello di riferimento per la figlia allieva (F. Frisoni, 1978, p. 5), che tenta, tuttavia, di risalire alle fonti della tradizione del classicismo bolognese, misurandosi con la pittura più vibrante e materica messa a punto da Annibale Carracci nella celebre *Madonna di san Ludovico* (Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale), sostituita proprio dalla tela di Giovanni Andrea.  
Un'interpretazione del sacro resa in termini più accostabili nel dialogo confidente e ravvicinato fra la Vergine con il Bambino in gloria e santi, quasi tangibili, disposti nello spazio imminente del gradino in primo piano; una tenerezza affettiva nascosta sotto superfici morbide e levigate a preludio delle propensioni stilistiche della pittrice: Elisabetta intraprende la sperimentazione di un proprio linguaggio, affrontando l'impegnativo e prestigioso genere della pala d'altare.

La pala, pur destinata ad una sede periferica, è la prima commissione pubblica della celebre pittrice ancora giovanissima, diciassettenne. L ’opera esprime la precocità del talento dell’artista ed evidenzia il legame ancora forte con la tradizione del classicismo bolognese per il riflesso della lezione di Annibale Carracci ed anche di Guido Reni, di cui Giovanni Andrea Sirani, padre e maestro di Elisabetta, fu allievo.
keywords: Pala d'altare;  Elisabetta Sirani; donne; Giovanni Andrea Sirani; Guido Reni; Pittrice; Trasasso; tematiche cristiane

en.name: Tympanum made of 16 tiles from the palace of the grand vizier Piale Pasha (c. 1515-1578)
description: These tiles decorated the palace of the Ottoman Grand Vizier Piale Pasha, or possibly the mosque the Vizier commissioned. Both buildings were completed in 1573 and richly decorated with tile panels. The palace and the mosque were restored after an earthquake in 1890, and the tile panels were sold all over the world. At least nine identical tympanums are now in American and European museums.

ar.name: لوحة سقفية
description: بالرغم من نهاية الحكم الإسلامي في شبه الجزيرة الإيبرية في عام 1492 فإن الطراز الإسلامي للفن والعمارة استمر شائعا بين الطبقة العليا للنخبة الحاكمة والعديد من الحرفيين المسلمين بقوا في إسبانيا ليلبوا الطلب المستمر على خدماتهم. وهذا المجتمع من المسلمين الإسبان والطراز الهجين الذي طوروه كان يعرف بالمدجن وقد صنع ليزين قصور النبلاء الإسبان الأثرياء ، وإن لوحات السقف مثل هذا النوع هي مثال عن الطراز المدجن في جمعه بين التصاميم الإسلامية والأوربية والتي ترى هنا في التزيين الهندسي الموافق المستوحى من النجمة والأسد الصرحي والقلعة والتي تساعد في ربط السقف ببناء في طليطلة.إن أصل السقف له قصة طريفة حيث أن آخر موطن له كان نادي كلية UCSB حيث تم تركيبه في المطبخ ومناطق الخدمات من عام 1968 وحتى 2014. ولا يعرف كيف لفت انتباه تشارلز موور Charles Moore الذي صمم النادي ولكن يوجد قصة في UCSB  بأن السقف كان سابقا ينتمي لـ W.R. Hearst . وقد أفضت أبحاثنا أن هيرست فعلا حصل على السقف في 1920s وقد شحنه إلى سان سيميون San Simeon وبالرغم من أنه كان يراد أن يوضع في قلعة هيرست Hearst Castle فإنه لم يركب قط فيها ومن المحتمل أن موور اشتراه من متاجر هيرست في عام 1967. ولوحات السقف الباقية سيتم المحافظة عليها بحيث أنه يمكن عرضها كسقف قريب من الكامل في 2020s.

en.name: Panel from a Ceiling
description: Despite the end of Muslim rule on the Iberian Peninsula in 1492, an Islamic style of art and architecture continued to be popular among the ruling elite, and many Muslim craftsmen remained in Spain to meet the enduring demand for their services. This community of Spanish Muslims and the hybrid style that they developed came to be known by the term mudéjar. Made to decorate the palaces of wealthy Spanish notables, ceiling panels of this type are an example of the mudéjar style in their combination of Islamic and European designs, seen here in the respective star-inspired geometric decoration and the heraldic lion and castle, which help to link the ceiling to a building in Toledo. The provenance of the ceiling makes for a compelling story; its last home was the UCSB Faculty Club, where it was installed in the kitchen and service areas, from 1968 until 2014. It is not known how it came to the attention of Charles Moore, who designed the club, but UCSB legend has it that the ceiling had once belonged to W.R. Hearst. Our research has shown that Hearst had indeed acquired the ceiling in the 1920s and had it shipped to San Simeon. Although it may have been intended for Hearst Castle, it was never installed there and Moore likely purchased it from Hearst's warehouses in 1967. The remaining ceiling panels will undergo conservation so that they may be displayed as a near-complete ceiling in the 2020s.

en.name: Saint Paraskeva
description:
Saint Paraskeva was born to Christian parents during the reign of Emperor Hadrian. She was given the name Paraskeva (Greek for “Friday”) since Friday was the day of Christ’s crucifixion as well as the day of her birth. She was arrested during the reign of Emperor Antoninus Pius for preaching Christianity. He offered her great wealth and even proposed marriage if she renounced her faith, but she refused. The enraged emperor placed her in boiling oil, and when she did not show any pain, demanded to know whether she had used magic to cool the oil. She responded by throwing the hot liquid at the emperor, instantly blinding him. He asked Paraskeva for help and she healed him with water from a nearby stream. Antoninus Pius set her free, converted to Christianity and stopped persecuting Christians. The inscription on the scroll in this icon reads as follows:  
  
\[H\]ighly praised is thy name – of Father and Son and Holy Spirit, my Lord God – now and forever. For thou forgave me and did not reject my humility nor my prayer; and thy being pleased by me is incomprehensible.
keywords: Saints; Religious iconography

en.name: Pair of Torchères
description:
These two grandiose torchères were ordered for the Chapel of Saint John the Baptist to be installed in São Roque church in Lisbon. With a triangular base, in gilt bronze, they form a pyramid held by titans. Above, a cornice developing into a dome is finished with Rocaille-inspired shells and a D. João V shield on each of the three surfaces of the torch holders. In niches below the dome, forming an oratory, the Doctors of the church are seated: St Jerome, St. Thomas Aquinas, Sr. Ambrose and St. Bonaventure, St. Augustine and St. Leo the Great. The hybrid ornamentation develops upwards in fluid volutes – wing, acroterion, cymatium – flowers in the shape of garlands, phytomorphic elements – rope, laurel and acanthus – and zoomorphic elements, as well as a variety of *putti* inspired by the Roman Baroque.  
They were conceived and produced by Giuseppe Gagliardi with the cooperation of the metalworker Fellice Schiffone, the carpenter Lucano Celladini, Agostino Ancidoni another metalworker, and Lorenzo Morelli a silversmith and founder. Following the death of Giuseppe Gagliardi minor finishing and the lamination were concluded by his son, Leonardo Gagliardi, who like his father was a master silversmith.

A splendid pair of torch holders in gilt bronze and chiselled silver, they form part of a royal commission for the Chapel of St. John the Baptist. Designed and produced by Giuseppe Gagliardi, the metalworkers Fellice Schiffone and Agostino Ancidoni collaborated with him on the project. Lucano Celladini was the carpenter and Luciano Morelli was the silversmith and founder.

pt.name: *Par de tocheiros*
description:
Este par de tocheiros integrava a grandiosa encomenda de alfaias religiosas destinadas à Capela de S. João Baptista.  
Sobre uma base triangular em bronze dourado, desenvolve-se uma ornamentação em pirâmide sustentada por titãs, sentados em edículas. Uma cornija, desenvolvendo-se em cúpula, é rematada por concha, de inspiração *rocaille*, com o escudo de D. João V, em cada uma das três faces dos tocheiros. No nicho, abaixo da cúpula, formando edícula, têm assento Doutores da Igreja: São Jerónimo, São Tomás de Aquino, Santo Ambrósio, São Boaventura, Santo Agostinho e São Leão Magno. Uma ornamentação híbrida desenvolve-se com ritmo ascendente, através de volutas, aletas, acrotérios, cimalhas, flores sob a forma de grinaldas, elementos fitomórficos – cardo, louro, acanto –, elementos zoomórficos e conchas, bem como uma diversidade de *putti*, que narram a evolução do gosto estético e decorativo romano, de inspiração barroca e *rocaille*.  
Concebidos e fabricados por Giuseppe Gagliardi, na sua execução colaboraram Fellice Schiffone, metalista; Luciano Celladini, carpinteiro; Agostino Ancidoni, serralheiro e Lorenzo Morelli, prateiro e fundidor. Por morte de Giuseppe Gagliardi, pequenos trabalhos de acabamentos e laminagem foram concluídos por seu filho Leandro (ou Leonardo) Gagliardi, mestre prateiro como o pai.
Esplêndido par de tocheiros de prata dourada e bronze dourado da grandiosa encomenda real de alfaias religiosas destinadas à Capela de S. João Baptista.

en.name: *The Judgment of Solomon*
description:
The only Persian artists in the 17th century who were able to break with the overwhelming influence of Riza-i Abbasi were those who were inspired by the greater naturalism that characterized not only European but also Indian painting.  
Shaykh Abbasi was one of them, and in this signed and minutely detailed painting, he set the court of Solomon in 17th-century Iran.
type: Miniature pasted on an album leaf
keywords: Leaf; India; Persia; Painting; Safawid; miniature

en.name: Seljuq Rug
description: This rug, found in the Konya Aladdin Mosque exhibits the richness of motif and colour of the Seljuq rugs. It is unique from others in the “Konya Group” because of its background colour and octagonal decoration. The characteristic *kufic* border is evidence of its origin. The main border is framed with a thin border of blue and brown lines. Pairs of stylized *kufic* letters in white are in the main border on a red background. Octagon shapes on the red background go to infinity. The inside of the motifs are dark red. The camel’s foot motif inside the octagons are made with a dark contour.
holder: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts
keywords: Middle Anatolia; Konya; Seljuq Rug

en.name: Carpet
description:
Three fragments mounted on machine-sewn burlap.  
Field: The decoration corresponds to a carpet of crowns. Within its corners it presents a pinkish flower as a defining feature and also contains floral cluster or vegetal motifs. In the corners a geometric floral set of three branches is visible. The background utilises reddish hues and the plant motifs are in dark and light shades of green along with a yellow outline.  
Border: The carpet fragment shows a narrow border of Franciscan knot that separates the field and the central border by yellow stripes. The Franciscan knot is of a single end and is outlined in yellow, the knots of the major and minor sides being different. The preserved decoration of these fragments allows us to perceive that the central border is formed by candlestick motifs on a light green background. The dark green motifs outlined in yellow also act as a potent contrast.  
The warp utilises wool with its natural colour and the weft utilises red dyed wool. The decorative aspects of the carpet consist of red, dark green and light green wool.
artist: Workshops of Alcaraz (Old Kingdom of Murcia)
keywords: Alcaraz
materials: Warp: Wool, Weft: wool, Knot: wool / Spanish knot [Warp: 5 knots / cm, Weft 5 knots / cm 3 or 4 weft threads oscillate for each irregular multiple half past]

es.name: Alfombra
description:
Tres fragmentos montados sobre una arpillera cosidos a máquina.  
Campo: La decoración corresponde a una alfombra de coronas. En sus cuatro extremos presenta una flor rosácea a modo de abrazadera. Contiene, además, motivos de racimos. En los ángulos se percibe un conjunto floral esquemático de tres ramos. El color utilizado para el fondo es el rojo y los motivos vegetales en verde oscuro y claro, perfilados en amarillo.  
Marco: Contiene una cenefa estrecha de cordón francisco que separa el campo y la cenefa central por franjas amarillas. El nudo franciscano es de un solo cabo y está perfilado en amarillo, siendo diferentes los nudos del lado mayor y el menor. La decoración conservada de estos fragmentos permite percibir que la cenefa central está formada por motivos a candelieri sobre fondo verde claro. Se destacan en ella los motivos en verde oscuro perfilados en amarillo.  
La urdimbre es lana en su color y la trama lana roja. La decoración es en lana de color rojo, verde oscuro y verde claro.
keywords: Alcaraz
materials: Urdimbre: Lana. Trama: lana. Nudo: lana. Nudo español  [Urdimbre: 5 nudos/cm. Trama 5 nudos/cm oscilan 3 ó 4 hilos de trama por cada media pasada múltiple irregular]

cs.name: *Vizovice - zámecká kaple*
description:
Interiér kaple situované na konci jižního křídla zámku ve Vizovicích na Valašsku a komponované na centrálním půdoryse se třemi apsidami, je završen kupolí. Kresebný návrh nám je představuje v jedné rovině. Vlevo kazatelnu s reliéfem Křest Krista, hlavní oltář Nanebevzetí Panny Marie  se svatostánkem ve formě sarkofágu, postavami Mariiných rodičů sv. Jáchyma a sv. Anny a mariánským obrazem vynášeným anděly, jehož vrchol tvoří monogram jména Maria. Druhý oltář zdobený konsekračními kříži tvoří rámec pro obraz sv. Jana Nepomuckého. Třetí pole tvoří návrh oratoře s iluzivní draperií. V místě dveří je vyobrazen poslední ze cviklů klenby, dekorovaných tetramorfy evangelistů s anděly nesoucími evangelia. Zleva sv. Matouš, sv. Jan (orel), Sv. Marek (lev) a  
sv. Lukáš (býk).  
Schweiglův návrh, vyznačující se jemnou ornamentikou ve stylu Ludvíka XVI., byl jen s drobnými obměnami realizován do r. 1777 v souladu s požadavkem stavebníka zámku Heřmana Hannibala z Blümegenu (+1774), který kapli věnoval vzácná mešní roucha a liturgické předměty, které se zde uchovaly dodnes. Pro kazatelnu byl na místo návrhu vytvořen reliéf Narození Páně a oratorium bylo pojednáno mnohem úsporněji, bez divadelní opony.  
Rokokový, plasticky zdobený interiér je příznačným stylovým protipólem uměřené, klasizující architektury Františka Antonína Grimma, praktikujícího  
v Římě v ateliéru Nicola di Salviho, ve Francii a v Německu. Návrh svědčí o všestrannosti vzdělaného brněnského sochaře, který nepodceňoval svou dekoratérskou úlohu, která s se završujícím stoletím  nabývala na významu.

en.name: *Vizovice Chateau, Chapel*
description:
The chapel in the south wing of the Vizovice Chateau in the Wallachia region is built into a central layout with three apses and crowned with a cupola. The drawing represents the chapel on a single level. On the left is a pulpit decorated with a relief of the Baptism of Christ, and the high altar with the Assumption of the Virgin Mary with a sarcophagus-shaped tabernacle, figures of Mary's parents, St. Joachim and St. Anne, and a Marian picture carried by angels, the top of which features a monogram of the name “Mary”. The second altar, decorated with consecration crosses, provides a framework for a picture of St. John of Nepomuk. The third field is a design for an oratory with illusionary drapery. In the place of the door is the last of the vaulting joints decorated with tetramorphs of the evangelists with angels carrying the gospels, from the left: Matthew, John (eagle), Mark (lion) and Luke (bull).  
Schweigl's design, with fine ornamentation in Louis XVI style, was executed with only minor changes (the latest of which was in 1777), in accordance with the requirements of the chateau's sponsor Heřman Hannibal of Blümegen (c. 1774), who also endowed the chapel with precious chasubles and liturgical objects that have survived to this day. A relief of the birth of Christ was created for the pulpit, replacing the original design. The decoration of the oratory is much more austere, without the theatre-like curtain.  
The Rococo interior with its relief decoration stands in contrast to the low-key classicist architecture of František Antonín Grimm who trained in Rome, in the studio of Nicolo di Salvi, in France and in Germany. The design bears witness to the versatility of the learned Brno sculptor, Andreas Schweigl. Schweigl did not underestimate the role of the decorator, something that gained in significance towards the end of the century.

The design shows the versatility of the learned Brno sculptor Andreas Schweigl, who did not underestimate the decorator’s role. The chapel interior, with fine Louis XVI ornamentation, contrasts with the low-key classicist architecture of František Antonín Grimm, who trained in Rome, France and Germany.
keywords: Rococo; Louis XVI style; evangelists; tabernacle; sculpture

en.name: Panel from the Ibn Tulun Mosque
description:
The panel was originally part of a frieze with passages from the Koran that is some two kilometers long. The inscription is in a simple and robust *Kufi* script whose only decorative element is a little increase in width at the end of the letters.  
The panel was purchased in Cairo in 1848 by the French consul Delaporte, after restoration work on the Ibn Tulun Mosque.

en.name: Carpet
description:
Following the 1834 abolition of Portuguese religious institutions, most of their portable heritage was transferred to the Portuguese State. The incorporation of textiles, including carpets, into State property is particularly relevant to the history and the creation of national museums and collections such as the National Museum of Ancient Art. This carpet, which has been in the NMAA’s collection since 1888, comes from the former convent of Estrela for which it had been commissioned by Princess Maria I (r.1777‒1816) after the birth of her son.  
Although building began in 1779, well after the date of this carpet’s production, its incorporation in the convent can be attributed to two reasons: as an offering from the Royal Portuguese House, owner of an impressive collection of Oriental carpets, to encourage offers from other donors, or even a transfer from another religious institution.  
The lack of documentation makes it difficult to ascertain its original function. These carpets were much appreciated and used as important decorative furnishings both in sacred and profane interiors, where they were meant to define spaces. One such example of physical delimitation lay in the use of carpets to cover the stairway and higher elevated daises that became an Iberian tradition within the female universe and lasted well into the 19th century.  
This carpet has undergone several restorative interventions, with its original size having been approximately a metre larger than at present; of almost eight-metres in length, this carpet shows a very balanced design and colour. It presents the classical ornamental motifs characteristic of this category, along with the field filled with “vine scrolls” alternating with palmettes and S-shape cloud scrolls (*tchi*). It also exhibits the characteristic contrast of colours between the field and the border (red/blue), both filled with palmettes and chinar leaves.
keywords: carpet; Iran; 17th century; Portugal
materials: Cotton and wool; knotted; knot, 2Z (4Z); asymmetric knot, open to the left
tags: Asymmetric knot, Open to the left

en.name: *The Tomb of Rachel*
short_description: The Tomb of Rachel is another sacred religious site described in *Palestine Past and Present* by Laura Jewry Valentine. The place was equally sacred for Jews, Christians and Muslims, but apart from a short reference to the prayers performed by the Muslim and Jews at this site, the description is devoted to finding the correspondence between the existing site and the Biblical story of Rachel. The site is therefore seen as one of the places revealing the main scope and aim of the book: the discovery of the Christian tradition related to the Holy Land.

en.name: Swiss Confederation 20 Franc coin
description: This Swiss 20 Franc gold coin minted between 1897 and 1949 is commonly known by its nickname «Gold Vreneli», from the diminutive form of the traditional Swiss girl’s name of Verena and the portrait of a lady on its obverse, as designed by Fritz Ulisse Landry (1842–1927). In April 1895 the Swiss Federal Council appointed a jury to assess the 21 design entries for a new gold coin. Among those who submitted designs were such famous names as the artist Albert Anker and the academic Friedrich Imhoof-Blumer. Fritz Ulisse Landry’s design won second prize; no first prize was awarded. The first 400,000 of these new gold coins were minted in 1897. In addition, 29 gold coins were produced using gold extracted from the mine at Gondo (Valais) that was abandoned that same year. This is one of the few remaining «Gondo-Vrenelis».
keywords: Gondo-Vreneli; Vreneli; Coin; Gold; Gondo; Valais; Fritz Ulisse Landry; 20; Franc; Franken; Switzerland

en.name: Blue glazed jar
description:
This jar, with two small handles, a narrow neck and a globular body is covered externally with a turquoise-blue glaze, while the interior is covered with a white glaze. The lip of the neck is protruding, which may have allowed for the placement of a small ceramic or wooden lid held by a textile.  
  
This functional object used for the storage and transportation of liquids, such as oil, water, wine or syrup. t was discovered at the Murwab archaeological site in northwest Qatar. The production of this type of jar appears to have ceased in the middle of the 9th century, according to the stratified archaeological findings of Susa (Iran), Samarra and Basra (Iraq). The most important workshop for this production was the centre of Basra.

en.name: Ramparts and Bastions
description:
The first enclosure built in Asilah dates from the Almohad era. It was restored during the Merinid era and reinforced by the Wattassids. But this first enclosure was unable to resist the assaults of the Portuguese who were in possession of heavy artillery. On seizing Asilah they began working, on the one hand, on reducing the surface area of the town in order to have better control over it, and on the other, on reinforcing the walls with bastions, circular in shape, which were armed with loopholes and machicolations.  
Hence one can view most of the actual enclosure walls, as well as the majority of the bastions, as having been built by the Portuguese, except perhaps those which are situated on the seafront and are rectangular in shape.

es.name: Muralla y torres
description: El primer recinto fortificado construido en Asilah data de la época almohade. Fue restaurado por los meriníes y reforzado por los wattasíes, pero esta primera muralla no pudo resistir el asalto de los portugueses, que poseían artillería pesada. Después de tomar Asilah los portugueses se dedicaron, por una parte, a reducir la superficie de la ciudad para estar en condiciones de dominar su espacio; y, por otra, a reforzar la muralla con torres que respondieran mejor a los embates de la artillería pesada; es decir, de forma circular y provistos de troneras y matacanes. Por ello se deduce que la mayor parte de la muralla del actual recinto es de construcción portuguesa, igual que las torres, salvo las que se encuentran de cara al mar, que son rectangulares.

fr.name: Muraille et bastions
description:
La première enceinte construite à Asilah date de l’époque almohade. Elle aurait été restaurée à l’époque mérinide et renforcée par les Wattassides. Mais cette première enceinte n’a pu résister aux assauts des Portugais qui étaient en possession d’artillerie lourde.Aussi, dès leur prise d’Asilah, ils s’attelèrent, d’une part, à réduire la superficie de la ville pour être en mesure de dominer l’espace, d’autre part, à renforcer la muraille de bastions qui répondaient mieux aux tirs de l’artillerie lourde, comme les bastions de forme circulaire munis de meurtrières et de machicoulis.  
C’est pourquoi on peut considérer que la plupart des murs de l’enceinte actuelle sont de construction portugaise ainsi que la majorité des bastions, sauf peut-être ceux qui se trouvent sur le front de mer et qui sont de forme rectangulaire.

en.name: Maqam of Rabi‘a al-‘Adawiyya
description:
Architectural examinations and excavations carried out in 1995 reveal that the *maqam* is a composite of different periods. The earliest finds date back to the Byzantine period, as the disovery of some ceramic fragments testify. On the west wall, there is a Greek inscription. It reads: “*Courage Dometilla. None is immortal*”. Even though some believe the site was built to honour Saint Pilagia, it was probably used as a burial place. A *kufic* inscription has also been found dating to the early Islamic period; although it has never been deciphered it may have religious significance since many stories have circulated since the 6th/12th century that refer to Rabi‘a al-‘Adawiyya’s place of burial. Furthermore, the ceramic material that has been uncovered here dates to both the Ayyubid and Mamluk periods, not to mention a wall that dates back to the 7th/13th – 8th/14th centuries.  
The site is named today after Rabi‘a al-‘Adawiyya. The Islamic historical sources refer to more than one person with the same name. The most famous was Um al-Khayr Rabi‘a al-‘Adawiyya al-Basriyya, the famous *sufi*, who died in 185/801 in Basra, Iraq. Another is the wife of Rabi‘a, Ahmad Ibn Abu al-Hawari, who is probably buried at this site. ‘Abd Allah al-Mukhlis commented on this in the 1930s, saying: *“It might well be that the Rabi‘a buried here on the Mount of Olives and below the Zawiya al-As‘adiyya is neither al-‘Adawiyya nor Ahmad Ibn Abu al-Hawari’s wife but another Rabi‘a whose history time has erased but whose name it has kept”*.  
The Shrine has a simple rectangular entrance. On top of it is a stone lintel, and above it a window. The entrance was originally an arch that was blocked up at a later stage. Its interior consists of two parts one of which, to the west, is a square room covered by a barrel vault. On its southern wall is a *mihrab*, which indicates that the area was used for prayer. Stairs, approximately 5 m. in length, separate the western from the eastern part. The floor of the eastern section drops below the level of the western part, which has a cement floor, an indication that it was built in modern times. This room is rectangular (5.6 × 3.4 m.) and is also covered by a barrel-vault. A cenotaph lies in the centre of the room.

es.name: Maqam Rabi‘a al-‘Adawiyya
description:
Los estudios arquitectónicos y las excavaciones arqueológicas efectuadas en 1995 indican que se trata de un edificio de estilo compuesto, cuya construcción se realizó a lo largo de distintas épocas. Los hallazgos más antiguos se remontan a los bizantinos, como indican algunos fragmentos de cerámica. En el muro oeste hay una inscripción en griego que dice: “Ánimo Domitila, nadie es inmortal”. Es probable que este lugar fuese empleado como tumba, aunque algunos autores piensan que fue dedicado a Santa Pelagia. En el edificio ha aparecido también una inscripción de estilo *cúfico* que podría corresponder a principios de la época islámica; aunque todavía no ha sido estudiada, podría tener un significado religioso, sobre todo porque nos han llegado muchos relatos desde el siglo VI/XII que indican la existencia de una tumba de Rabi‘a al-‘Adawiyya. Además, las vasijas descubiertas en el lugar se remontan tanto a la época ayyubí como a la mameluca, sin olvidar un muro fechado en los siglos VII/XIII-VIII/XIV, lo que indica que el lugar fue utilizado en sucesivas épocas.  
El *maqam* se atribuye hoy en día a Rabi‘a al-‘Adawiyya, aunque lo cierto es que las fuentes históricas musulmanas mencionan a más de una persona con ese nombre. La más famosa fue Umm al-Jayr Rabi‘a al-‘Adawiyya al-Basriyya, una famosa sufí, que falleció en 185/801 en Basora, Iraq. La segunda sería la esposa de Ahmad Ibn Abu al-Hawari, que probablemente sea la persona enterrada en este *maqam*. ‘Abd Allah al-Mujlis se refirió a este asunto en los años 1830: “Pudiera ser que la Rabi‘a enterrada aquí en el monte de los Olivos, y debajo de la *zawiya* al-As‘adiyya, no fuera ni la esposa de al-‘Adawiyya ni la de Ahmad Ibn Abu al-Hawari. Probablemente sea otra persona del mismo nombre cuya historia ha sido borrada por el tiempo, aunque se conserve su nombre”. El *maqam* tiene una sencilla entrada rectangular, coronada por un dintel de piedra sobre el que se superpone una ventana. Originariamente, esta entrada estaba formada por un arco que luego fue cegado. El interior tiene dos partes. La sala oeste, cuadrada, está cubierta por una bóveda de cañón. La presencia de un *mihrab* en el muro sur atestigua el uso del lugar para el rezo. Una escalera de unos 5 m de largo separa este espacio de la parte este, cuyo suelo está por debajo del nivel de la zona oeste, de época moderna, como su suelo de cemento indica. La estancia este rectangular (5,6 × 3,4 m) también está cubierta por una bóveda de cañón. En el centro de la habitación hay un cenotafio.

fr.name: Maqam Rabi‘a al-‘Adawiyya
description:
L’étude architecturale du site ainsi que les fouilles entreprises en 1995 montrent que l’édifice est d’un style composite et que sa construction s’est déroulée sur différentes périodes. Les trouvailles les plus anciennes remontent aux Byzantins, comme l’attestent certains tessons de céramique. Sur le mur occidental, une inscription en grec proclame: “Courage, Domitilla, nul n’est immortel.” Même si certains pensent qu’il était dédié à sainte Pélagie, le site fut probablement utilisé comme sépulture. Une inscription coufique a également été mise au jour, qui daterait de la première époque islamique; bien qu’elle n’ait pas encore été déchiffrée, elle pourrait avoir une signification religieuse, étant donné que, depuis le VIe/XIIe siècle, plusieurs récits évoquent l’existence d’une sépulture de Rabi’a al-‘Adawiyya. De plus, les poteries qui ont été découvertes sur place datent aussi bien de l’époque ayyoubide que de l’époque mamelouke, sans oublier un mur datant du VIIe/XIIIe-VIIIe/XIVe siècle. Il est donc clairement établi que le site a bien servi pendant de longues périodes successives.  
Aujourd’hui, le *maqam* porte le nom de Rabi‘a al-‘Adawiyya. Cependant, dans les sources historiques musulmanes, ce même nom désigne plusieurs personnes différentes. La plus connue est Oum al-Khayr Rabi‘a al-‘Adawiyya al-Basriyya, la célèbre soufie décédée en 185/801 à Bassora en Irak. La deuxième est Rabi‘a, l’épouse de Ahmad Ibn Abou al-Hawari, qui pourrait être enterrée sur le site. ‘Abd Allah al-Mukhlis en a parlé dans les années 1830 : “Il se pourrait bien que la Rabi‘a enterrée ici sur le mont des Oliviers et sous la *zawiya* al-As‘adiyya ne soit ni l’épouse de al-‘Adawiyya, ni celle de Ahmad Ibn Abou al-Hawari, mais une autre Rabi‘a dont le temps a effacé l’histoire, mais conservé le nom.”  
Le *maqam* s’ouvre sur une simple entrée rectangulaire surmontée d’un linteau en pierre puis d’une fenêtre. À l’origine, l’entrée était formée par un arc, qui a été comblé ultérieurement. L’intérieur est composé de deux parties. La salle occidentale carrée est couverte d’une voûte en berceau. La présence d’un *mihrab* dans le mur sud prouve que l’endroit était utilisé pour la prière. Un escalier de 5 m de longueur environ sépare cette pièce de la partie orientale, dont le sol est plus bas que celui de la pièce occidentale, d’époque moderne, comme l’indique le sol cimenté. Cette pièce orientale rectangulaire (5,6 x 3,4 m) est également couverte par une voûte en berceau. Un cénotaphe se trouve au centre de la pièce.

en.name: Pottery jar
description: Although blue and white porcelains were described as vulgar by Chao Zaho (Chao Mingzhong) in his 1388 book about art and antiquities (the first book for connoisseurs) entitled *Gego yaolun* (The Essential Criteria of Antiques), these porcelains became more beloved and fashionable from their earliest appearance in Chinese and European markets. The first use of these two colours: blue (evoking the infinity of sea and sky) and white can be traced back to the Near and Middle East. They had a large impact on Chinese ceramics. Blue is also said to be effective against bad intentions. The pigments used for underglaze blue in Persia were lapis lazuli (*lajavard*) and cobalt, which was cheaper. The inside of the bowl is decorated with dynamic, loose floral motifs applied with sparse brushstrokes under the greyish-white glaze of the bowl on a small base. The rim is lined with blue.

en.name: Solomon's Pool
description:
The three pools lie amidst captivating pinewoods within a beautiful landscape, just at the outset of Wadi Artas, which is covered by vegetation and fruit trees. It is not known when the pools were first constructed, but both the middle and upper pools existed during Herod’s time (37–4 BC). The third, lower pool was built during the reign of the Mamluk Sultan Khushqadam (865/1460–872/1467), who also ordered the renovation of the whole water system. Nevertheless, the most important rebuilding work on the pools was carried out in 943/1536–1537, during the Ottoman Sultan Sulayman the Magnificent’s time; hence these pools still bear his name. He completed the water system and linked it to Jerusalem, adding a series of fountains that can still be seen today in the Old City of Jerusalem.  
The pools served as reservoirs that collected rain and water from nearby springs, while the aqueducts carried the water over on bridges and through tunnels inside the hills and along their slopes to Jerusalem, right up until 1922 by means of pumping engines. Some of the water was collected from areas 15 km. away. The longest aqueduct at 68 km. had to follow a natural zigzag course along hillsides using gravity, with a straight of only 21 km. Today the visitor can enjoy the full view of the pools, the remains of the aqueducts and the surrounding tunnels.  
The first pool is 116 m. long, 70–72 m. wide and 6–12 m. in depth, in volume it is 85,000 m3. The middle pool is 129 m. long, 70–76 m. wide and 12 m. in depth, in volume it is 90,000 m3. The lower Mamluk pool is the largest at 177 m. long, 86–95 m. wide and 15 m. in depth, in volume it is 113,000 m³.

es.name: Albercas de Salomón
description:
Estas tres albercas se encuentran en un hermoso entorno situado entre cautivadores bosques de pinos, al principio del verde valle de Artas, fértil en árboles frutales.  
No se sabe cuándo se excavó la primera alberca, pero la superior y la central ya existían en tiempos de Herodes Antipas (4 a. C.-39). La tercera alberca, situada en la parte inferior, fue construida por el sultán mameluco Juchqadam (865/1460-872/1467), quien también renovó totalmente el sistema hidráulico. Sin embargo, la obra más importante realizada en estas albercas la llevó a cabo el sultán otomano Sulayman al-Qanuni en 943/1536, quien completó el sistema de canalizaciones y lo prolongó hasta Jerusalén, donde añadió una serie de fuentes que todavía se pueden ver en la ciudad antigua.  
Estas albercas se utilizaron para recoger el agua de lluvia y de los manantiales naturales dispersos por la región, para, posteriormente, canalizarla hasta Jerusalén, a través de una red de acueductos y de conductos subterráneos que atravesaban las colinas. A veces el agua se recogía a más de 15 km. Para aprovechar la pendiente natural de las colinas, el acueducto más largo debía seguir un trazado de 68 km, aunque la distancia en línea recta es solo de 21 km. Este sistema funcionó hasta 1922, fecha de la instalación de las primeras bombas eléctricas. En la actualidad, el visitante puede disfrutar de una vista general sobre las albercas y ver los vestigios de los acueductos y las conducciones subterráneas que las rodean.  
La primera alberca tiene una longitud de 116 m, una anchura de 70-72 m, una profundidad de 6-12 m y una capacidad de 85.000 m³. La central mide 129 m de largo, 70-76 m de ancho, 12 m de profundidad y tiene una capacidad de 90.000 m³. La alberca inferior, construida en la época mameluca, es la de mayor tamaño y capacidad, con una longitud de 177 m, una anchura de 86-95 m, una profundidad de 15 m y una capacidad de 113.000 m³.

fr.name: Piscines de Salomon
description:
Dans un paysage admirable, les trois bassins se découvrent au coeur d’une splendide pinède, à l’extrémité de la verdoyante vallée d’Artas, fertile en arbres fruitiers. On ne sait pas à quel moment fut creusé le premier bassin, mais le bassin supérieur et celui du milieu existaient déjà sous Hérode Antipas (4 av. J.-C.-39 apr. J.-C.). Le troisième bassin, celui du bas, fut construit par le sultan mamelouk Khuchqadam (865/ 1460-872/1467), qui fit aussi entièrement rénover le système hydraulique. Mais l’intervention la plus importante concernant les trois piscines date de 943/1536- 1537, sous le règne de Soliman le Magnifique, qui compléta le système des canalisations et le prolongea jusqu’à Jérusalem, où il ajouta une série de fontaines toujours visibles dans la vieille ville.  
Les bassins servaient à collecter l’eau de pluie et celle des sources environnantes, avant qu’elles ne soient acheminées jusqu’à Jérusalem par tout un réseau d’aqueducs empruntant des ponts et des canalisations souterraines pour franchir les collines. L’eau était parfois recueillie à plus de 15 km. Pour respecter la pente naturelle des collines, l’aqueduc le plus long devait suivre un tracé de 68 km en zigzags, alors que, à vol d’oiseau, la distance n’est que de 21 km. Ce dispositif fonctionna jusqu’en 1922, date à laquelle les premières pompes électriques furent mises en place.Aujourd’hui, le visiteur peut jouir d’une vue intégrale sur les piscines, les vestiges des aqueducs et des canalisations alentour.  
Le premier bassin est long de 116 m, large de 70 à 72 m et profond de 6 à 12 m ; son volume est de 85 000 m3. Le bassin central est long de 129 m, sa largeur varie de 70 à 76 m, sa profondeur est de 12 m et sa capacité de 90 000 m3. Le bassin inférieur (d’époque mamelouke) est le plus grand avec une longueur de 177 m, une largeur de 86 à 95 m, une profondeur de 15 m et une capacité de 113 000 m3.

en.name: "The Concourse of the Birds"
names: Folio 11r from a Mantiq al-Tayr (Language of the Birds)
description: The illustration on this folio depicts a scene from a mystical poem, Mantiq al-tair (Language of the Birds), written by a twelfth-century Iranian, Farid al-Din 'Attar. The birds, which symbolize individual souls in search of the simurgh (a mystical bird representing ultimate spiritual unity), are assembled in an idyllic landscape to begin their pilgrimage under the leadership of a hoopoe (perched on a rock at center right). The careful, harmonious composition is consistent with that of the late fifteenth-century Timurid miniatures also in the manuscript, but three factors indicate that this image is later: the presence of the hunter, who has no place in the narrative; his firearm, a weapon that gained currency in Iran after the mid-sixteenth century; and the signature of the late sixteenth- to early seventeenth-century artist Habiballah.
materials: Ink, opaque watercolour, gold, and silver on paper

description: The basin is made of brass, with a wide, shallow rim and a concave body with a flat base. The bowl-shaped opening supports a soap holder, which sits as a plate and, after a slight neck, has straight sides folded upwards. The soap holder features a star at its centre and curved, three-pointed openwork perforations on the edges and underside. en.name: Villa Crespi
short_description: An astonishing three-storey villa in Moorish style, near Lake d’Orta in Piedmont, Northern Italy. It features a 48-meter high minaret and has richly decorated interiors made with lavish marbles imported from several countries. Construction lasted 12 years. The estate includes a greenhouse, a wet dock, stables, a big fountain, an annex, and is surrounded by walls with valuable wrought iron gates.
holder: Since the 1980s, Villa Crespi has been transformed in a 4-star hotel owned by the 'Villa Crespi-Ca.pri srl'
history:
Cristoforo Benigno Crespi was a successful businessman active in the cotton industry. In 1879, he bought an estate near Lake d’Orta (Piedmont, Northern Italy), to build a vacation house in honour of his wife, Pia Travelli.  
Crespi had fallen in love with the architecture of Baghdad, where he went to buy cotton, and asked architect Angelo Colla to build for him a villa in Moorish style. Architect Enrico Combi designed the magnificent park.  
After it was inaugurated, the villa became a centre of high-society life: it hosted members of the Italian royal family and even the King of Spain. The Crespi organised theatre performances in the park and invited nobles, industrialists and bankers. At the end of the 1980s, Villa Crespi was transformed into a four-star hotel.

en.name: \[The clown\] *"Chocolat" entertaining children at the hospital*
short_description: Rafael Padilla (1868–1917) was born to an African family and sent to Cuba as a slave, where he was bought by a farmer from Bilbao. Once in Paris, he performed as a duo with Footit for twenty years. They drew their success from the contrast between the bad-tempered white clown and his punch-bag in the form of a black clown named "Chocolat", which left parisians, still unaccustomed to difference, in hysterics.

ar.name: لوحة تذكارية.
description:
قام السلطان المملوكي الظاهر بيبرس بصد الهجوم المغولي على حدود مصر. في عام 664 / 1265، فتح مدينة سيليسيا (أو سيس) في بلاد الأرمن بعد أن أضر أهلها بمصالح المسلمين وتعاونوا مع المغول في حربهم على الدول الإسلامية.  
  
توقف الظاهر بيبرس أثناء عودته إلى مصر في مدينة حمص، ودخل جامع الصحابي (صاحب رسول الله محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم) خالد بن الوليد (توفي عام 21 / 642)، المحارب العربي الذي قاد المسلمين ضد القوات البيزنطية في عهد الرسول، والذي كان يلقب بسيف الله. أمر بيبرس بإقامة ضريح فوق قبره مع وضع نصوص تذكارية تخلد انتصاره في معركة سيس. هذه اللوحة هي إحدى اللوحات التي وضعت في الجامع. اللوحة ذات شكل مستطيل، وضلعها العلوي على شكل قوس. نُقش على هذه اللوحة نص من خمسة أسطر بخط الثلث، وزيِّن النص بأشكال نباتية لطيفة. ويلاحظ آثار الألوان الأخضر والأسود على هذه اللوحة.  
  
ويمكن قراءة نص النقش على النحو التالي:  
"بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم أمر بإنشائه على حرم سيف الله وصاحب رسول الله خالد بن الوليد رضي الله  
عنه مولانا السلطان الملك الظاهر ركن الدنيا والدين وسلطان الإسلام والمسلمين قاتل الكفرة والمشركين قاهر الخوارج  
والمتمردين \[ محـ\] يي العدل في العالمين ملك البحرين صاحب القبلتين خادم الحرمين الشريفين ، وأزين الملك سلطان العرب والعجم والترك  
اسكندر الزمان وصاحب القرآن بيبرس الصالحي قسيم أمير المؤمنين أعز الله سلطانه عند عوده على  
\[حمص \] للغزاة ببلاد سيس وذلك في شهر ذي الحجة سنة أربعين وستين وستماية."  
ملاحظـة: الكلمة "أربعين" التي وردت في السطر الخامس من النص يجب أن تكون "أربع".
لوح من خشب الصندل، عليه نقش تذكاري يؤرِّخ نصر القائد المملوكي السلطان الظاهر بيبرس على المغول في صقلية بالإضافة إلى تذكارات للعديد من القادة المسلمين.
keywords: بلاد الأرمن؛ جامع؛ حمص؛ خالد بن الوليد؛ خشب صندل؛ خشب محفور؛ خشب ملوّن؛ ؛ سيس؛ سيليسيا؛ صندل هندي؛ مغول.

en.name: Memorial Panel.
description:
The Mamluk Sultan al-Zahir Baybars undertook the task of repelling the Mongols in the AH mid-7th / AD mid-13th century as they advanced towards Egypt. In AH 664 / AD 1265, he occupied the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia, including the city of Sis (Kozan), since its rulers had allied themselves with the Mongols in their war against the Muslims. On his way back to Egypt after the campaign, he stopped in the city of Homs and visited the Mosque of the Companion (of the Prophet Muhammad) Khalid bin al-Walid (d. AH 21/ AD 642), the Arab commander who led the Muslims against Byzantine forces during the time of the Prophet, and who was known as the "Sword of God". Baybars ordered the completion of a panel above the tomb of Khalid that commemorated his victory in Cilicia.  
This panel is one of a series that were placed in the mosque. Its overall form is rectangular, but its upper side is in the shape of an arc. There are five lines in Arabic *thuluth* script carved on the panel. The text translates as follows:  
(1) In the name of God, the Merciful and Compassionate, this construction in the sanctuary of the Sword of God and the Companion of the Prophet of God, Khalid bin al-Walid, may God be pleased with him, was ordered  
(2) by the Lord Sultan al-Malik al-Zahir, the pillar of religion, the ruler of Islam and Muslims, the killer of unbelievers and polytheists, the killer of rebels  
(3) and insurgents, the one who revives justice in the two worlds, king of the two seas, ruler of the two *qiblas*, servant of the two holy sanctuaries, the grace of sovereignty, the sultan of Arabs, Persians, and Turks,  
(4) ruler of time and companion of the Qur'an, Baybars al-Salihi, partner of the Commander of the Faithful, may God support his rule against his enemies, in  
(5) \[Homs\], for the victory is in the year six hundred sixty-forty after the *hegira*  
*Note: The word "forty" in line five should be "four."*  
This text is decorated with finely executed vegetal motifs, and has traces of green and black on it.

The text carved on this sandalwood panel commemorates the victory of the Mamluk Sultan al-Zahir Baybars against the allies of the Mongols in Cilicia and serves to associate the Mamluk ruler with the memory of other great Muslim warriors.
place: Mosque of Khalid bin al-Walid, Homs, Syria.
keywords: Indian sandalwood; carved wood; painted wood; Hims (Homs); Mosque; Khalid bin al-Walid; Sultan al-Zahir Baybars; Mongols; Cilicia; Armenian Kingdom

es.name: Panel conmemorativo.
description:
A mediados del siglo VII / XIII, el sultán mameluco al-Zahir Baybars combatió a los mongoles que avanzaban hacia Egipto. En 664 / 1265 ocupó el reino armenio de Cilicia, incluida la ciudad de Sis (Kozan), porque sus gobernantes se habían aliado con los mongoles en la guerra contra los musulmanes. De regreso a Egipto tras esta campaña, se detuvo en la ciudad de Homs y visitó la mezquita del Compañero (del profeta Muhammad) Jalid ibn al-Walid (m. 21 / 642), el comandante árabe conocido como “la espada de Dios” que encabezó a los musulmanes contra las fuerzas bizantinas en tiempos del Profeta. Baybars ordenó que se hiciera un panel conmemorativo de su victoria en Cilicia para ponerlo sobre la tumba de Jalid.  
Este panel forma parte de una serie que se encontraba en la mezquita. Es rectangular, pero el borde superior lo tiene en forma de arco. Consta de una inscripción de cinco renglones tallados en letra *zuluz* que dicen lo siguiente:  
(1) En el nombre de Dios, el Misericordioso y Compasivo, esta construcción en el santuario de la Espada de Dios y Compañero del Profeta, Jalid ibn al-Walid, que a Dios complazca, fue encargado  
(2) por el señor el sultán al-Malik al-Zahir, pilar de la religión, soberano del islam y los musulmanes, asesino de los infieles y politeístas, asesino de los rebeldes  
(3) y los insurgentes, aquel que restablece la justicia en los dos mundos, rey de los dos mares, soberano de las dos *qibla*, sirviente de los dos santuarios sagrados, gracia de la soberanía, sultán de árabes, persas y turcos,  
(4) soberano del tiempo y compañero del Corán, Baybars al-Salihi, compañero del Comandante de los Fieles, que Dios sostenga su gobierno contra sus enemigos, en  
(5) \[Homs\], por la victoria en el año seiscientos sesenta y cuarenta \[sic, debería decir “cuatro”\] después de la Hégira.  
El texto está decorado con motivos vegetales exquisitamente elaborados y presenta restos verdes y blancos.

Este documento histórico data de 664 / 1265 y está tallado en un panel de madera. Conmemora la victoria del sultán mameluco al-Zahir Baybars contra los aliados de los mongoles en Cilicia y vincula al soberano mameluco con la memoria de otros grandes guerreros musulmanes.

materials: Madera de sándalo de la India tallada.

fr.name: Panneau commémoratif.
description:
Au milieu du VIIe siècle H (XIIIe siècle J.-C.), le sultan al-Dahir Baybars entreprit de repousser les Mongols qui avançaient vers l'égypte. En 664 H / 1265 J.-C., il occupa le royaume arménien de Cilicie et la ville de Sis (Kozan), alliée aux Mongols dans leur guerre contre les musulmans. De retour en égypte à l'issue de cette campagne, il s'arrêta dans la ville de Homs et visita la mosquée du Compagnon (du prophète Muhammad) Khalid bin al-Walid (m. 21 H / 642 J.-C.), surnommé l’épée de Dieu, qui avait commandé les troupes musulmanes contre les forces byzantines au temps du Prophète. Baybars ordonna d'achever un panneau qui se trouvait au-dessus de la tombe de Khalid pour commémorer sa victoire en Cilicie.  
Ce panneau fait partie d'une série qui décorait la mosquée. Sa forme générale est rectangulaire, mais sa partie supérieure est incurvée. Cinq lignes de texte en écriture *thoulouth* sont sculptées dans le bois :  
(1) Au nom de Dieu, de Clémence et de Miséricorde, cette construction dans le sanctuaire de l'épée de Dieu et Compagnon du Prophète de Dieu, Khalid bin al-Walid, que Dieu soit satisfait de lui, a été commandée  
(2) par le Seigneur Sultan al-Malik al-Dahir, pilier de la religion, souverain de l'Islam et des Musulmans, tueur des incroyants et des polythéistes, tueur des rebelles  
(3) et des insurgés, celui qui restaure la justice dans les deux mondes, roi des deux mers, souverain des deux *qibla*, serviteur des deux saints sanctuaires, grâce de la souveraineté, sultan des Arabes, des Perses et des Turcs,  
(4) souverain du temps et compagnon du Coran, Baybars al-Salihi, associé au Commandeur des Fidèles, que Dieu soutienne son règne contre ses ennemis, à  
(5) \[Homs\] pour la victoire en l'an six cent soixante-quarante \[*sic*, lire quatre\] après l'Hégire.  
Le texte est décoré de motifs végétaux de fine exécution et conserve des traces de couleur verte et noire.

Le texte sculpté sur ce panneau en bois de santal commémore la victoire du sultan mamelouk al-Dahir Baybars sur les alliés des Mongols en Cilicie et associe la mémoire de ce grand souverain à celle d'autres grands guerriers musulmans.
place: Mosquée de Khalid bin al-Walid, Homs, Syrie.
keywords: Bois de santal indien ; bois sculpté ; bois peint ; Hims (Homs) ; mosquée de Khalid bin al-Walid ; sultan al-Dahir Baybars ; Mongols ; Cilicie ; royaume d'Arménie

de.name: Mariae Himmelfahrt
description: Das Altarblatt des einst frühbarocken Hochaltars verbildlicht auf kurfürstlichen Wunsch hin dem Patrozinium gemäß die Himmelfahrt Mariens. Der Münchner Maler portraitierte sich selbst aus dem Bild blickend als Apostel Johannes. Die Komposition folgt einem Kupferstich nach dem themengleichen Hochaltarblatt des Pieter Paul Rubens in der Kathedrale zu Antwerpen.

en.name: Assumption of Mary
description: Upon electoral request, the altarpiece of the once Early Baroque high altar depicts the Assumption of Mary according to the saint’s patronage of the church. The Munich painter portrayed himself as the apostle Johannes looking out of the painting. Theme and composition follow a copperplate depiction of the high altarpiece of Peter Paul Rubens in the Cathedral of Antwerp.
